jobs.title: Fertilizer Procurement Strategy Associate
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Professional & Technical Competencies:

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Italian Teacher
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

In response to the increased refugee arrivals into Europe, the IRC established the program initially in Greece, which was expanded with programs in Serbia and wider Balkans and with programs in Germany. Following a first assessment conducted in January 2017 in Italy and another one in July 2017, several critical protection gaps were identified within assistance provided to refugees and migrants in Italy: mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), assistance to unaccompanied children, information provision and legal support. To respond to the identified gaps IRC established a small presence in Italy. The IRC in Italy provides essential safety, empowerment, education, livelihood and health services to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. Our programs operate across the country, including in Trieste, Milan, Rome, Turin and various locations in Sicily and Calabria, with a strong focus on supporting the most vulnerable populations, such as women and children.

**Context of the Assignment**

IRC, in partnership with Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Piemonte, Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Friuli Venezia Giulia, Powercoders, Progetto Tenda, is implementing the **Digital Horizons projec**t in Turin and Trieste, since February 2025.
Digital Horizons helps young refugees and migrants in Italy accessing sustainable employment through free software development training, job support, individual guidance and social support. The project focuses on youth aged 16–25, arrived in Italy in recent years, who are seeking to break down integration barriers, improve mental health and build pathways to long-term work opportunities.

By working with public job centers (PES), vocational training providers (VET), IT companies and employers, the project prepares participants for high-demand digital careers and supports them with mental health services, individual job counselling and psychosocial support, job placement, a safe and quiet space to study, access to social services, language training, and childcare.

Simultaneously, it also builds the capacity of institutions and employers to create more inclusive opportunities for the target population.

The Digital Horizons intensive (5hs day, monday-friday) training in software development has been delivered in Trieste since mid October 2025, by IRC partner ENAIP FVG. To support the group of participants with heterogeneous knowledge of Italian language, IRC is seeking a teacher for **italian classes (A2-B1-B2),** includingspecific IT **vocational language,** to support students learning outcomes, before the start of the IT training.

**Purpose of the Assignment**

**Job Overview**

The Digital Horizons Italian Teacher will be based in Trieste and will design and deliver middle advanced (A2-B1-B2 as needed) Italian language classes and IT vocational language, to a group of Digital Horizons students, in person. Under the Economic Wellbeing Manager’s supervision and in collaboration with the IRC Italy Integration Counselor and ENAIP FVG staff, the Italian teacher will conduct classroom teaching activities in Trieste, ensuring no student is left behind.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

**Specific Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Plan, design, and deliver lessons** in Italian at A2-B1–B2 level, integrating IT-related terminology and vocational language relevant to software development.
- **Develop tailored teaching materials** that combine general Italian language learning with specialized IT vocabulary and contexts.
- **Address student questions** and provide clarification on both general and IT-specific language content.
- **Help develop students’ confidence and learning skills**, encouraging students to use Italian effectively in technical and professional settings.
- **Identify learning gaps** and adapt teaching strategies to meet diverse linguistic needs within the group.
- **Promote intercultural communication** by clarifying information and bridging cultural differences that may affect learning.
- **Manage classroom dynamics** and handle any critical issues that arise during sessions, ensuring a supportive learning environment.
- **Encourage collaborative learning** through peer-to-peer support and group exercises for language practice with IT-related content.
- **Maintain accurate records** of attendance, progress, and outcomes to support monitoring and reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the IT trainer, other ENAIP vocational training staff and IRC Integration Counselor to achieve the course objectives.

The **Digital Horizons Italian teacher** will deliver updates to IRC Staff, on the classroom learning process and possible challenges identified.

**Deliverables**

- Italian classes sessions conducted (40 hs)
- Attendance Sheets signed

**Timeframe**
The assignment will end upon completion of above-listed deliverables and in any case no later than on 16th November 2026. Classes schedule will be decided in agreement with IRC and ENAIP staff and will be held in the morning (Monday to Friday, between 9.00 and 13.00 am)

**Competencies and skills**

- Proven experience developing learning content and delivering Italian language group teaching activities
- Experience working with migrant population and/or youth is highly desirable.
- Experience or knowledge of IT Sector is an asset
- Bachelor's degree in language or social sciences
- Proven experience in multicultural work or educational environments
- Knowledge of strength-based education and participatory learning
- Understanding of fundamental educational and psychological principles related to learning and communication
- Strong organizational and planning skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Problem-solving abilities
- Personal qualities: empathy and patience, works well in and promotes teamwork, comfortable in a multi-cultural environment, flexible, communicates clearly.
- Additional knowledge of English, Arabic, Spanish, French, Ukrainian, Urdu, Pashtu, Farsi are an asset

**Application Process and Requirements:**

**Application Documentation:**

CV in English OR Italian

**Agreement and payment terms**

The specific details of the agreement, including the scope of work, timelines, deliverables, intellectual property rights, and any other pertinent provisions, will be negotiated and outlined in the contractual agreement to ensure clarity, transparency, and mutual understanding between IRC and the consultant/group of consultants.

**Compensation:** (Total of 1200 EUR). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Country Director
jobs.description:
**The Organisation**

Plan International is a rights-based development and humanitarian organisation working for better lives for all children. We are independent of government and have no political or religious affiliation.

Our purpose is to strive for a just world that advances children’s rights and equality for girls.

We have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years, and are now active in more than 70 countries.

Our global strategy has a specific focus on girls, as they are often the most marginalised and most often left behind. We have committed ourselves to the ambitious target of reaching 100 million girls over 5 years, to ensure they can learn, lead, decide and thrive. This is our contribution to reaching the sustainable development goals, and in particular the goals on gender equality.

Our organisation is transforming itself to meet this enormous challenge everywhere we work.

We need bold, forward-thinking and innovative individuals to lead our country operations, driving change and delivering results that will allow us to reach our target of 100 million girls.

**The Opportunity**

Plan International is seeking an experienced, values-driven and strategic leader to serve as Country Director for Cambodia. This is a pivotal leadership role, responsible for setting the overall direction of Plan International’s work in Cambodia and ensuring strong programme delivery, influencing impact and sustainable organisational performance.

As Country Director, you will lead a team of about 80 staff and oversee a country programme with an annual budget of approximately USD 8 million. You will represent Plan International at senior levels with government, donors, civil society, media and partners, while ensuring the organisation delivers relevant, gender-transformative impact for the most vulnerable children, particularly girls.

This role requires a leader who is comfortable driving transformative change, strengthening organisational culture and accountability, and ensuring that Plan International Cambodia remains a credible, influential and effective development and humanitarian actor.

**In this pivotal role, you will:**

- Provide strategic and operational leadership for Plan International’s development, humanitarian and influencing work in Cambodia, aligned with the global strategy and the organisation’s commitment to gender equality and girls’ rights.
- Lead the development and implementation of an ambitious Country Strategy grounded in gender transformation, child rights and participation.
- Ensure programme and influencing work achieves impact at scale by linking grassroots action with national-level influencing and advocacy.
- Drive effective emergency preparedness, risk reduction and resilience building, and ensure readiness to respond to both predictable and sudden-onset emergencies.
- Strengthen resource mobilisation across institutional, multilateral, corporate and National Office funding sources, ensuring long-term sustainability.
- Lead and develop a high-performing, inclusive and values-driven team, embedding Plan International’s standards on safeguarding, gender equality, accountability and ethical practice.
- Ensure strong financial stewardship, legal and donor compliance, and effective planning, budgeting, reporting and performance management systems.
- Act as Plan International’s senior in-country representative, building trusted relationships with government, donors, media, INGOs, national NGOs, communities and other stakeholders.
- Contribute as an active member of the Regional Leadership Team, supporting regional collaboration, organisational learning and shared services.

**Do you have what it takes?**

*To excel in this role, you will need among other things:*

- Proven senior leadership experience with increasing responsibility in an international development environment.
- A strong understanding of child rights, gender in development and girls’ rights, and the ability to translate these commitments into impactful programmes and influencing strategies.
- Experience in sustainable community development and participatory approaches in development interventions.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements and sound financial management.
- Experience of programming in challenging environments, with a strong understanding of the political, social, economic, humanitarian and security context in Cambodia or a comparable environment.
- Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate diverse teams, manage organisational change, and build an efficient and motivated workforce.
- Strong political acumen, networking and negotiation skills, with experience engaging governmental and non-governmental actors.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Khmer, with strong diplomatic and media-facing communication skills.
- A relevant university degree in development, social science, business administration or a related field.

*For a detailed job description which includes the full list of accountabilities and requirements,* [*please go to this link*](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/lk4xz4pp1lld9eelcm2zm/Cambodia-CD-JD-March-2026-final.pdf?rlkey=ap8qwup484gvhvn7h05y4d5nz&st=xfavun0d&dl=0)

jobs.title: Director of Pacific Programmes, Pacific Region
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Director of Pacific Programmes

**Location:** Melbourne or Port Moresby, with frequent travel

**Contract:** Permanent

**Reporting to:** South East Asia and the Pacific Department Director

**Responsible for:** Directing Conciliation Resources’ programmes in the Republic of Fiji, the Solomons Islands and Papua New Guinea

**Salary:** $127,488 AUD (Exclusive of Superannuation)

**Deadline:** 17:00 Friday, 6th Nov 2026.

## Conciliation Resources

Conciliation Resources is an independent international organisation working with people in conflict to prevent violence, resolve conflicts and promote peaceful societies. We believe that building sustainable peace takes time. We provide practical support to help people affected by violent conflict achieve lasting peace. We draw on our shared experiences to improve peacebuilding policies and practice worldwide. We have worked in the South East Asia and the Pacific (SEAP) regions since 1994 and currently work in: the Republic of Fiji, the Solomon Islands, Papua New Guinea and the Philippines.

Our work seeks to contribute to building more peaceful societies through enhanced analysis and comparative knowledge and through supporting and implementing targeted and adaptive peacebuilding and mediation support programmes. We seek to contribute to change through long-term partnerships; and enhance context-specific peacebuilding and mediation practice through comparative learning.

Within the Pacific region Conciliation Resources supports community led peacebuilding initiatives, working with numerous civil society partners, including in Fiji, Solomon Islands and PNG Highlands and Bougainville, PNG. The programme also supports processes of political dialogue and mediation. Conflict challenges the programme is currently working on include: dealing with past legacies of conflict; the intersection between governance and peace; masculinity, youth and violence; and climate change and conflict.

## Job Purpose

The Director of Pacific Programmes leads Conciliation Resources’ peacebuilding and mediation support work in the Pacific region. They are responsible for developing and managing multiple peacebuilding and mediation support teams - the PNG team, with programmes in Bougainville and the PNG Highlands; The Fiji and Solomon Islands team, including developing programmes related to climate change and conflict. This position will provide strategic leadership and operational management to the whole Pacific team, with direct line management of Project Managers.

The postholder is responsible for setting and overseeing programme budgets, and for ensuring the integrity and credibility of Conciliation Resources’ reputation in the Pacific region. They lead the team’s efforts in developing new programmes, and working to secure new funding for our work. The Director of Pacific Programmes is also a member of Conciliation Resources’ Senior Leadership Team, working with Conciliation Resources’ senior leaders around the world.

## Person specification

### Essential knowledge, skills and experience

● Significant (min 6-8 years) project management experience, designing and implementing conflict resolution and peacebuilding interventions, including programme design, budget development, programme implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

● Practical and conceptual knowledge of peacebuilding and conflict transformation processes, of processes of social and political change and of supporting the development of local capacities for peacebuilding.

● Significant (min 4 years) senior team management experience, including line managing project / programme managers and their teams, and overseeing team performance management and professional development.

● Experience of working with local and national partners in an accompaniment role, including capacity enhancement and due diligence.

● Significant financial management, including experience preparing and managing annual budgets of at least AUD1.5mil, monitoring and forecasting spend, and overseeing internal and external financial reporting.

● Experience of managing research projects.

● Experience of leading government or other donor-funded programmes, including donor relationship management, programme development and reporting.

● Significant experience of securing funding for new work, including concept development, building donor relationships and writing proposals and budgets.

● Understanding of anti-racist and decolonisation approaches to peacebuilding practice, team management and programme management.

● Excellent communication skills, to communicate complex issues effectively and adjust communication style to varying circumstances, including ability to listen actively to people from varying backgrounds and with a range of political, cultural, gender and sexual identities and value orientations, combined with an ability to engage with them clearly and sensitively.

● Excellent written and spoken English.

● Experience implementing projects in difficult social and political situations or conflict contexts, and experience of hostile environment training or willingness to undertake hostile environment training.

● Graduate-level study or equivalent by experience in conflict resolution, international relations, development studies, international humanitarian law, gender, peace and security or other related fields.

● Excellent organisational and coordination skills, including the ability to think and plan strategically while also retaining close attention to detail, to manage and prioritise a diverse and demanding workload, to convene and run efficient meetings and meet deadlines.

● Ability to navigate political sensitivities and awareness of the complexity of working in conflict-affected situations, including appreciation of confidentiality and handling sensitive information with due care.

● Willingness and ability to work irregular hours on occasions and to undertake frequent international travel in sometimes uncomfortable or insecure conditions.

● Excellent word processing, spreadsheet, database and email software skills.

### Desirable knowledge, skills and experience

● Experience facilitating workshops and dialogue processes.

● Experience developing and managing advocacy strategies and engagement with policymakers.

● Experience of and managing advocacy projects.

● Experience of producing high-quality written work.

● Experience of designing, organising and managing research and advocacy events.

● Extensive knowledge of the social and political landscape in the Pacific and wider region, and its conflicts.

● Experience living and working in the Pacific region.

jobs.description:
**About ACTED**

“ We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

- Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.
- Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles
- Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy:**
The MEAL Assistant has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). And has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. The MEAL Assistant carries out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.
**Location:** **Damascus & Rural Damascus – Syria**
**Start Date:** **ASAP**

**Duration of the Contract: 6 Months.**

**Job Purpose**

The MEAL Assistant is responsible for assisting the MEAL Officers to implement all MEAL field activities and tasks including assessments, beneficiary verification, data entry, reporting, collection of and ensuring adherence to lessons learned and best practices, and any other tasks as required. He/she will be responsible for supporting the team of MEAL enumerators in the field.
**Objectives**

1. Implement MEAL assessments in the field in a reliable, accurate and transparent manner, including collecting primary and secondary data, reporting on findings, and supporting the development of tools and methodologies.
2. Support organizational learning by ensuring adherence to MEAL technical guidelines, lessons learned, and best practices.
3. Ensure lessons learnt and best practices are discoursed and documented by reporting them in a timely manner.
4. Contribute to the effective functioning of beneficiary complaints and response mechanism and enhance the trust and confidence of beneficiaries, identify areas of our work which need to be improved and ensure that Acted learns from the feedback provided through this process.

## **Duties and Responsibilities:**

1. **Appraisals, Monitoring Missions, and Evaluations**

***1.1 Field Data Collection***

- Supervise and support MEAL enumerators team during data collection in the field;
- Coordinate with the Area MEAL Officer to carry out the assessments (including, but not limited to: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) surveys, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, baseline and endline surveys, as well as other types of assessments and data collection that is required);
- Check that material necessary to carry out the assessment is sufficient and appropriate;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately;
- Record and forward all complaints and suggestions received while in the field to the appropriate Accountability Officer/Accountability assistant.
- Collect evidence where applicable
- Probe to clarify unclear answers;
- Write down the observations and answers in an ordinate and clear way, recording responses accurately;

1. ***2 Reporting***

- Report monitoring findings and any other findings and observation emerged during data collection activities frequently to the MEAL Officers so to communicate the progress of assessment activities;
- Recognize and give account of problems in obtaining data and provide useful feedback from field research activities;
- In the absence of a dedicated Data Entry Officer, enter all field data into appropriate databases on an accurate and timely basis;
- Cross-check the accuracy of data entry;
- Support the maintenance of an efficient and accurate filing system for all electronic and hard copy documents;
- Report monitoring findings at Daily/Weekly Area Meetings, as required by MEAL Officer;
- Collect high-resolution and good quality photos of Acted project activities in the field, featuring donor, partner and Acted logos, and delivery photos to the AME Officer (in line with Acted Child Protection Policy and Photo Guidelines).

1. ***3 Support the Development of MEAL Tools and Methodologies***

- Support the MEAL Officer in designing appropriate information collection tools and methodologies, including assessment Terms of Reference, and questionnaires;
- Support the translation of tools and methodologies into local language(s) as required.

1. **Support to Organizational Learning**

***2.1 Collection of Lessons Learned and Best Practices***

- Collect lessons learned and best practices from beneficiaries, community leaders, partners, and other stakeholders during assessment/monitoring missions;

***2.1 Monitoring Adherence to Program Strategies and Guidelines***

- Cross-check that project implementation adheres to the technical guidelines for the program, as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Monitor the implementation of lessons learned and best practices;
- Cross-check the accuracy and relevance of beneficiary selection according to contractual criteria.

**Other**
- Participate in any meetings or conferences as required by the MEAL Officer;
- Perform any other related activities as assigned by immediate supervisor.

**Key Performance Indicators**

- Mechanism in place and functional to provide data on project indicators in a timely manner
- Mechanism in place and functional that allows at least the reporting on Acted 16 global standard indicators
- Lessons learnt and best practices recorded in the Area Lessons Learnt and Best Practices document according to Acted standard learning procedures and updated in regular and timely manner.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

- At least one year experience with NGOs and/or International Institutions in Monitoring and Evaluation
- University Degree /institute.
- Number of years of relevant experience in monitoring & Evaluation.
- Basic English skills is an asset
- Resident in Damascus/Rural Damascus governorate
- Ability to travel locally
- Good command of using KOBO application via smartphones.
- Good command of using MS Excel and MS Word
- Good command of using GPS devices/programs for data collection
- Ability to build and sustain relationship with team members and interviewees in the field as well as the local authorities i.e., camp managers…. etc.
- Flexibility and adaptability are essential, as well as the ability to plan, take initiative and work under minimal supervision.
- Capability to work under pressure and travel to the targeted areas within Acted projects

jobs.title: Lead, Client Impact, BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)
jobs.description:
**BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Lead, Client Impact, BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)**

**Job Location: Nairobi, Kenya | Open to Kenyan and international candidates.**

**Application deadline: 23 October 2026**

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF) oversees its microfinance subsidiaries outside Bangladesh, which are wholly or majority owned by the legal entity BRAC International Holdings B.V. (BIHBV), operating across eight countries in Africa and Asia. Within this mandate, BI MF expands financial inclusion by responsibly delivering financial services to people at the bottom of the pyramid, particularly women living in poverty in rural and hard-to-reach areas, to create self-employment opportunities, build financial resilience, and harness their entrepreneurial spirit by empowering them economically. The achievement of both ‘Impact and Scale’ are critically important, ensuring that each subsidiary has systems in place to realise both components of the mission.

BI MF provides strategic direction, governance oversight, and institutional strengthening across the portfolio. Today, its operations serve clients (97% women) across the eight operating countries, managing a loan portfolio of approximately USD 277 million, and employing over 7,000 staff, of whom 87% are women.

**About the Role:**

This is an opportunity to shape how one of the world’s leading INGO measures, manages and improves its impact across a multi-country microfinance portfolio.

The **Lead, Client Impact** is responsible for providing overall leadership on Impact Measurement & Management (IMM) and Social Performance Management (SPM) within BI MF and ensuring appropriate technical support required to all BI MF entities in these areas. The role gathers insights and works with operations teams to ensure we achieve our impact objectives. The role will leverage BRAC’s established impact measurement capabilities, research, client insights and multi-country microfinance experience to ensure BI MF focuses on the right outcomes and the right processes to drive impact as the bottom line. This role will assist BI MF entity teams to measure performance against metrics in key social impact categories: client access, social outcomes, financial resilience, client agency, client protection, and client experience and satisfaction, among others. It will strengthen how BI MF measures, manages and improves impact at scale, ensuring our services remain inclusive, scalable and client-centric, particularly for women, youth and people living in poverty.

The position will report to the Associate Director, Strategy and will work across the BI MF team and closely with the leadership of each entity. They will also work closely with the BRAC International Learning & Effectiveness team to deliver on our promise as a learning organization, continuously examining and changing practices based on data and reflections from the field. They will also collaborate with BRAC’s social development programmes and various affiliates for overall achievement of BRAC’s goals and mission.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**A. Impact Measurement & Management (IMM):**

- Lead and support the BI MF Client Impact team to ensure quality implementation of our flagship annual IMM activities across BI MF country entities:
- **60 Decibels Lean Data Report** to provide standardized and actionable client insights pertaining to poverty outreach, household wellbeing, quality of life, and challenges faced by BI MF clients.
- **Internal Dropout Surveys** to better understand drivers of client retention and address issues that cause attrition at the BI MF entity level.
- Maintain and institutionalize a detailed **customer journey map** framework to help BI MF entities enhance and promote a positive client experience as well as address key pain points.
- Strengthen **poverty outreach measurement** and cross-country learning through review, integration, and documentation of effective poverty tracking mechanisms; ensure that our BI MF entities have in place an innovative approach to poverty outreach and tracking.
- Continuously improve the **complaint handling framework** to strengthen client protection pathways and provide clients with means to resolve issues safely and efficiently.
- **Ensure knowledge transfer and capacity building for BI MF entity teams strengthening their capability to implement the client impact agenda consistently and effectively across BI MF entities.**
- Work closely with the Technology team to ensure that client impact related data is captured, stored and available to country leadership and frontline staff.

**B. Social Performance Management (SPM):**

- Oversee the Social Performance Management function to ensure quality reporting and dissemination on client impact data for both internal and external stakeholders.
- Oversee the Social Performance Management team to guide BI MF entities through the quarterly SPI5 Audit process to assess BI MF entities against the Universal Standards of Social Performance Management (USSPM) and Client Protection Principles (CPPs).
- Ensure timely updates to the BI MF leadership team, including on client impact metrics related to poverty outreach and key social outcome indicators.
- Serve as the focal point for client impact reporting needs to Boards (both BIHBV and BI MF entities), investors, and donors.
- Lead client impact reporting integration across BI MF (aligning with global frameworks as applicable).
- Collaborate with BI MF Finance and Technical teams to lead design standardized templates for client impact data collection and narrative reporting.
- Oversee quality assurance of client impact data from BI MF country entities and support them in meeting applicable compliance standards.
- Identify client impact reporting requirements and gaps; develop action plans for compliance and implementation.

**C. Operationalisation of the BI MF Strategy:**

- Operationalise and support the BI MF strategy and direction as it relates to Impact Management & Measurement (IMM) and Social Performance Management (SPM) in consultation with BI MF senior management, technical teams, and BI MF entity leadership teams to strengthen impact research, client outcomes, Lean Data, dropout/retention insights and impact dashboards, and embed evidence into business decisions.
- Develop and implement strategies that will maximize the synergies between microfinance and other programmes and ensure quality implementation for achievement of BRAC’s overall holistic goals.
- Lead or oversee research design and project management on IMM activities.

**D. Team Leadership:**

- Responsible for building a high performing, motivated team by capitalizing on each team members' individual strengths, skill sets, experience and ambitions.
- Ensure clear roles and responsibilities and fluid collaboration within and between departments and teams for timely and high level output.
- Coach and develop team members to translate IMM and SPM expertise into actionable business insights, stronger client outcomes and portfolio-level impact.
- Provide individual mentorship to each team member to continuously develop leadership skills and ensure succession planning, with a focus on creating women leadership.

**E. Safeguarding:**

- Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation. Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
- Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
- Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place and encourage others to do so.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's Degree in Concentration / Major in Economics, Development Studies, Business, Finance, or related fields
- Master’s degree (or higher) in Economics, Development Studies, Business, Finance, or related fields (preferred)

**Experience:**

- 8-12 years’ experience, including 5 years plus working in the financial inclusion space.
- Previous management roles in financial Inclusion for women, program design and project management, strategy development and implementation, impact measurement and management.
- Deep understanding of challenges and issues in financial inclusion for women, youth, and people at the bottom of the pyramid.

**Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of impact frameworks with demonstrated ability to turn impact data into management decisions
- Highly motivated with a strong interest and experience in development and social issues
- Experience of bringing structure to ambiguous problems and driving solutions at scale.
- Ability and willingness to train and mentor people and experience working with a diverse, global team.
- Strong communication and presentation skills. Fluency in English required (spoken, reading and written)
- Strong data analysis skills and attention to detail
- Ability and willingness to work in a challenging environment with poor infrastructure and human capacities and difficult security conditions

Core Competencies:

- Collaboration, Innovation, Accountability, Trust, Strategic Alignment

Leadership Competencies:

- Develops Talent, Drives Purpose, Mission Focus, Communication, Adaptability, Results-Oriented

**Employment type:** Contractual

**Salary:** Negotiable

jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

## **About the Role**

To drive seamless data flow between the Back Office Portal and SAP B1 and to optimize workflows to ensure 100% data delivery to MCF within 45 days. Key role in process improvement.

## **Responsibilities**

Accounting Systems & Systems Integration

- Drive data flow management and system integration between the Back Office Portal and SAP Business One (SAP B1), troubleshooting integration errors and optimizing system workflows.

Master Data Management & Process Improvement

- Manage and update vendor master records to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and compliance with company policies and donors’ audit-required standards.

Cross-Functional Communication & Technical Translation

- Serve as the technical bridge between Tech, FRC, and FAS teams by translating complex data insights and system requirements into actionable process improvements.

Collaborative Quality Assurance

- Partner across departments to make sure that processes are fully documented, maintain spreadsheet audit standards, streamline reporting workflows, and establish organization-wide data management best practices.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Finance, Business Information Systems, or a related field.
- At least 2 to 5 years of experience in data integration, master data management, or systems analysis.
- Demonstrated proficiency with ERP systems, specifically SAP Business One (SAP B1).
- Advanced Excel skills (PivotTables, XLOOKUP, logical formulas) for data manipulation and auditing.
- Proven track record in process optimization, root-cause analysis, and data error troubleshooting.
- Strong cross-functional communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical data issues into actionable solutions for non-technical stakeholders.
- Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda is required.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kigali, Rwanda

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

2 years

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

## **Application Deadline**

03 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Consultant - Financial Systems Review, Benchmarking, and Alignment under One Program Approach (OPA) with Localization Focus
jobs.company: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
jobs.description:
## **Organizational Context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian organization, with a network of 191-member National Societies (NSs). The overall aim of IFRC is “to inspire, encourage, facilitate, and promote at all times all forms of humanitarian activities by NSs with a view to preventing and alleviating human suffering and thereby contributing to the maintenance and promotion of human dignity and peace in the world.” IFRC works to meet the needs and improve the lives of vulnerable people before, during and after disasters, health emergencies and other crises.

IFRC is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement (Movement), together with its member National Societies and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The work of IFRC is guided by the following fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General, and has its Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. The Headquarters are organized into three main Divisions: (i) National Society Development and Operations Coordination; (ii) Global Relations, Humanitarian Diplomacy and Digitalization; and (iii) Management Policy, Strategy and Corporate Services.

IFRC has five regional offices in Africa, Asia Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and the Americas. IFRC also has country cluster delegations and country delegations throughout the world. Together, the Geneva Headquarters and the field structure (regional, cluster and country) comprise the IFRC Secretariat.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

## **Consultancy Purpose**

The Lebanese Red Cross (LRC), as the host National Society, leads humanitarian action in Lebanon. Multiple Partner National Societies (PNSs) operate using varied financial and operational systems.
LRC has already initiated a mapping of partner systems and internal processes. However, in light of evolving international financial standards, compliance requirements, and localization priorities, there is a need to:

- Update and validate the existing mapping.
- Benchmark LRC financial systems against current best practices and Movement
standards.
- Identify gaps in alignment between LRC and partners.
- Analyze discrepancies across partners (e.g., why some partners meet standards while
others do not).

This assignment will support strengthening financial governance, accountability, and host National Society leadership under the One Program Approach (OPA).

##
**Objectives**

The consultant will:

1. Conduct a comprehensive financial review of LRC systems (Finance & Accounting as a
priority, with linkages to HR, Logistics, and Procurement where relevant).
2. Update and validate the existing mapping of Partner National Societies’ systems against LRC frameworks.
3. Benchmark LRC financial systems against best international standards, ensuring
relevance to today’s operational and compliance environment.
4. Analyze gaps and discrepancies, including:
- Why LRC may not fully meet certain standards (if applicable).
- Factors influencing varying levels of alignment with the benchmarking framework, including donor requirements, headquarters policies, operational modalities, system configurations, and internal governance arrangements.
5. Provide actionable recommendations to strengthen alignment, improve financial systems, and ensure partners adopt best processes.

## **Consultancy Duties and Responsibilities**

- **Finance & Accounting**
Review LRC financial policies, procedures, and systems.
- Assess alignment with best international standards (audit, compliance, donor
requirements).
- Evaluate:
- Budget consolidation under OPA.
- Financial tracking systems and tools.
- Reporting cycles and compliance.
- Documentation and audit trails.
- Identify gaps in practice versus standards and propose practical improvements.

**Comparative Partner Analysis**

- Update existing mapping of PNS financial systems.
- Categorize partners based on level of alignment (high, medium, low).
- Conduct comparative analysis, including:
- Partners that meet standards vs. those that do not.
- Practices that enable compliance (good practices).
- Constraints preventing alignment.

**Cross-Functional Linkages**

Where relevant, assess how financial processes interact with:

- Procurement (compliance, documentation, supplier payments)
- Logistics (inventory valuation, tracking)
- HR (payroll, staff cost allocation)

**Scope of Work**

**Financial Systems Review (LRC)**

- Review existing financial frameworks, SOPs, and tools.
- Benchmark against up-to-date international
- Identify strengths, gaps, and risks.

**Mapping Update and Validation**

- Review previously conducted mapping exercises.
- Validate accuracy with current practices.
- Update alignment scoring based on latest data.

**Comparative Analysis**

- Conduct a structured comparison between:
- LRC vs. international standards.
- Partner vs. LRC systems.
- Partner vs. partner practices.
- Highlight reasons for misalignment and enabling factors for compliance.

**Recommendations**

- Provide:
- Practical recommendations for LRC system strengthening.
- Partner-specific alignment actions.
- Priority actions based on risk and impact.
- Ensure recommendations are feasible, localized, and reinforce LRC leadership.

**Deliverables**

1. Financial Systems Assessment Report (LRC): Benchmarking against current international and Movement standards.
2. Updated Mapping Report: Validated and revised mapping of partner financial systems.
3. Comparative Analysis Report:
- LRC vs. standards
- Partner vs. LRC
- Partner vs. partner
4. Including gap analysis and root causes.
5. Recommendations Matrix: Clear, prioritized actions for LRC and partners.

**About the role**

**Consultant to Facilitate Digital Advocacy and Strategic Communications Training for Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) in Zimbabwe**

The Realisation of the African Disability Protocol (RAD-P) Project seeks to promote the rights, inclusion and meaningful participation of persons with disabilities in Zimbabwe through advocacy, policy engagement, awareness raising and institutional strengthening of Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs). The project supports OPDs to advocate for the implementation of disability-inclusive laws, policies and programmes, including the Constitution of Zimbabwe, the National Disability Policy, the Disability Act and the African Disability Protocol.

The RAD-P Project will convene a four-day Digital Advocacy and Strategic Communications Training targeting partner OPDs. The training seeks to equip participants with practical knowledge and skills to strengthen organisational visibility, policy influence and stakeholder engagement through strategic use of digital communication tools and platforms.

Sightsavers are therefore seeking to engage a qualified consultant to design, facilitate and document the training workshop.

**Purpose of the Consultancy**

The consultant will design and deliver a practical and participatory training programme that strengthens the capacity of OPDs to utilise strategic communications, digital advocacy, accessible communication approaches, website management, media engagement and ethical AI tools to advance disability rights advocacy and organisational visibility.

**Objective of the consultancy**

The consultant will support the RAD-P to strengthen the capacity of participating OPDs to effectively utilise strategic communications, websites, social media platforms and media engagement approaches. They will equip participants with practical skills in website development and management, content creation, digital storytelling and ethical use of AI tools, and enhance their understanding of accessibility standards, digital governance, media regulations and data protection requirements.

The consultant will be responsible for:

- Reviewing the concept note and other relevant project documents.
- Developing an inception report outlining the understanding of the assignment, methodology, workplan and approach.
- Developing training materials, presentations, handouts, practical exercises and case studies.
- Developing pre- and post-training assessment tools.
- Ensure all training materials are accessible to persons with different disabilities.

Facilitate a four-day training programme covering;

- Strategic communications for disability rights advocacy.
- Website development, management and administration.
- Affordable digital tools and AI for advocacy.
- Legal, policy and ethical frameworks governing digital advocacy.
- Social media management and digital advocacy.
- Advocacy content creation and digital storytelling.
- Media engagement and public relations.
- Accessible communication and inclusive digital content.

Post-Training Phase

- Analyse participant evaluation results and learning assessments.
- Prepare a comprehensive training report.

The full objective, scope of work, and deliverables can be found within the [ToR](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQAWJx6xg3TbQKbfZoWiSFE6AaKP984YuFXVCdlEo_UHbck?e=CxbQhq)

**Skills and Experience**

As the successful consultant you will possess relevant experience or a Master’s degree or higher in Communications, Journalism, Media Studies, Public Relations, Development Studies, Information Technology, Disability Studies or a related field. You will hold extensive experience in strategic communications, digital advocacy, media engagement, website development or related fields, and a background in facilitating capacity-building workshops for civil society organisations, NGOs or OPDs.

Further requirements include:

- Strong knowledge of disability inclusion and accessible communication practices.
- Practical experience in website development platforms such as WordPress, Google Sites and Wix.
- Demonstrated knowledge of social media management, digital campaigns and content creation.
- Familiarity with Zimbabwe's digital governance, media and data protection frameworks.
- Experience in the ethical application of AI tools for communication and advocacy purposes.

This is a highly varied and involved consultancy position, and the above is not an exhaustive list of deliverables or required professional skills. jobs.description:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: 01/11/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**
**Location: West and Central Darfur**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was one of the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.
In February 2024, SI opened a base in North Darfur to provide emergency assistance to populations, as very few humanitarian organizations were operational in the state. Similarly, SI opened an office in Zalingei, Central Darfur in November 2024 and East Darfur and West Kordofan in early 2026. In addition an office in Khartoum was maintained and in 2025 operations were opened in Jazeera state. Today, thanks to the support of SHF, CDCS, SDC, GFFO, SIDA, ECHO and BHA, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Jazeera and Khartoum States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors.
Across the Darfurs, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc. In the East the focus is on rehabilitation and recovery of water systems as well as emergency WASH interventions for health crises. Besides, SI implements food assistance mostly through cash and voucher modalities. West and North Darfur team also implements agricultural support activities (seeds distribution, provision of tools, training) as well as market strengthening support.
SI also has an Emergency Response Team based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA) as well as in North Darfur.
In North Darfur, SI was one first to intervene and are presently a leader in WASH response. The FSL work has brought in some great result in North Darfur.
Recently, we opened our new base in Al Dein in East Darfur and West Kordofan. The teams are already working on strong WASH response along with some critical Cash response. The team is currently assessing and opening new areas in Kordofans.
In the Eastern part of the country, SI is present with Wash and FSL activities in Khartoum and Jazeera, under ECHO, CDCS, and SHF.
Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The WASH PM will be in charge of launching and implementing SI's WASH activities in West and Central Darfur states.
S/he will be in charge of ensuring projects are delivered in a timely manner according to WASH quality standard and in accordance with context specifications and communities preferrences.
S/he will be in charge of coordinating and providing support to two technical teams accross West and Central Darfur states, providing adequate support and capacity-building when needed and working in a remote managemet set up.
S/he will be in responsible to lead needs assessments in different areas of West and Central Darfur and consequently developing the SI response plan, including with local partners.

**The main challenges:**

- Important workload with a wide range of WASH activities in different geographical areas
- Remote management context as 2 WASH teams in 2 different states
- Access & security challenges

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Launch newly starting projects and update workplan according to priorities
- Supervision of technical works including new borehole drilling and water points solarization
- Coordinate WASH response with SI stakeholders, mainly WASH actors, authorities and line ministries

**Security constraints:**

Level 4: High risk environment, threats less predictable and requiring strict protocols, Curfews in place (often 6pm–8pm), Walking strictly limited to approved times, locations,

### YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

A Bachelor or Master's degree in Water Resource Management, Engineer, Project management

Experience in the humanitarian sector: 3 Years

Experience on a similar position : 3 Years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Proven experience in WASH emergency/ealry recovery programming and WASH in institutions
2. Strong experience in water points solarization, solid waste management
3. Proven experience in partnership - preferable with local organizations
4. Experience in cholera prepardness or response
5. Strong experience in management
6. Good analytical skills and proactive, solution-oriented approach to work.
7. Experience in protracted crisis context (being able to switch between short/medium/long-term solutions).

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong organizational skill
2. Interpersonal and communication skills
3. Ability to work under pressure
4. Ability to adapt to different implementation contexts including remote supervision
5. Experience working with SI and prior experience working in Sudan is an assest

**LANGUAGES**

- English Mandatory
- Arabic would be an advantage

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2310 gross per month (2100 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Guest house is of good standard, with good internet connexion, solar panels and running water. Social life is limited to contact with other NGO staff

**Background/IRC Summary:**

The Syria crisis is often described as the worst humanitarian catastrophe since the end of the Cold War. Today, 13.4 million people in Syria - more than half of the country's population - are in need of humanitarian assistance with needs increasingly being exacerbated by economic decline. Of these, 6.8 million are refugees and asylum-seekers who have fled the country. This is no short-term humanitarian episode. The devastating human consequences to huge numbers of people will endure for decades. The destruction of relationships, communities, livelihoods, homes and infrastructure will take years to repair.

IRC is offering a robust humanitarian response to the Syria crisis a rapidly expanding portfolio, supported by more than 1000+ staff in Syria Country Program. IRC is undertaking programs in Syria and the neighboring countries of Turkey, Iraq, Lebanon and Jordan in the fields of health, child protection, early childhood development, education, women’s protection and empowerment, non-food items and food distribution, cash assistance, water and sanitation, protection and rule of law, and livelihood programming. Our work in these challenging settings gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, security, funding and coordination.

ACT Alliance is the world's largest coalition of Protestant and Orthodox churches, and church-related organisations engaged in humanitarian, development, and advocacy work. It consists of 164 members working together in over 125 countries, with headquarters in 73 countries, whose aim is to create positive and sustainable change in the lives of poor and marginalised people regardless of their religion, politics, gender, sexual orientation, race, or nationality, in keeping with the highest international codes and standards. For more details, visit [www.actalliance.org](http://www.actalliance.org/).

The Communication Officer is responsible for developing and implementing communication and visibility activities for ACT Appeals and the Rapid Response Fund, with the objective of:

- increasing the visibility and understanding of ACT Alliance's humanitarian response;
- communicating the impact and added value of ACT members' and forums’ work;
- supporting fundraising and donor engagement;
- strengthening the visibility of local and national ACT members;
- producing high-quality, timely and compelling digital content;
- ensuring accountability through transparent communication about humanitarian funding and results; and

The Officer will work closely with the HOHA and RRF Managers, head of communications, humanitarian colleagues, ACT members, communications colleagues and fundraising/donor engagement functions.

## Key responsibilities

**A. Communication Strategy and Planning**

- Develop and implement communication plans for the RRF and ACT Appeals in coordination with ACT Alliance Communication team.
- Ensure communication activities are aligned with ACT Alliance's broader communications and fundraising strategies.
- Identify communication opportunities throughout the humanitarian funding cycle, from crisis alert and funding mobilisation through implementation, results and close-out.
- Develop clear communication objectives, target audiences, key messages and content plans for each funding mechanism.
- Ensure that communication is timely and appropriate to the humanitarian context and does not compromise the safety, dignity or privacy of affected people and partners.

**B. RRF Communication and Visibility – 50%**

- Lead day-to-day communication activities related to the Rapid Response Fund.
- Develop communication packages around RRF-funded responses, including:
- human-interest stories;
- impact stories;
- case studies;
- photos and visual content;
- short videos and reels;
- social media content;
- web stories;
- donor-facing updates;
- infographics and other digital materials.
- Proactively identify RRF-funded responses with strong communication and fundraising potential.
- Work directly with ACT members, forums and Regional Representatives to gather high-quality information, stories, photographs, quotes and other content.
- Develop clear procedures and tools to facilitate systematic collection of communication materials from RRF-funded members.
- Ensure that RRF results and impact are regularly documented and communicated.
- Develop an annual RRF communication and visibility calendar.
- Support communication around RRF milestones, including funding decisions, portfolio achievements, learning, localisation and innovation.
- Highlight the added value of the RRF as a rapid, flexible and locally led humanitarian financing mechanism.
- Communicate the role of the RRF within ACT Alliance's wider humanitarian architecture.
- Develop content that demonstrates how RRF funding translates into concrete results for crisis-affected communities

**ACT Appeals Communication – 50%**

- Support communication and visibility for ACT Alliance humanitarian Appeals.
- Develop and coordinate communication materials throughout the Appeal cycle.
- Support the production of:
- Appeal launches;
- situation updates;
- human-interest stories;
- impact stories;
- donor updates;
- social media campaigns;
- website content;
- newsletters;
- videos and multimedia products.
- Coordinate with ACT members to collect timely information, photographs, testimonies and programme results and avoid duplication of efforts, particularly in major responses
- Lead the humanitarian communications group and coordinate calls as appropriate
- Translate technical humanitarian information into accessible and compelling communication products.
- Support fundraising campaigns linked to ACT Appeals.
- Ensure that Appeal communication demonstrates the collective added value of ACT Alliance members.
- Contribute to donor visibility and reporting requirements.
- Support communication around Appeal results, achievements, lessons learned and funding gaps.
- Identify stories and content that can help sustain donor engagement throughout the Appeal cycle.
- Support communication around the humanitarian system and mechanism as a whole.

**Fundraising and Donor Engagement**

A specific responsibility for both appeals and RRFs will be to ensure that communication contributes directly to **fundraising and resource mobilisation**.

- Develop compelling fundraising-oriented stories demonstrating the impact and added value of funding.
- Translate programme results into content suitable for donor engagement.
- Develop communication materials for prospective and existing donors.
- Support the preparation of donor presentations, fundraising campaigns, briefs and digital materials.
- Identify opportunities to use impact stories to demonstrate the value of investing in locally led humanitarian response.
- Work with colleagues to develop a pipeline of communication materials supporting future resource mobilisation.
- Support donor visibility requirements while ensuring that communication remains consistent with ACT Alliance policies, principles and partner ownership.
- Contribute communication inputs to donor proposals and fundraising materials where relevant.

**Digital Media and Content Production**

The position will have a strong focus on **digital communication and multimedia content**.

- Produce engaging content for ACT Alliance digital platforms.
- Develop social media content adapted to different platforms and audiences.
- Create short-form video content, including reels and other mobile-first formats.
- Develop simple visual assets, infographics and data-driven communication products.
- Support story, photography and video content collection from ACT members.
- Edit and package multimedia content for digital dissemination.
- Maintain content libraries in the ACT Mediabank and ensure appropriate informed consent, storage and accessibility of communication assets.
- Monitor digital engagement and use analytics to improve communication performance.
- Identify emerging digital communication trends and recommend approaches relevant to ACT Alliance humanitarian work.

**Storytelling and Content Development**

- Develop compelling stories that place affected people and local responders at the centre of humanitarian communication.
- Identify human-interest stories demonstrating the concrete impact of ACT funding.
- Ensure that stories are accurate, evidence-based and representative of programme results.
- Develop stories that demonstrate the contribution of local and national organisations and their leadership in humanitarian response.
- Ensure appropriate informed consent and compliance with safeguarding, data protection and ethical communication policies and requirements.
- Avoid communication approaches that portray affected people solely as victims or beneficiaries.
- Promote dignified, empowering and locally owned storytelling.

## Key working relationships

Head of Humanitarian Affairs; RRF Manager; Head of Communications; Secretariat communications team; humanitarian team; Regional Representatives; ACT members and forums; donor-reporting colleagues and communications focal-point network.

## Education, experience and skills

- University degree in communications, journalism, humanitarian affairs, international development, public relations or a related field.
- At least 5 years of relevant communications experience, preferably in humanitarian, NGO, faith-based or international network settings.
- Demonstrated experience developing and implementing communication strategies or campaigns.
- Strong experience in **digital communications and social media**.
- Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality written and visual content.
- Experience developing human-interest stories, case studies and impact stories.
- Experience working with photographs, video and short-form digital content.
- Demonstrated experience communicating complex information to different audiences.
- Experience of working with NGOs, humanitarian organisations, international organisations or similar institutions.
- Experience working with faith-based organisations is an asset.
- Strong understanding of ethical and responsible humanitarian communication.
- Demonstrated ability to work with multiple stakeholders and manage competing priorities.
- Excellent written and spoken English; additional languages relevant to ACT regions are an asset.

## General obligations

- Uphold and model ACT Alliance values, policies and ways of working, including safeguarding, PSEAH, accountability, inclusion, environmental responsibility and ethical conduct.
- Participate in ACT Secretariat planning, reporting, performance management and learning processes as required.
- Undertake other duties consistent with the purpose and level of the position, as reasonably assigned by the line managers.
- Undertake international travel as required in connection with the responsibilities and objectives of the position.
