jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Project Description**

I Have Rights provides legal information to asylum seekers on the island of Samos, prepares applicants for their asylum interviews, holds legal information workshops, appeals procedures for rejected applicants and accompanies applicants to interviews. As a political organisation, I Have Rights speaks out about the situation on Samos and in Greece and actively advocates for policy and practice reforms that are responsible for human rights violations in both Samos and Europe.

The organisation on Samos consists of a project coordinator, a Greek lawyer, a senior case worker, one to two volunteer case workers and one volunteer responsible for communications and advocacy.

The remote team consists of the fundraising and strategic litigation coordinator, the finance support, the board, interpreters and various volunteers involved in the Task Forces. The organisation aims towards flat hierarchies; the structures are evolving, and we would like to welcome you to play an active role in shaping the project.

I Have Rights is committed to safeguarding the well-being of everyone we work with. Team members are expected to uphold our policies, including our Code of Conduct, and adhere to the 'do no harm' principle in all their actions. You can find our policies [here](https://ihaverights.eu/about-us/#_vision-purpose-values).

Detailed information on the project can be found at: [www.ihaverights.eu](http://www.ihaverights.eu)

**Role & Responsibilities**

As Project Coordinator, you will play a central role in ensuring the continuity and cohesion of IHR’s work on Samos and in Greece in general. You will maintain a strategic overview of all ongoing activities, foster close collaboration between staff, volunteers, and partner organisations, and serve as one of the key contact points for Greek authorities. We are looking for someone who brings initiative, critical thinking, and a strong sense of responsibility—while embracing flat hierarchies, collective ownership, and a collaborative approach to decision-making grounded in shared values. You will help steer the project forward by connecting the dots across legal work, advocacy, and funding.

You will supervise a rotating team of one to three case workers on Samos (who typically stay for six months) as well as remote interpreters, working closely with the supervising Greek lawyer. In collaboration with other team members, you will take part in recruiting and assessing candidates to ensure a good team fit. In the area of advocacy, you will oversee the work of the communications and advocacy officer on Samos and coordinate advocacy activities.

You will also be supporting the organisation’s funding efforts.

**Your tasks will include:**

Team Coordination:

- Coordinating the work of in-person case workers and remote interpreters in close collaboration with the senior case worker and the supervising lawyer
- Participating in the recruitment and onboarding of new staff, volunteers, and interpreters
- Maintaining regular feedback structures with team members and clients
- Overseeing the day-to-day organisation of the office and volunteer accommodations
- Ensuring smooth coordination of case work and administrative tasks

Implementing safeguarding policies and responding appropriately to concerns

Advocacy Coordination:

- Connecting the legal work on Samos with the advocacy and strategic litigation task force
- Supporting the planning and delivery of advocacy projects and materials
- Acting as the focal point for the Border Violence Monitoring Network
- Representing IHR in relevant workshops, trainings, and conferences

Funding Support:

- Supporting funding efforts in collaboration with the Funding Task Force
- Drafting funding applications and project budgets
- Maintaining an overview of all funders, deadlines, and deliverables
- Ensuring timely and transparent reporting to funders
- Identifying and evaluating new funding opportunities

Overall Project Coordination:

- Maintaining a strategic overview of all ongoing activities and ensuring alignment with IHR’s mission and values
- Supporting the implementation of internal policies and safeguarding a collaborative, inclusive team culture
- Fostering strong relationships with partner NGOs and actors on Samos, Athens and beyond
- Carrying out administrative tasks such as preparing internal meetings, monitoring timelines, and renewing contracts

**Qualification & Education Requirements**

- Experience in grant writing, preferably within the Greek NGO sector
- Experience in team coordination or project management
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to keep an overview, coordinate workflows, and delegate tasks effectively
- Basic understanding of the asylum procedure and its legal and practical implications
- High proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- High resilience, adaptability, and ability to work in a dynamic environment
- Ability to work independently and take initiative within a collaborative team structure
- Proficiency in MS Office programs and Google Workspace
- Eligibility to reside and work in Greece, as the position is based on Samos

**Preferred Skills**

- Familiarity with the Greek non-profit or legal aid sector
- Experience in advocacy, campaigning, or public-facing communication
- Proficiency in Greek and/or German
- Experience with safeguarding frameworks
- Experience working in flat hierarchy structures

**Benefits**

- Work in a committed and international team at the intersection of legal aid, advocacy, and strategic litigation
- Contribute to an organisation shaping practice in an evolving field of European human rights law
- Opportunities for learning and exchange through collaborations with legal and advocacy networks across Europe
- We might ask you to travel to Berlin occasionally. Travel expenses and accommodation will be paid.

jobs.title: Country Representative - IGNITE (PERU)
jobs.description:
**SUMMARY**

IGNITE (Inclusive Growth and Networks for Investment, Trade and Economic Linkages) is a six-year (2026–2031) technical assistance program funded by Global Affairs Canada and implemented by Catalyste+. The program supports governments and key stakeholders across Latin America to strengthen institutional capacity, improve enabling conditions for inclusive and sustainable economic growth, and foster trade, investment, and economic partnerships.

Reporting to the Program Manager (PM) in Canada, the Country Representative (CR) for IGNITE will lead the implementation of the project strategy in country, aligned with program objectives, local priorities, and donor requirements. Depending on program needs and operational considerations, the CR may also provide support and coordination for a limited number of activities in the region, as part of the program portfolio.

The CR must reside in Peru.

The CR will serve as IGNITE's primary in-country representative and relationship focal point, and will support the identification and development of partnership opportunities, coordinate technical assistance assignments, and ensure effective delivery of program activities and results.

The CR will professionally steward the Catalyste+ brand and mission, maintain strong relationships with stakeholders throughout the partnership and assignment cycle, and contribute to the achievement of inclusive and sustainable economic development outcomes through institutional strengthening, capacity development, and knowledge transfer initiatives.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Program Management

- Lead in-country stakeholder consultations to support the identification of priorities, opportunities, and technical assistance needs in alignment with program objectives and donor priorities.
- Build and maintain productive working relationships with public institutions, regulatory bodies, private sector organizations, business associations, chambers of commerce, development partners, donors, Canadian missions, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Lead assignment design, as guided by the Program Manager and in line with program strategies, ensuring assignments respond to partner needs and contribute to program outcomes.
- Serve as the primary focal point for local partners throughout the assignment cycle, ensuring timely communication, coordination, problem resolution, and follow-up.
- Contribute to the recruitment and deployment of appropriately skilled Catalyste+ Advisors (CAs) and consultants by providing contextual information, logistical support, and stakeholder coordination.
- Support program implementation, stakeholder engagement, and coordination activities in designated secondary countries, as required.
- Provide guidance to Advisors and consultants in developing work plans and implementing assignments, ensuring alignment with program objectives, local context, and Catalyste+ policies and procedures.
- Oversee assignment logistics and provide support to Advisors during in-country assignments to ensure a productive and positive experience.
- Apply Results-Based Management (RBM) principles through constructive collaboration with partners, stakeholders, Advisors, consultants, and Catalyste+ departments.
- Ensure continuity and coherence across assignments by maintaining regular communication with partners, stakeholders, Advisors, consultants, and Catalyste+ staff.
- Monitor relevant economic, institutional, policy, and development trends and communicate developments, risks, and opportunities relevant to the program.
- Contribute to annual work plans, progress reports, donor reporting, and other program documentation as required.
- Respond to ad hoc requests from the PM, the Program Director (PD) and other Catalyste+ departments in a timely manner.

**Partnership Development and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Develop and maintain strong relationships with diverse partners and stakeholders, identifying opportunities for collaboration, institutional strengthening, technical assistance and future programming aligned with country priorities and program objectives.
- Support engagement with public sector institutions at national and sub-national levels, including ministries, regulatory agencies, local governments, and public service organizations.
- Maintain awareness of national development priorities, public sector reforms, economic trends, and sector-specific opportunities relevant to the program.
- Represent Catalyste+ at relevant meetings, conferences, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events.
- Support collaboration with Canadian missions and other Canadian stakeholders to identify areas of mutual interest and cooperation.
- Collaborate with the Sr. Director, International Services, and the PD, IGNITE, to identify and explore additional opportunities aligned with Catalyste+ priorities and interests, including opportunities that strengthen inclusive economic development, institutional effectiveness, sustainable trade, investment, and public-private collaboration.

**Operations Management**

- Collaborate across Catalyste+ departments to support delivery of program targets, assignments, and Advisor days.
- Administer assignments and program activities in accordance with Catalyste+ systems, policies, and procedures.
- Maintain accurate program records and ensure proper use of Catalyste+'s management information systems.
- Manage assigned budgets and ensure appropriate financial management, documentation, and reporting.
- Support local registration, compliance, and administrative requirements, as needed.
- Coordinate with other organizations and initiatives to identify synergies, avoid duplication, and maximize program impact.

**Leadership**

- Exemplify Catalyste+ values of transparency, integrity, accountability, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
- Foster collaborative and professional relationships with partners, Advisors, consultants, and Catalyste+ staff.
- Provide ongoing supervision, leadership, guidance, mentorship, and support to local staff, as applicable.
- Contribute to a positive, respectful, and inclusive working environment.
- Ensure compliance with Catalyste+ policies and procedures related to security, safeguarding, code of conduct, conflict of interest, harassment prevention, and other administrative requirements.
- Liaise with Canadian Embassies and local representatives of Canadian organizations regarding programming, security, and operational matters.

**Organizational Learning**

- Support implementation of Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) systems and processes.
- Ensure timely collection and submission of high-quality program data and supporting documentation.
- Contribute to organizational learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement efforts.
- Support preparation of donor reports and other reporting requirements.

**KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- University degree in International Development, Public Administration, Economics, Business Administration, Political Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

**Experience**

- Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience.
- Proven experience working with or engaging public sector institutions, including ministries, regulatory agencies, local governments, or other public entities.
- Experience in international development, economic development, governance, public administration, trade promotion, private sector development, or related fields.
- Experience working with donor-funded development programs.
- Experience managing stakeholder and partner relationships.
- Experience in project management and applying Results-Based Management principles.
- Sound knowledge of gender equality, women's economic empowerment, and the inclusion of vulnerable and underrepresented populations
- Experience working with Canadian-funded development programs is considered an asset.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, networking, and partnership development skills.
- Strong interpersonal, communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and exercise sound judgment.
- Strong organizational and coordination skills.
- Knowledge of the country's economic, institutional, and development context.
- Ability to engage effectively with stakeholders from both the public and private sectors.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
- Fluency in Spanish and professional working proficiency in English.

Contract type: Independent Contractor.

Salary: Negotiated based on candidate experience, qualification and country of residence.

jobs.title: Communications Adviser - Pacific Women Lead
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Human Rights and Social Development Division (HRSD)** has a vision for just, equitable and resilient Pacific societies and it aims to achieve this by advancing human rights, equality and social inclusion for all Pacific people, grounded in cultural values and principles. The work of this Division includes work previously undertaken by the Regional Rights Resource Team (RRRT) in the area of human rights and the Social Development Programme (SDP) in the areas of gender equality and social inclusion, culture and youth development.

In line with its vision, the work of the Division will encompass the following focal areas:

- **Objective 1:** Pacific institutions are strong, transparent, and responsive for upholding and promoting human rights and implementing inclusive, gender sensitive and culturally respectful development.
- **Objective 2**: Pacific Civil Society understand and can advocate for their rights and uphold cultural values.
- **Objective 3:** Pacific culture is protected, preserved, and promoted and culturally relevant and appropriate knowledge and systems are integrated across all work.
- **Objective 4:** All PSC programs and operations are grounded in people centered approaches and consider the rights and cultural values of diverse groups including women, children, youth and persons with disabilities.
- **Objective 5:** HRSD Division teams work collectively, coherently, and efficiently and to a high standard to achieve shared success for Pacific societies.

The role – **Communications Adviser – Pacific Women Lead**will oversee the coordination and implementation of strategic communications, engagement and outreach plans for the programme. This role also coordinates visibility communications through the development of high-quality, multi-media communication and media products for a wide range of stakeholders. As the role may require working across the objectives of other HRSD work programmes and broader SPC delivery, the role will have matrix reporting and working relationships with others in the Division.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Visibility communications and strategic communications**

- Develop and implement communication workplans and strategies including monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) for SPC’s gender equality flagship and outcome area, complementing DFAT’s gender equality Communications Strategy for SPC’s GE flagship.
- Manage and monitor the delivery of the workplans by leading the development of high quality, innovative and engaging programme communications and knowledge products to meet the needs of the PWL programme.
- Ensure appropriate visibility of the gender equality outcome area by working with partners and the media, and by producing quality media statements, stories, Op Eds, publications and other resources that are promoted publicly.
- Identify opportunities to engage and promote the gender equality outcome area for SPC HRSD and the GE flagship to existing and new audiences through different platforms and networks including senior level partners such as ministerial and diplomatic staff.

**Communications for development design, outreach and engagement and knowledge management**

- Develop targeted and well-planned engagement and outreach strategic approaches to engage key partners, SPC member countries’ government and NGO stakeholders, and grantees.
- Ensure SPC staff are able to effectively represent and relay the role SPC plays in the region, supporting key engagement and outreach initiatives that drive better member – and public - engagement and understanding of SPC’s work.
- Oversee communications reporting for organizational, donor and other reports.
- Work with MEL to ensure the high-quality presentation and content of reports resulting in donor satisfaction, and to contribute to ongoing resource mobilisation.

**People management and capacity building**

- Manage and report on delivery of SPC’s gender equality communication plans and related activities.
- Manage the leave approvals, management plans and performance appraisals of team.
- Conduct inward facing communication training for SPC HRSD team. Where practical, extend communications training to external partners including grantees and funded activities.

**One-SPC approach and integrated approaches to gender equality communications across SPC.**

- Participate in the One-SPC Gender Equality Flagship meetings and roundtable events contributing technical advice for strategic communications, while also supporting with visibility communications such as social media coverage of events.
- Co-lead the SPC Communications coordination for the PPA convening: the Triennial Conference of Pacific Women and the Pacific Ministers for Women Meeting.
- Participate in the monthly One-SPC core communications group meetings, monthly story group meetings and training organised by Corporate Communications throughout the year.
- Ensure all programmatic and divisional communications content meets brand guidelines, as well as content co-developed with partners (for projects led by SPC).

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A post graduate qualification in a relevant field such as journalism, communications, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7 years of strategic communications and visibility-related experience, preferably in the Pacific region.
- Experience managing the development and design of print, online and all multi-media communications materials for a range of audiences, to tight deadlines. Examples to be provided.
- Ability to translate text-heavy documents or information into user-friendly visual materials.
- Excellent interpersonal and representational skills with experience in building and maintaining effective working relationships with a range of different individuals and organisations.
- Demonstrated understanding and knowledge of Pacific cultural values, gender equality concepts and issues, human rights, good governance and development challenges in the region.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** –This position is funded until **31 December 2027** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Communications Adviser – Pacific Women Lead** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,703‒3,379 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 8,354–10,442 (USD 3,623-4,528; EUR 3,269-4,086). Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - Pacific Women Lead
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, education, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Human Rights and Social Development Division** has a vision for just, equitable and resilient Pacific societies and it aims to achieve this by advancing human rights, equality and social inclusion for all Pacific people, grounded in cultural values and principles. The work of this Division includes work previously undertaken by the Regional Rights Resource Team (RRRT) in the area of human rights and the Social Development Programme (SDP) in the areas of gender equality and social inclusion, culture and youth development.

In line with its vision, the work of the Division will encompass the following focal areas:

- **Objective 1:** Pacific institutions are strong, transparent, and responsive for upholding and promoting human rights and implementing inclusive, gender sensitive and culturally respectful development.
- **Objective 2:** Pacific Civil Society understand and can advocate for their rights and uphold cultural values.
- **Objective 3:** Pacific culture is protected, preserved, and promoted and culturally relevant and appropriate knowledge and systems are integrated across all work.
- **Objective 4:** All PSC programs and operations are grounded in people centered approaches and consider the rights and cultural values of diverse groups including women, children, youth and persons with disabilities.
- **Objective 5:** HRSD Division teams work collectively, coherently, and efficiently and to a high standard to achieve shared success for Pacific societies.

The Gender Equality Flagship aims to effectively support SPC’s member countries and territories in advancing gender equality with the vision of Pacific women and girls in all their diversity enjoy their fundamental human rights, are safe, empowered and equitably share resources, opportunities and decision-making with men and boys. The Flagship works across five dimensions:

- gender-based violence
- governance and leadership
- learning and livelihoods
- women’s and girls’ health
- resilience and climate action

The **Programme Coordinator – Pacific Women Lead** is a senior role in the Gender Equality pillar of the Human Rights and Social Development (HRSD) Business Plan and, in parallel, for the SPC Gender Equality Flagship. The role will lead and manage the operationalisation of the programme plan. This includes managing the programme team, providing technical, operational and administrative support, implementing activities, building capacity, and managing the programme budget and finances. The role also provides technical, programming and strategic direction to help ensure the programme achieves its goal and intended outcomes. Where work links the objectives of the HRSD work programme and the Gender Equality Flagship, the Programme Coordinator has a matrix reporting relationship with others in the team, as required. The role also develops its direct reports.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Manage day-to-day implementation of the programme and ensure high quality advice and technical support to the programme**

- Manage the PWL at SPC grant portfolio including project management, partnership management and monitoring, analysis and advice on grant progress
- Alongside the Manager Programmes (Pacific Women Lead at SPC) work to identify and develop new activities, systems and processes that will contribute to PWL at SPC outcomes. This includes developing concept notes, conducting due diligence assessments and finalising work plans, budgets and schedules for grant agreements.
- Provide technical inputs to the design, implementation and monitoring of programme activities.
- Review all materials and information developed under the programme.

**Supervision, mentoring and supporting team members**

- Supervise and mentors the advisers and programme officers.

- Provide advice, mentoring and support in the design and delivery of programme strategies, training programmes and other activities in relation to the programme.

**Strategic planning, policy and programming**

- Lead strategic advice with respect to planning, policies and programming for PWL at SPC.
- Contribute to national, sub-regional, regional and international planning, policies, programming and institutions that support PWL at SPC.

**Stakeholder engagement, networking and partnership coordination**

- Represent PWL at SPC and HRSD effectively at national, regional, and international forums.
- Liaise with stakeholders, including donors and programme partners and grantees, including to share information on progress and outcomes of the programme.
- Collaborate with other gender advisory units across SPC.
- Establish, strengthen, and support partnerships that advance the programme objectives at national, regional and international levels.

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning**

- Contribute to the design and implementation of effective MEL system for PWL at SPC, using both qualitative and quantitative indicators.

- With support from the MEL Manager, collate and document the learnings from the programme and feeds this into SPC’s overall MEL processes.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A post graduate degree in social sciences, development or related discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.
- Diploma or certificate course in programme management.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ experience in development programme management.
- Proven experience leading teams, including managing and developing teams, recruiting, supervising, appraising and mentoring staff.
- Extensive experience in programme management and reporting for large complex programmes including budget management, preferably for a development or donor-funded programme.
- Knowledge and understanding of gender equality concepts and issues, including in the Pacific including familiarity with the Pacific gender equality ecosystem and how it applies to programming
- Working knowledge of gender responsive planning, gender transformative approaches and MEL.
- Proven record of accomplishment in coordination and partnership building with donors, governments, development partners and civil society.
- Demonstrated understanding and knowledge of Pacific cultural values and international human rights principles and standards.
- Pacific experience and an in-depth understanding of the human rights (including violence against women), good governance and development challenges in the region.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** –This position is funded until **31 December 2027** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Programme Coordinator – Pacific Women Lead** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,743‒4,679 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 11,566–14,458 (USD 5,016–6,270; EUR 4,526–5,658). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva** – SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Development Effectiveness & Learning (DEL)
jobs.description:
**Program Background**

Climate Resilient Communities (CRC) supports implementation of the Australian Government's climate change commitments under *Australia's International Development Policy*, in line with partner government priorities.

CRC supports the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to increase climate investments, drive climate integration, and better address climate change and disaster risk across Australia’s development portfolio.

CRC incentivises funding towards gender-responsive, inclusive climate and disaster resilience programming, particularly in the water, food, nature-based solutions, and energy sectors.

DFAT has engaged DT Global to support the implementation of CRC through a Support Unit.

For further information about CRC, visit the [**DFAT website**](https://www.dfat.gov.au/international-relations/themes/climate-change/supporting-indo-pacific-tackle-climate-change/climate-resilient-communities).

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[**https://tinyurl.com/yeyufywe**](https://tinyurl.com/yeyufywe)

You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary team working to advance gender-responsive and inclusive climate and disaster resilience programming across the Indo-Pacific, while playing a central role in turning strategic priorities into well-coordinated, high-quality results.

jobs.description:

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Area Manager, reporting to the Deputy Director of Field Operations (DDFO), provides strategic leadership, oversight, programming/field operations, serving as the principal point of contact for government, UN bodies, and humanitarian stakeholders Office. The position ensures project alignment with organizational strategy, navigates complex regulatory environments, compliance. The post holder is expected to lead on the development, planning, implementation, and monitoring of programming closely across all departments, including Technical Advisors, Grant Acquisition and Management, Finance, People and Culture, Program Support, to achieve high-quality results and operational excellence.

Likewise, the Area Manager provides overall leadership and management of staff based in the Area Program, different technical units/departments, to ensure effective program operations and staff cohesion. Thus, Program will administratively report directly to the Area Manager and will have a dotted-line reporting Heads or Line Managers.

Internally, for smoother field operations processes, the Area Manager (AM) should ensure proper coordination operations staff and other departmental staff based in the Field office/Area Program. Likewise, the AM, leads the review and updating of internal field operations processes at the Area Program, in coordination functions, if and when needed.

**PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT**

- Provide oversight and support to ensure that projects assigned to Project Managers are properly planned and implemented to meet agreed results, timelines, and budget indicators.
- Ensure that assigned projects are adequately staffed to facilitate effective implementation.
- Facilitate reporting on the progress of field implementation.
- Analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of field implementation and introduce corrective measures where needed (key focus on managing burn rates).
- Ensure proper implementation of projects (financially and programmatically) according to WVSR standards throughout the life of the Project Cycle Management.
- In collaboration with the Partnerships Manager, identify areas for staff/partner development.

- Participate in relevant meetings, conferences, and cluster coordination forums by authorities, organized by authorities, UN agencies, and humanitarian actors.
- Lead discussions with security forces, local councils, and government entities to facilitate approvals, resolve access issues, and maintain operational continuity.
- Coordinate and engage the Risk and Compliance Unit for support for all Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) between WVSR and authorities, ensuring all agreements are finalized for the project start-up.

- Support the revision and correction of internal processes within WVSR in coordination with other departmental functions.

- Experience designing and implementing multi-sector humanitarian programs
- Experience managing and overseeing budgets of at least $3M

- Strong communication skills with the ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively (oral humanitarian community as well as with field practitioners.

**Location : NWS-Aleppo**

jobs.title: Title: Regional Study on Gender Dynamics, Risks, and Decision-Making Related to Syrian Returns in Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, and Syria
jobs.description:
**Title:** Regional Study on Gender Dynamics, Risks, and Decision-Making Related to Syrian Returns in Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, and Syria

**Background**

The question of Syrian return has gained renewed prominence across the region following shifts in the political and security landscape since late 2024. After more than a decade of protracted displacement, the Syria crisis remains one of the largest globally, with over 6.1 million Syrian refugees hosted primarily in neighboring countries, including approximately 2.9 million in Türkiye, 755,000 in Lebanon, and 611,000 in Jordan .

Since December 2024, there has been a significant increase in return movements, largely spontaneous and occurring under evolving and often uncertain conditions. As of early 2026, estimates indicate that over 1.5 million Syrians have returned to Syria from neighboring countries, primarily from Türkiye, Lebanon, and Jordan. Of these:

- Over 500,000 returns have been recorded from Türkiye alone
- Approximately 180,000 returns from Jordan
- Hundreds of thousands have returned from Lebanon, including over 500,000 departures reported in 2025 and 168000 due to the recent escalation in Lebanon

More broadly, over one million refugees have returned from neighboring countries since late 2024, alongside nearly two million internally displaced persons (IDPs) returning within Syria. Projections suggest that millions more may return in the coming years, underscoring the urgency of understanding return dynamics.

Despite these movements, returns are taking place in a context where 16.7 million people inside Syria still require humanitarian assistance, and where infrastructure, services, and protection systems remain severely strained. Evidence indicates that many returns are not necessarily driven by improved conditions in Syria alone, but also by increasing pressures in host countries, including economic hardship, restrictive policies, reduced assistance, and rising social tensions.

While the scale of return is growing, there remains a critical gap in understanding the gendered dimensions of return decision-making, experiences, and outcomes. Existing data and policy discussions often treat return as a household or population-level phenomenon, without adequately capturing how gender norms, roles, and power relations shape who decides, who moves, under what conditions, and with what consequences.

Women, men, girls, and boys experience displacement and return differently. Gender intersects with age, disability, marital status, legal status, caregiving roles, and access to resources, shaping:

- Return intentions and aspirations
- Exposure to risks and protection concerns
- Access to livelihoods, services, and documentation
- Reintegration outcomes and long-term sustainability

Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that many return decisions are not fully voluntary, but rather shaped by structural pressures, including:

- declining access to income and services in host countries,
- insecurity related to legal status and documentation,
- social and political pressure to return,
- and misinformation or lack of reliable information about conditions inside Syria.

At the same time, there is limited systematic evidence on the lived experiences of returnees, particularly from a gender perspective. Questions remain around:

- how return affects intra-household dynamics and decision-making power,
- how gender roles shift post-return,
- and whether return leads to improved safety, dignity, and resilience for different groups.

Given the scale of ongoing and anticipated return movements, there is an urgent need for a regional, gender-responsive analysis that captures both:

1. The perspectives of Syrians who have already returned, and
2. Those who are considering or planning return from host countries.

This study, covering Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, and Syria, aims to fill this gap by generating evidence on the gendered drivers, risks, decision-making processes, and reintegration outcomes of return. The findings will support more informed, rights-based, and gender-responsive approaches to policy, programming, and advocacy, ensuring that return processes align with principles of voluntariness, safety, dignity, and sustainability. In addition, there is a need to better understand how displacement itself may have reshaped gender norms, roles, and individual agency.

**Purpose and Objectives of the Study**

This study aims to generate evidence on the gendered drivers, decision-making processes, risks, and reintegration outcomes of Syrian return across Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, and Syria, in order to inform gender-responsive policy, programming, and advocacy, with a focus on how power, gender norms, and control over resources shape people’s ability to make decisions about return, mobility, and their future. Specifically, the study will:

- Examine how gender norms, roles, and intra-household power relations influence return intentions and decisions, including who decides, under what conditions, and to what extent decisions are voluntary**, as well as how perceived trade-offs related to safety, livelihoods, dignity, and personal freedoms influence these decisions.**
- Assess differentiated risks faced by women, men, girls, and boys in relation to return, including exposure to GBV, movement restrictions, forced recruitment, child protection risks, and social stigma.
- Analyze how gender affects access to civil documentation, housing, land and property (HLP), livelihoods, basic services, and mobility—both in shaping return decisions and in post-return reintegration.
- Evaluate the extent to which returns are safe, voluntary, and dignified, and how return impacts safety, economic security, social roles, and well-being across different population groups, including potential changes in agency, autonomy, and mobility, particularly for women and girls.
- Provide practical, gender-responsive recommendations to inform humanitarian and development programming, advocacy priorities, and policy engagement on Syrian return at national and regional levels.

**Scope of Work**

This study will be conducted at a **regional level**, covering **Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, and Syria**, and will generate both **comparative regional analysis** and **country-specific insights** on gendered dimensions of Syrian return based on primary information gathering.

The study will include:

- Syrians who have already returned to Syria, and
- Syrians currently residing in host countries who are considering, discussing, or planning return.

As part of the assignment, the consultant/team will be responsible for:

1. **Refining the research framework**
Further develop and refine the **research questions**, ensuring they capture gendered drivers, decision-making processes, risks, and reintegration outcomes across contexts.
2. **Designing a context-appropriate methodology**
Propose and apply a mixed-methods, gender-sensitive, and protection-informed research approach, combining:

- desk review of existing data and literature,
- qualitative methods (e.g. key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and in-depth interviews), and
- where feasible, complementary quantitative data collection or analysis.

The methodology should ensure disaggregation by sex, age, and other vulnerability factors, and allow for comparative analysis across countries and population groups.

1. **Defining sampling and geographic coverage**
Identify feasible and relevant locations and participant groups in each country, ensuring inclusion of diverse profiles (e.g. women, men, youth, persons with disabilities, and female-headed households).
2. **Conducting data collection and analysis**
Collect and analyze primary and secondary data to generate evidence on:

- gendered return intentions and pressures,
- protection risks,
- access to services and livelihoods,
- reintegration experiences and outcomes, and
- changes in gender norms, roles, and agency across pre-displacement, displacement, and post-return contexts.

1. **Producing actionable outputs**
Deliver a set of analytical outputs, including a regional report and practical recommendations to inform policy, advocacy, and programming.

**Key Principles**

The study will be guided by the following principles:

- Do No Harm: Ensure that all research activities minimize risks to participants and do not exacerbate existing vulnerabilities or protection concerns.
- Informed Consent: Participation must be fully voluntary, with clear explanation of the study purpose, use of data, and the right to withdraw at any time.
- Confidentiality and Data Protection: All data must be collected, stored, and reported in a manner that ensures anonymity and protects sensitive information.
- Gender-Responsive and Inclusive Approach: The research design must actively account for gender dynamics and ensure meaningful inclusion of women, men, girls, boys, and marginalized groups, while recognising them as active agents with diverse perspectives, preferences, and aspirations, rather than only as groups at risk.
- Protection-Centered Approach: All tools and interactions must be sensitive to protection risks, particularly related to GBV, child protection, and other vulnerabilities.
- Conflict Sensitivity: The study must consider the broader political and social context and avoid reinforcing tensions or harmful narratives.

**Ethical and Safeguarding Requirements**

The consultant/team must demonstrate a robust approach to ethics and safeguarding, including:

- Clear safeguarding protocols for working with vulnerable populations
- Procedures to ensure confidentiality, anonymity, and secure data management
- Protocols for handling distress, disclosure, or sensitive information, particularly related to GBV or protection concerns
- Identification of safe and appropriate referral pathways where needed
- Measures to avoid raising expectations related to assistance, return support, or services
- Commitment to SHEA (Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse) and Safeguarding principles, and to follow ActionAid’s related policies throughout the assignment
- This commitment must be written into the contract or signed together with it

All research activities must align with international ethical standards for research in humanitarian settings, particularly when engaging women, children, and other at-risk groups.

**Deliverables**

The consultant/team will be expected to produce the following:

1. Inception Report: Including refined research questions, methodology, sampling strategy, tools, workplan, and ethical safeguards.
2. Data Collection Tools: Draft and final versions of interview guides, FGD guides, and any survey tools, including consent protocols.
3. Preliminary Findings Presentation: A concise presentation of emerging findings for validation and feedback.
4. Draft Regional Report: Comprehensive analysis including methodology, findings, comparative insights, and initial recommendations.
5. Final Regional Report: Revised report incorporating feedback, with clear, actionable, gender-responsive recommendations.
6. Final Presentation: Presentation of key findings and recommendations to stakeholders.

**Duration**

The assignment is expected to be completed within **10–14 weeks.** The consultant/team is expected to propose a detailed timeline as part of the inception phase.

**Fees and Tax**

- The consultant is fully responsible for all taxes, and similar costs linked to this assignment.
- The agreed fee is inclusive of all taxes, including income tax.
- ActionAid will not pay any tax or similar cost on top of the agreed fee.
- Payment is not on a “plus tax” or “net of tax” basis. The amount in the contract is the total amount ActionAid will pay.
- Consultants should set their rates knowing they must cover their own tax obligations from the fee.
- Consultants based outside Jordan should state their country of tax residence in the financial proposal.

**Team Requirements**

The assignment may be undertaken by an individual consultant or a team, with preference for a multidisciplinary team covering the full regional scope.

**Required expertise:**

- Proven experience in gender analysis and feminist research approaches
- Strong knowledge of Syria displacement, return dynamics, and regional contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye, Syria)
- Demonstrated expertise in qualitative and/or mixed-methods research
- Experience working on protection, GBV, or humanitarian programming
- Strong analytical and report-writing skills in English

**Language requirements:**

- **Fluency in Arabic is required**

**Desirable:**

- Experience working with women-led, refugee-led, or local civil society organizations
- Experience translating research into policy and advocacy outputs

**Application Requirements**

Interested consultants or teams are requested to submit a complete application package including the following:

1. **Technical Proposal**
Including:

- Understanding of the assignment and key issues

jobs.description:
**About ACTED**

“ We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

- Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.
- Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles

jobs.description:
**Senior Technical Advisor – Capacity Development (Civil Defence), Syrian Arab Republic**

**The starting salary package for this position is £87,628 GBP, including all allowances.**

**This is a fixed-term role for 18 months.**

**This is an unaccompanied post.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

Reporting to the Country Director with a technical line to the Technical Director, you will be responsible for Leading MAG’s capacity development partnership with Syria Civil Defence, providing senior technical advice at institutional level and building a nationally owned capacity to plan, manage and deliver explosive ordnance response and risk education safely and to standard. Managing MAG’s embedded capacity development team, ensuring their work is coordinated, technically sound and directed towards agreed capacity development outcomes.

As well as support the Country Director in developing the strategy, plans, proposals and budgets for this workstream, and to manage MAG’s contractual and reporting obligations to the donors funding it. Represent MAG on capacity development matters with Civil Defence, SNMAC, the Ministry, UNMAS, GICHD, donors and the wider mine action sector.

**About the Syria programme:**

MAG has been responding to the Syria crisis since 2013, working to support development by finding and destroying the explosive remnants of war so that communities can raise their families and pursue their livelihoods in a safe and secure environment, free from fear of death or injury. In addition to our current programme in the North East, you will also support the safe expansion of initiatives across all of Syria, based on where and how opportunities arise in the future.

**Responsibilities:**

**Institutional Capacity Development and Technical Governance**

· Lead MAG’s technical relationship and capacity development partnership with Civil Defence, agreeing institutional priorities, intended outcomes and a sequenced capacity development plan.

· Oversee the development and embedding of the systems needed for safe and effective delivery, including training, standard operating procedures, quality management, accreditation and operational information management, aligned with National Mine Action Standards, IMAS and MAG Global Technical Standards.

· Advise Civil Defence leadership on operational planning, tasking, prioritisation, equipment and resource requirements, and support preparation for accreditation and formal national tasking arrangements.

· Coordinate the specialist input required from MAG and external partners to address wider institutional capacity needs, avoid duplication and support the mobilisation of appropriate resources.

· Support Civil Defence participation in relevant standards, technical and sector coordination processes, and promote learning and exchange with other national mine action capacities.

**Management of the Capacity Development Team**

· Line manage the Technical Field Managers, Community Liaison Manager and National Technical Coordinator, setting clear objectives, monitoring performance and ensuring their work is integrated and directed towards agreed capacity development outcomes.

· Ensure that embedded staff mentor and coach rather than substitute for Civil Defence personnel, and oversee the quality of mentoring, on-the-job training and technical support provided to supported teams.

· Manage, motivate and develop the team, ensuring appropriate recruitment, appraisal and development arrangements and compliance with MAG policies, SOPs, safeguarding requirements and agreed boundaries with Civil Defence.

**Community Liaison and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education**

· Provide strategic and technical oversight of the development of Civil Defence’s community liaison and explosive ordnance risk education capacity, including appropriate procedures, training, materials, targeting and delivery methods.

· Ensure that community liaison supports non-technical survey, task prioritisation and community reporting of hazards, with relevant information incorporated into national systems.

· Promote coordination with national authorities, UNICEF and the wider sector, and ensure that quality assurance, delivery data and community feedback inform continuous improvement and the transition to Civil Defence-led delivery.

**Programme Development, Donor Management and Representation**

· Support the Country Director in developing the strategy, operational plans, proposals, budgets and medium-term resource requirements for the capacity development workstream.

· Manage MAG’s contractual and reporting obligations to donors funding this work, working with programme funding colleagues and the Programmes Quality Team to ensure compliance and timely, accurate reporting.

· Represent MAG on capacity development matters with Civil Defence, SNMAC, relevant ministries, UN agencies, donors, technical bodies and sector coordination mechanisms.

· Keep the Country Director, Technical Director and Programmes Quality Team appropriately briefed on significant technical, operational, relationship and delivery issues.

· Contribute learning from Syria to MAG’s wider approach to capacity development and localisation, including the development of organisational policy, guidance and standard approaches.

**Technical Safety, Risk and Quality**

· Within the authority delegated to the role, ensure that the health and safety of MAG staff working on the project is effectively managed in line with MAG policy and standards.

· Ensure that MAG’s and Civil Defence’s respective responsibilities, operational boundaries and risk controls are clearly documented, understood and applied in practice.

· Advise the Country Director on technical, operational and contextual security risks arising from work alongside Civil Defence, and contribute to programme risk management and the country Incident Management Team.

· Ensure that accidents, incidents and technical non-conformities involving MAG staff or supported Civil Defence teams are reported, investigated and analysed within MAG’s remit, and that corrective actions and learning are followed through.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Essential Experience**

· Senior experience of developing, implementing and leading humanitarian mine action operations in conflict-affected contexts, including responsibility for multi-team or multi-asset delivery, staff, resources and budgets.

· Experience of designing and leading capacity development or localisation programmes with national authorities, national operators or local partner organisations.

· Experience of developing and embedding technical SOPs, training programmes and quality management arrangements within an organisation.

· Experience of leading and developing diverse teams and of mentoring and coaching national counterparts to build sustainable capability.

· Experience of developing and managing institutional donor-funded programmes, including proposals, budgets, reports and contractual obligations.

**Essential Skills and Knowledge**

· Strong and current technical knowledge of explosive ordnance, EOD and clearance, with the judgement to translate policies and standards into practical plans, procedures and controls.

· Strong organisational and strategic planning skills, including the ability to identify capacity gaps, coordinate complex work over the medium to long term and draw in appropriate internal or external expertise.

· Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication, interpersonal and diplomatic skills, with the ability to influence and build trust with national authorities, partners and donors.

**Essential Qualifications**

· Explosive Ordnance Qualification to IMAS Level 3, meeting the requirements established in IMAS 09.30/01/2022, from a recognised military, civilian or humanitarian mine action organisation.

**Desirable Experience, Skills and Knowledge**

· Experience in Syria or a comparable Middle Eastern mine action context, ideally involving a civil defence or first-responder organisation.

· Experience of developing National Mine Action Standards or contributing to relevant technical working groups.

· Knowledge and experience of community liaison, EORE, non-technical survey and mine action information-management systems, including IMSMA or comparable systems.

· Experience of integrated land release, EOD and clearance in an urban environment.

· Written and spoken Arabic language skills.

**Desirable Qualifications**

· Explosive Ordnance Qualification to IMAS Level 3+ and/or IEDD Level 3+ from a recognised military, civilian or humanitarian mine action organisation.

· Formal accident and incident investigation training, a recognised programme or project management qualification, or a degree in a relevant subject.

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

Women are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Financial Analyst, Manchester UK**

**The starting salary package for this position is £35,604 GBP (plus contributory pension)**

**This is a fixed-term role for 6 months.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in over 40 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

The Finance Analyst (FA) will provide remote finance and analytical support to the MAG Ukraine Programme from the UK. The role will focus on financial analysis, budget monitoring, forecasting, donor and management reporting, data quality and month-end support. Working closely with the Ukraine Finance team and relevant UK colleagues, the FA will help turn financial data into clear information for programme decision-making, identify variances and trends, and support timely follow-up on financial actions.

**About the Ukraine programme:**

Since the Russian invasion of 24 February 2022, Ukraine has been subjected to heavy artillery bombardment, missile, and air strikes, as well as the use of landmines and cluster munitions. The scale of the conflict and the use of high impact and indiscriminate weapons requires an urgent and extensive response. MAG responded to the crisis in 2022 and now employs nearly 440 staff in our Ukraine programme, in a range of operational and support/administrative activities, with further scale-up planned during 2026. The programme has a representation office in Kyiv, and operational offices in Mykolaiv (also covering accessible areas of Kherson) and Kharkiv.

**Responsibilities:**

• Prepare and maintain regular budget versus actual analysis for Ukraine projects, departments and cost centres, highlighting significant variances, trends and areas requiring follow-up.

• Support the preparation and updating of programme forecasts, working with budget holders and the Ukraine Finance team to ensure assumptions are clear, reasonable and supported.

• Assist with monthly management accounts and internal financial reporting, including concise commentary for managers and budget holders.

• Support with budgets for proposals or realignments throughout project periods

• Support donor financial reporting and grant-management processes, including review of expenditure, coding, supporting schedules and reconciliation to approved budgets.

• Review financial data for completeness, accuracy and consistency, and raise identified issues with the relevant Finance team member or budget holder.

• Develop and maintain clear financial analysis tools, trackers, and Excel-based reports to support programme management and decision-making.

• Assist with project set-up, budget coding and the maintenance of accurate project and donor financial records.

• Provide finance support to budget holders, helping them understand expenditure, forecasts, variances, and financial responsibilities.

• Work closely with the Ukraine Finance team, Programme colleagues and MAG UK Finance to resolve financial queries and improve the quality and timeliness of financial information.

• Provide ad-hoc financial analysis in response to programme priorities, including scenario modelling, cost comparisons, and other management information as required.

• Maintain confidentiality and ensure all work is carried out in accordance with MAG financial policies, procedures, safeguarding requirements and standards of conduct.

• Undertake other similar finance and analytical duties as reasonably required to support the Ukraine

Programme.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Knowledge and Experience**

- Relevant finance, accounting, economics or business qualification, or equivalent practical experience.
- Good understanding of accounting principles, budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting.

**Skills**

- Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify, explain and communicate financial trends and variances.
- Advanced working knowledge of Microsoft Excel; experience of finance systems and data analysis tools is desirable.
- Good written and spoken English. Ukrainian language skills are strongly desirable for effective support to the Ukraine Programme.
- Excellent attention to detail, organisation and ability to work accurately with large volumes of financial information.

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website\*\*.\*\*

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

**Programme Officer, Senegal**

**The starting salary package for this position is £34,580 GBP, including all allowances.**

**This is a fixed-term role for 6 months with a possibility of extension.**

**This is an unaccompanied post.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

Reporting to the Country Director, you will provide direct support to the Country Director in the effective management and implementation of MAG’s programme in Senegal. The role will support grant and project management, donor

reporting and proposal development, project monitoring including the follow-up of results and indicators, and

internal and external programme communications and visibility. The Programme Officer will work across the

programme to ensure that project information is accurate, up to date and clearly communicated, and will contribute

to the effective delivery and continued development of MAG’s activities in Senegal.

**About the Senegal programme:**

MAG has been working in Senegal since 2014, initially supporting the Senegalese Armed Forces with safe destruction of obsolete ammunition, secure storage, and capacity-building. Since 2021, MAG has expanded into Humanitarian Mine Action in Casamance, at the request of the National Mine Action Centre (CNAMS). In Casamance, MAG supports CNAMS through training, strengthening information management systems, and conducting non-technical surveys and risk education to better understand contamination and raise awareness among affected communities. Casamance remains contaminated with mines and explosive remnants of war, limiting access to land and livelihoods. Through the new CLEAR-Casamance project, MAG will reduce these risks, release safe land, and restore access to productive areas. This will support recovery, enable displaced families to return safely, and contribute to lasting peace and stability in the region.

**Responsibilities:**

**Grant management & monitoring**

• Provide day-to-day monitoring of grants and contracts according to work plans agreed by the CD.

• Support the CD to ensure effective grant management and the timely preparation and submission of donor reports.

• Provide timely and accurate information and analysis on current grant and proposal status, as required by the CD and MAG HQ.

• Maintain up-to-date grant management tools, including reporting deadlines, key deliverables and donor requirements.

• Coordinate the collection of information required for proposal development, including programme, operational and financial inputs.

• Contribute when required by CD to donor meetings, visits and briefings, including the preparation of relevant programme information and materials.

**Programme Monitoring & Information Management**

• Develop and maintain systems and tools for recording and monitoring programme activities, outputs, results and indicators.

• Coordinate the regular collection and consolidation of programme data, ensuring information is complete, accurate and up to date.

• Monitor progress against project indicators and targets and highlight gaps or areas requiring follow-up.

• Support the analysis of programme data and results to inform project management, donor reporting and programme decision-making.

• Establish appropriate internal reporting formats and ensure effective information flows between field teams, the country office and MAG HQ.

**Programme Communications & Visibility**

• Support the development and implementation of communications and visibility activities for the Senegal programme.

• Develop high-quality communication materials, including case studies, success stories, programme brief, brochures, presentations and other donor-facing materials.

• Collect and develop programme content, including stories, photographs, key results and operational updates, in coordination with programme and field teams.

• Use tools such as Canva to produce professional and visually engaging communication and visibility materials.

• Ensure that communication materials are consistent with MAG’s corporate identity, messaging and communication guidelines, in coordination with MAG HQ Communications.

• Support donor visibility requirements across projects and ensure that relevant visibility commitments are appropriately implemented.

• Maintain an organised library of programme communication materials, including photographs, case studies and key programme information.

• Support and train programme staff on MAG’s communications and visibility guidelines, including the appropriate collection and use of photographs, beneficiary stories and informed consent.

• Assist in the planning and hosting of programme visits by MAG staff, donors and partner agencies.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Essential Experience**

• Significant experience working in development and humanitarian program related field operations or field activities in developing countries

• Experience of developing and supporting projects.

**Essential Skills and Knowledge**

• Experience working in humanitarian or development programmes.

• Experience in grant/project management, including donor reporting and monitoring of project results and

indicators.

• Experience supporting the development of proposals.

• Experience developing communication and visibility materials for programmes, including case studies, programme briefs, brochures and donor-facing materials.

• Experience using tools such as Canva to produce professional communication products.

• Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn programme information and results into clear and engaging content.

• Good eye for visual presentation and attention to detail.

**Desirable**

**Community Liaison Manager, Ukraine**

**The starting salary package for this position is £47,910.80 GBP including all allowances.**

**This is a fixed-term role for 12 months.**

**This is an unaccompanied post.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in over 40 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

In this role, you will play a vital part in supporting communities living with the daily realities of explosive ordnance. As Community Liaison Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring MAG’s approach to community participation lead how communities shape and guide our mine action work, ensuring their knowledge, priorities, and concerns are central to everything we do in your area of operation. In close coordination with the Community Liaison Manager – Team Leader, you will manage and mentor Community Liaison teams, work closely with technical colleagues, and ensure high‑quality delivery of non‑technical survey and explosive ordnance risk education that directly informs safe land release and clearance.

**About the Ukraine programme:**

Since the Russian invasion of 24th February 2022, Ukraine has been subjected to heavy artillery bombardment, missile, and air strikes, as well as the use of landmines and cluster munitions. The scale of the conflict and the use of high impact and indiscriminate weapons requires an urgent and extensive response. MAG responded to the crisis in 2022 and now employs nearly 440 staff in our Ukraine programme, in a range of operational and support/administrative activities, with further scale-up planned during 2026. The programme has a representation office in Kyiv, and operational offices in Mykolaiv (also covering accessible areas of Kherson) and Kharkiv.

**Responsibilities:**

**Technical**

· Provide technical guidance on non-technical survey (NTS) and explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) to CL teams.

· Contribute to decision-making on tasking for NTS and EORE activities

· Liaise with technical teams to facilitate CL support to clearance operations

· Support and build the capacity of teams on analysis of evidence and decision making during the NTS process

· Conduct QA on NTS and EORE activities within the area of operations

· Support the development, testing, and deployment of new EORE materials and modalities

· Provide research and analysis of relevant socio-economic data in order to help prioritise social target groups and geographical areas for EORE and land release activities.

· Conduct on-going liaison with all relevant stakeholders (government, INGOs, national NGOs, mine action centres, the military, health care providers etc.) and establish and maintain networks for information exchange.

· Maximise productivity, project outcomes and cost benefit to the donor and beneficiaries through CL programme activities.
