jobs.title: Directeur.trice Général.e
jobs.description:
*Zie hieronder voor een beschrijving in het Nederlands.*

**Avocats Sans Frontières (ASF), fondée en 1992 à Bruxelles, est une ONG internationale spécialisée dans la promotion de l'accès à la justice et la défense des droits humains. ASF lutte contre les injustices au sein de nos sociétés et promeut le principe de l'État de droit fondé sur les droits humains.**

La fonction de Directeur / Directrice Général(e) s’inscrit dans le pilotage stratégique et institutionnel global du réseau international d’ASF. Elle garantit la cohérence et l’impact d’ASF, tandis que les Directeurs Régionaux et les Directeurs Pays assurent le pilotage opérationnel de leurs zones respectives. Elle contribue ainsi à renforcer l’impact des interventions d’ASF pour les bénéficiaires finaux, tout en veillant à la qualité du fonctionnement, au développement et à l’intégrité d’ASF, dans le respect de ses valeurs fondatrices

## **Objectifs principaux de la fonction**

- **Garantir la performance, l’intégrité et le développement d’ASF**, dans le respect de ses valeurs et orientations, afin de renforcer durablement son impact auprès des bénéficiaires.
- **Piloter et fédérer l’organisation**, en définissant et en assurant la mise en œuvre de la stratégie globale, en mobilisant les équipes autour de l’approche « One ASF » et en garantissant la soutenabilité économique et la maîtrise des risques.
- **Porter et développer le rayonnement d’ASF**, en assurant sa responsabilité légale, administrative et financière, en renforçant la vie associative et les relations avec les organes de gouvernance, et en représentant l’organisation auprès des partenaires, bailleurs et réseaux d’ONGI.

## **Responsabilités de la fonction**

- *Définir et piloter la stratégie globale d’ASF* : élaborer le cadre stratégique avec le Comité stratégique, assurer sa déclinaison opérationnelle dans l’ensemble de l’organisation, définir les stratégies de financement et de partenariats, et piloter les évolutions nécessaires à la pérennité et au développement d’ASF.
- *Garantir la cohérence et la performance de l’action* : coordonner le Comité de Direction et les directions régionales/pays, mettre en place les outils de pilotage et de suivi, et veiller à la cohérence des stratégies d’intervention et de leur mise en œuvre avec le projet associatif défini par le CA et l’AG.
- *Assurer la responsabilité globale des opérations et des risques* : superviser les ressources humaines, les finances (incluant la définition d’adéquation des ressources aux besoins) et les opérations, garantir la mise en œuvre des dispositifs de sécurité et apporter un soutien direct aux équipes dirigeantes en cas de crises sécuritaires, juridiques, administratives ou opérationnelles.
- *Superviser le Comité de direction* à scope international et assurer, en collaboration avec les Directeurs Régionaux et les Directeurs Pays, l'animation globale et la cohésion de l'ensemble des équipes d'ASF dans ses différents pays d'intervention.

**Advocaten Zonder Grenzen (ASF) is een internationale NGO gespecialiseerd in het bevorderen van toegang tot de rechtspraak en de verdediging van mensenrechten, opgericht in 1992 in Brussel. ASF strijdt tegen onrechtvaardigheid in onze samenlevingen en draagt het principe uit van de rechtsstaat gebaseerd op mensenrechten.**

De functie van Algemeen Directeur/Directrice situeert zich in de globale strategische en institutionele aansturing van het internationale netwerk van ASF. Ze waarborgt de samenhang en de impact van ASF, terwijl de Regionale Directeurs en de Landendirecteurs instaan voor de operationele aansturing van hun respectieve zones. Op die manier versterkt de functie de impact van de interventies van ASF voor de eindbegunstigden en waakt ze over de kwaliteit van de werking, de ontwikkeling en de integriteit van ASF, met respect voor haar waarden vooropgesteld bij de oprichting.

## **Hoofddoelstellingen van de functie**

- **De prestaties, de integriteit en de ontwikkeling van ASF waarborgen**, met respect voor haar waarden en krachtlijnen, teneinde haar impact voor de begunstigden blijvend te versterken.
- **De organisatie aansturen en verenigen**, door de globale strategie te bepalen en de uitvoering ervan te verzekeren, de teams te mobiliseren rond de "One ASF"-benadering en de economische leefbaarheid en de risicobeheersing te garanderen.
- **De uitstraling van ASF dragen en uitbouwen**, door de juridische, administratieve en financiële verantwoordelijkheid op te nemen, door het verenigingsleven en de relaties met de bestuursorganen te versterken en de organisatie te vertegenwoordigen bij partners, donoren en netwerken van internationale ngo's.

**Verantwoordelijkheden van de functie**

- *De globale strategie van ASF bepalen en aansturen*: het strategisch kader uitwerken met het Strategisch Comité, de operationele vertaling ervan in de hele organisatie verzekeren, de strategieën inzake financiering en partnerschappen bepalen en de nodige evoluties sturen voor het voortbestaan en de groei van ASF.
- *De samenhang en de performantie van de actie waarborgen*: het Directiecomité en de Regionale Directeurs en Landendirecties coördineren, sturings- en opvolgingsinstrumenten invoeren en waken over de coherentie van de interventiestrategieën en de uitvoering ervan met de visie en het project van ASF zoals bepaald door de Raad van Bestuur en de Algemene Vergadering.
- *De algemene verantwoordelijkheid voor de operaties en de risico's opnemen*: toezicht houden op de human resources, de financiën (inclusief het bepalen van de afstemming van de middelen op de noden) en de operaties, de uitvoering van de veiligheidsmaatregelen waarborgen en de leidinggevende teams rechtstreeks ondersteunen bij veiligheids-, juridische, administratieve of operationele crisissen.
- *Het Directiecomité begeleiden* op internationaal vlak en in samenwerking met de Regionale Directeurs en de Landendirecteurs instaan voor de globale dynamiek en de samenhang van alle teams van ASF in de verschillende landen waar ASF intervenieert.

jobs.description:
Communications Officer

Full-time: 37.5 hours per week

Line managed by: Communications Manager

Salary: starting at £29,000

Location: London, UK – hybrid with at least 2 days in GISF’s London office

## About GISF

The Global Interagency Security Forum (GISF) is a member-led NGO network working to strengthen security risk management across the humanitarian and development sectors. With over 150 member organisations, GISF provides resources, convening spaces, and expertise to help keep aid workers safe.

GISF also leads communications for several strategic initiatives and delivers a programme of events, campaigns, and resources that strengthen NGO security risk management.

## About the role

We’re looking for an enthusiastic and organised Communications Officer to join our friendly team. This is a varied and hands-on role that would suit someone who enjoys working with people, is confident communicating with different audiences, and is keen to strengthen their skills across digital communications, content, and events.

The Communications Officer is responsible for the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications and content. Working closely with the Communications Manager and colleagues across GISF, the postholder will manage GISF’s digital channels, produce, and publish engaging content, and support communications for GISF’s programmes, events, publications, and campaigns.

A key focus of the role is strengthening GISF’s use of digital communications and data. The postholder will monitor performance across GISF’s website, social media, and email channels, using analytics and audience insights to understand what is working and inform continuous improvements to content and channel delivery.

As part of a small Secretariat, the postholder will work across multiple projects and priorities and will need to be organised, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day communications delivery. The postholder will work closely with colleagues across GISF to help deliver engaging communications and to ensure our members, supporters and stakeholders stay informed and connected.

## Key responsibilities

### Digital communication and content creation

- Manage the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications across its website, social media, newsletters, and member-only community platform.
- Plan, produce, schedule, and publish digital content, adapting messaging, format, and presentation for different audiences and channels.
- Gather stories, case studies, and updates from colleagues, members, and community partners, and explore creative and multimedia approaches to communicating GISF’s work.
- Help maintain GISF’s social media channels, creating simple graphics and promotional materials using Canva and existing templates.
- Keep up to date with social media trends, platform developments, and best-practice techniques, applying learning to strengthen content and drive audience engagement.
- Manage the production and delivery of GISF’s newsletters and other email communications, including building and scheduling campaigns and maintaining mailing lists and audience segments.
- Deliver engaging communications to GISF members, working closely with the Membership/Engagement team to ensure members receive timely and relevant information about GISF activities, opportunities, and resources.

### Analytics and digital performance

- Monitor and analyse performance across GISF’s website, social media and email channels, producing regular reporting against agreed objectives and KPIs.
- Use analytics and audience insights to understand audience behaviour and inform improvements to content, formats, targeting, timing and channel delivery.
- Support the Communications Manager to evaluate communications activities and strengthen GISF’s approach to measuring communications performance and impact.
- Keep abreast of developments in digital communications, platforms and tools, identifying opportunities to strengthen GISF’s digital communications.

### Events and communications delivery

- Support the planning and delivery of events, workshops, and community engagement activities, helping with registrations, event materials, presentations, signage, and promotional resources.
- Help coordinate practical arrangements with venues, suppliers, digital agencies, and colleagues.
- Gather feedback from participants to inform future events and communications.
- Support the delivery and dissemination of GISF research and publications, including coordinating copyediting, design, and other production processes where required
- Ensure communications outputs consistently meet GISF’s editorial, brand and accessibility standards.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across GISF to coordinate communications requirements, deadlines, and inputs.
- Help keep communications templates and shared documents organised and up to date, and support consistent ways of working.
- Respond to, or route, general communications queries received through GISF’s shared inboxes.
- Undertake other duties as may reasonably be required, consistent with the level and purpose of the role.

## Person specification

### Essential experience and skills

- Experience creating digital communications, gained through employment, internships, volunteering, freelance work or other relevant settings.
- Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear and engaging content for different audiences and digital channels.
- Strong visual communication and design skills, with experience creating engaging graphics and digital content using tools such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
- Creativity and a strong visual eye, with the ability to develop engaging content ideas and present information in accessible ways.
- An understanding of digital communications and how websites, social media, and email can be used to reach and engage different audiences
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
- Ability to work collaboratively and communicate effectively with colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Enthusiastic, with a can-do attitude and a willingness to learn, and an ability to build positive relationships with a wide range of people, including members, partners and colleagues.
- Confidence and technical know-how for using digital tools and learning new systems.

### Desirable experience and skills

- A degree in Communications or related qualifications
- Experience working in, or an interest in, the humanitarian, development, charity or NGO sector.
- Experience using website content management systems, email marketing platforms, or digital analytics tools
- Experience producing or editing video, photography, or other multimedia content.
- Experience creating content for social media, websites or newsletters, or supporting events and community activities.
- Familiarity with website CMS systems, social media scheduling tools, CRM systems, newsletter platforms and event platforms such as Eventbrite.

### What we offer

- 25 days of annual leave increasing annually after 2 years, up to a maximum 30 days (plus bank holidays)
- Office shutdown between Christmas and New Year
- Employer Pension contributions
- A focus on professional development, including access to overseas events, workshops; and CharityComms membership for training and development opportunities, mentoring, events, resources and networking with communications professionals across the charity sector.

## Purpose of the Post

Under the supervision of the Senior Human Resources Officer and close coordination with the HR Officer (Entitlements and Information Management), the incumbent supports the accurate, timely, and compliant administration of payroll, compensation, benefits, and staff entitlements, contributing to the effective delivery of high-quality human resources services.

### Required Competencies

- Ability to plan, organize and prioritize a high volume of tasks/transactions and manage time efficiently to meet deadlines.
- Thoroughness and meticulous attention to detail, ensuring accuracy of output.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure with a hands-on and solutions-oriented approach.
- Effective oral and written communication skills, with the ability to provide clear guidance and explain complex payroll concepts and processes in a concise and understandable manner to diverse audiences.
- Ability to work harmoniously, build and maintain effective working relationships with staff at all levels in a multicultural team.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and to deal tactfully in all situations and interactions.

### Professional Experience

A minimum of six years of relevant experience in payroll, HR, and social security/pension administration, or related areas are essential. Experience with an international Organization, especially within the United Nations Common System, would be an asset.

### Education

A minimum of completed secondary education is required for this role. A qualification in finance or human resources (payroll) would be an added advantage.

### Language Skills

Complete proficiency in English (oral and written), including ability to draft clearly and concisely. Working knowledge of any other UN languages would be an asset.

### Other Skills

Ability to effectively use MS Office tools (Windows, Word, Power Point, Excel and standard database software). Working knowledge of SharePoint, and an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system such as SAP, Umoja, PeopleSoft or similar Payroll/HR ERP is desirable.

## Main Duties and Responsibilities

The successful candidate would provide a broad range of administrative, HR (including payroll), and financial support to the team. The incumbent will:

- Create, maintain staff appointments and related personnel data in SAP, applying the appropriate salary, benefits and entitlements for different staff categories in accordance with applicable rules and procedures.
- Liaise with the Workforce Planning team to ensure the timely transmission of all required documentation for the smooth appointment and onboarding of staff.
- Respond to staff queries on all payroll-related matters and escalate to appropriate officers in cases of complex queries.
- Prepare staff cost estimates for incoming Junior Professional Officers (JPOs) and Senior Professional Officers (SPOs) based on Member States’ requirements and their Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
- Administer and monitor compensation and benefits actions, ensuring timely and accurate payroll processing of staff status changes, including within-grade increases, promotions, and seasonal ticket loans as applicable.
- Create and administer health insurance-related-payroll records and process related changes for newly appointed, serving and retired staff members.
- Ensure all entitlements changes are processed before the payroll cutoff date and create entries for all payroll actions in the SAP log.
- Administer staff separations and end-of-service benefits, including separation processing, repatriation-related entitlements, payment of unused annual leave and recovery or referral of outstanding obligations, as applicable.
- Conduct thorough reviews of supporting documentation to determine staff entitlement and eligibility in accordance with the Staff Regulations and Staff Rules and escalate complex cases as required.
- Coordinate with the external pension administrators and other relevant stakeholders on pension-related notifications, deductions, separations and staff queries, within established procedures.
- Maintain accurate, secure and confidential payroll and personnel records in accordance with applicable information-management and data-protection requirements.
- Assist in the onboarding of newly recruited staff members.
- Contribute to initiatives, projects, and activities of Human Resources Services.
- Perform other duties, as may be required

## **Contract Information**

\*Local status requires applicants to have unhindered permission to live and work in the UK.

jobs.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF Ljubljana is a permanent DCAF regional office, based in Slovenia. The office is responsible for two main programmes: implementation of the Police Cooperation Convention for Southeast Europe (PCC SEE) and the Western Balkans Border Security Programme (BSP). With funding from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), DCAF Ljubljana is implementing the “CHAIN BiH” project, which aims to strengthen sub-national case-building and inter-agency coordination against organised immigration crime (OIC) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on Una-Sana Canton. DCAF Ljubljana is looking to employ a motivated, well-organised and positive individual to be our next **Project Officer (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: DCAF Ljubljana, Slovenia, with frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina \***

**Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: Fixed-term employment until 31 March 2029, with the possibility of extension \*\***

**The role**

Join DCAF Ljubljana as a Project Officer, supporting the implementation of the project “CHAIN BiH”. Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for the operational, logistical, administrative and financial support of project activities, and will contribute to monitoring, evaluation and learning, reporting and coordination with national and cantonal partners in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

**Key areas of operation**

**Project implementation support**

- Support the Project Manager in the planning, organisation and day-to-day implementation of project activities, including workshops, trainings, field visits, working meetings and meetings of the Practice Review Forum.
- Manage the logistical and administrative preparation of activities, including travel, venues, interpretation and translation, participant lists and procurement of goods and services, in line with DCAF procedures.
- Prepare background materials, agendas, presentations, minutes and summary notes of meetings and activities.
- Support the evidence-gathering and diagnostic work of the project, including the collection, organisation and basic analysis of information from the field.

**Coordination and communication**

- Maintain regular contact with focal points in partner institutions, external experts and service providers.
- Support the organisation of the participation of officers from EU Member States within the framework of the PCC SEE.

**Financial and administrative management**

- Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget in close cooperation with the Project Manager and the DCAF finance and administration team.
- Prepare, verify and file financial documentation, contracts, invoices and supporting documents in compliance with donor and DCAF requirements.
- Keep project documentation and records complete, accurate and audit-ready.

**Monitoring, reporting and visibility**

- Collect and maintain monitoring data against project indicators, including sex- and age-disaggregated data, and support the documentation of lessons learned.
- Contribute to the preparation of narrative and financial reports for the donor and DCAF management.
- Support project visibility and communication activities in accordance with donor requirements.

**Your experience**

We are looking for a motivated, well-organised and detail-oriented professional with solid experience in supporting international projects, who enjoys working in a team and in a multi-cultural institutional environment.

You bring

- University degree (Bachelor’s or higher) in a relevant field (e.g., security studies, law, social studies, international relations, public administration, economics or related disciplines)
- 3 to 5 years professional experience, including a minimum of 2 years of experience in supporting the implementation of international projects
- Experience in the organisation and logistics of events, trainings and meetings
- Experience in contributing to project monitoring and to narrative and financial reporting
- Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in multi-cultural environments;
- Professional working proficiency in English and Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, including the ability to provide consecutive interpretation;
- Very good knowledge of Microsoft Office tools, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

**Desirable assets**

The following would be considered an advantage:

- Experience in project administration and financial monitoring, including handling of financial documentation in line with donor requirements
- Familiarity with UK Government (FCDO)-funded programmes or other bilateral donor-funded projects
- Experience working with international organisations or EU-funded programmes
- Understanding of gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) principles and experience with collecting disaggregated data

**We offer**

At DCAF Ljubljana, you will have the opportunity to contribute to a project that supports more effective, rights-based responses to organised immigration crime and stronger security sector governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

We offer:

- an opportunity to work on a high-impact international project with tangible regional impact
- a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience
- the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people
- opportunity for professional growth, international networking and continuous learning
- the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

***\* The post holder is expected to undertake regular travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to Una-Sana Canton.***

***\*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.***

**Your experience**

jobs.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

The Europe and Asia Entity at DCAF works across Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus, Central Asia and other parts of Europe and Asia, providing policy advice, capacity-building, technical assistance and support to institutional reforms. Its work covers areas such as democratic oversight, accountability, integrity and anti-corruption, human rights, defence and security governance, and institutional resilience, working closely with governments, parliaments, security institutions, civil society and international partners.

For our country office in Kyiv, Ukraine, we are looking for a highly-motivated and dynamic individual to be our next **National Advisor (Europe and Asia).**

**The role**

The National Advisor provides senior substantive expertise and policy advice on DCAF’s civilian security sector governance portfolio in Ukraine. The position supports policy dialogue, programme development and implementation, and sustained engagement with relevant Ukrainian state institutions, law enforcement actors, oversight bodies and civil society. The National Advisor monitors emerging reform priorities and developments in the security sector and translates these into relevant programming priorities and opportunities for DCAF engagement.

The position contributes to ensuring that DCAF’s support is grounded in the Ukrainian context and responsive to both ongoing reform processes and the realities of the wartime environment. jobs.location: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

jobs.description:
The Head of Information, Communication and Technology Services (ICTS) reports directly to the Chief of Central Support Services within the Administrative Division and provides strategic leadership for all ICTS activities in support of IMO’s programmes and long-term modernization objectives.

The role is responsible for developing and implementing IMO’s digital strategy, strengthening ICT governance, and ensuring that secure, reliable, and scalable technology services support business needs. This includes leading digital transformation, ERP integration, cloud adoption, cybersecurity maturity, and data-driven decision-making.

As the principal advisor to senior management on technology, digital services, data, enterprise architecture, and ICT operations, the Head of ICTS translates business priorities into practical technology solutions and maintains an information and technology architecture roadmap aligned with organizational goals.

The Head of ICTS leads the development, management, and enforcement of ICT policies, standards, frameworks, and guidance across IMO. The role also promotes continuous improvement, collaboration, service excellence, and innovation within the ICT function.

The Head of ICTS oversees information security operations, ensures appropriate controls are in place, and supports audit, investigation, and incident response activities by enabling secure access to required systems and data while maintaining confidentiality.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning:**

- Leads the formulation and implementation of the vision strategy, and roadmap for transforming ICT solutions, operations, and service delivery to achieve the organization’s goals, fostering digital transformation and prioritizing IMO initiatives.
- Drives the design and execution of a comprehensive digital modernization roadmap, embedding innovation, interoperability, and resilience into ICT operations.
- Leads the development and enforcement of data governance frameworks, including data quality standards, analytics capabilities, and business intelligence tools that support informed decision-making.
- Leads the digital enablement and operational alignment of ERP/SAP systems with IMO’s core processes, ensuring enterprise-wide integration, data coherence, and improved resource planning through modern ICT platforms.
- Acts as champion for emerging technologies that advances organisational agility and effectiveness, providing direction for innovation, awareness, and adoption of new digital tools and IT-enabled work practices that fosters and contributes to a continuous change management environment.
- Translates strategic and complex requirements of stakeholders and clients, into innovative, scalable, value driven ICT plans and solutions.
- Facilitates organization-wide alignment on the ICT and data strategy, related investment decisions, and ICT and security risk management based on strategic and data-driven insight.
- Establishes enterprise standards and metrics to measure, guide and communicate contribution of ICT and data services to optimizing internal operations and implementing secretariat mandates.
- Standardizes and modernizes approaches for the secure, continuous integration and continuous deployment of systems led and managed by the secretariat.

**Leadership:**

- Leads the ICTS section fostering a purpose-driven, client-oriented, and inclusive team culture that values excellence, innovation, and accountability to stakeholders and partners.
- Drives an inclusive, innovative, enabling and collaborative culture, that encourages diversity, job satisfaction, technical development, and individual well-being of the ICT section.
- Guides the organisation’s digital maturity and adoption planning through advocacy for continuous transformative solutions and change management.
- Ensure development, oversight and adherence to service delivery metrics, ensuring that large-scale transformational projects are delivered within established time, cost, and quality parameters.
- Acts as a visible and inspiring leader, promoting agile and client-focused system development and service delivery.
- Actively participates in, leads, or co-leads UN forums and clusters to advance the broader UN mandate and demonstrate effective IMO leadership in information and technology.

**Management:**

- Oversees the planning, resourcing and monitoring of annual work plan of activities for ICTS, ensuring efficient allocations of human and financial resources and technical expertise.
- Oversees the strategic management, integration, and optimization of the Organization’s enterprise platforms, ensuring their alignment with IMO’s operational needs and interagency standards
- Governance and management of ICT budget and oversees its implementation, ensuring balancing of strategic investment, operational need and financial transparency.
- Manages a complex and dynamic ICT environment, including high volumes of structured data exchanges with internal and external entities, as well as unstructured data related to content management.
- Oversees critical aspects of enterprise architecture and the development of a data services architecture.
- Oversees the enterprise-wide deployment, customization, and lifecycle management of ERP/SAP systems, ensuring their full integration with IMO’s core operational processes, financial management, and HR services.
- Provides strategic oversight to ensure optimal configuration, user adoption, and long-term system sustainability.
- Ensure coordination of the design and delivery requirements of ICT services to support onsite and offsite hybrid workshops, meetings, and conferences.
- Supervises the design and implementation of the Information Security Management Programme.
- Oversees the design and continuous strengthening of risk management and information security frameworks, promoting a risk-aware, compliant, and resilient ICT environment
- Ensures that the organization's business processes are supported by user-friendly, streamlined, and appropriately scaled technology solutions.
- Holds accountability for ICT’s IT systems, communication networks, and technologies, ensuring they are cost-effectively harmonized across the organization. In this regard, actively engages with other UN organizations to strive for system-wide coherence.

**Representation and Partnerships**

- Represents the secretariat in information technology at the international level and with its internal and external clients.
- Serves as a strategic and technical resource for Secretariat leadership in ICT-related intergovernmental processes
- Builds and nurtures partnerships with external entities, UN Agencies, and donor and government officials to exchange innovative approaches, best practices and service delivery metrics.
- Supports institutional efforts to build and develop integrated partnerships aligned with organisational goals and resource mobilisation strategies.

**Performs other job-related activities required to support the goals and objectives of the Secretariat.**

**Required Competencies**

1. Strategic leadership in ICT strategy, governance, and service delivery.
Expertise in hybrid infrastructure, enterprise systems, and cloud platforms (especially Microsoft Azure and M365).
2. In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity, data protection, and ISO frameworks (e.g., 27001, 27701, 20000, 9001).
3. Strong budget and procurement planning skills, including cost optimization and vendor management.
4. Proven ability to lead digital transformation projects, implement AI and automation tools, and improve service efficiency.
5. Excellent communication and stakeholder management across technical and non-technical audiences.
6. Strong organizational, planning, and risk management skills.
7. Ability to lead high-performing and diverse teams in a multicultural environment.
Commitment to continuous learning, innovation, and client satisfaction.

**Professional Experience**

A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in ICT management, including infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, or enterprise application delivery.

At least 5 years of experience in a strategic leadership role managing ICT operations or teams.

Demonstrated experience leading major digital transformation or modernization projects.

Proven experience with hybrid cloud management (Azure), cybersecurity governance, and ISO implementation.

Experience in budget planning, procurement, and ICT governance frameworks.

Experience in UN system or intergovernmental organizations is desirable.

Experience in inter-agency collaboration or participation in UN/IGO digital governance initiatives is desirable.

**Education**

A Master's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field is essential. A first level or university degree (Bachelor’s or equivalent) in these fields, combined with four additional years of qualifying professional experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree.

Relevant technical or management certifications would be an asset.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (oral and written) is essential. Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.

**Other Skills**

Advanced skills in Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Intune, Power Platform, and enterprise systems.
Strong understanding of IT service management (ITIL), information security (ISO 27001, 27701), and project management (PRINCE2, PMP).

Experience with procurement systems (e.g SAP) , budgeting tools, and data analytics platforms (e.g., Power BI).

Familiarity with ServiceNow, GitHub, automation tools, and digital workplace solutions.

Provide secretariat support to the Facilitation Committee (FAL), the Expert Group on Data Harmonization (EGDH), and other related subsidiary bodies and working groups, as required including the preparation of briefs, notes, documents and reports, and the development and review of manuals, guidance and other publications.

A minimum of five years of progressively responsible professional experience in maritime transport, shipping, port management, data management, maritime facilitation or related fields is essential.

**Education**

University degree or equivalent in Maritime Transport, Shipping and Port Management, Logistics International Trade or data management.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (written and oral). Working knowledge of other official language/s of the UN, will be an advantage.

**Other Skills**

Relevant professional experience in the maritime and port sector is essential. Advanced skills in MS Office applications. Thorough knowledge of relevant international conventions and other IMO instruments. Proven ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary and multi-national management team.

Under the immediate supervision of the Director, Administrative Division, the incumbent leads and provides direction to the Office of Central Support Services which provides the following services to the Secretariat: information, communication and technology services, facilities management, procurement, asset management, publishing, catering, travel, diplomatic, and registry/mailroom and distribution.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities**

1. Plan, oversee and provide direction to the management of Central Support Services (CSS), including facilities management, procurement, asset management, publishing, catering, travel, diplomatic, UNLP and registry/mailroom and distribution.
2. Oversee and supervise the budget and financial management of expenses within CSS’s remit (Regular Budget, Headquarters Capital Fund, Trading Fund), including the approval of variable works requested by contractor under the total facilities management contract.
3. Develop and maintains up-to-date policies and procedures for CSS services.
4. Provide strategic, policy and budgetary advice to senior management on all CSS matters.
5. Recommend purchases of equipment and services aligned to CSS objectives.
6. Serve as Country Security Focal Point for the United Kingdom within the framework of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS).
7. Serve as the certifying officer for the request for the issuance of UNLP and documents related to diplomatic car and duty free goods privileges.
8. Serve as the focal point for the Organization for the United Nations Organizational Resilience Management System (ORMS).
9. Perform any other duties as may be requested.

Within delegated authority, the Chief, CSS, is responsible for the following:

**Facilities Management Services (FMS)**

- Oversee the organization’s FM activities and financial management of budget and expenses, including the approval of variable works requested by the contractor and reviewed by the Facilities Manager.
- Comply with the Organization’s obligations as a tenant: long-term planning of major works, in collaboration with Landlord (host Government) and appointed Managing Agent; protect the Organization’s interests on building-related matters and payment of rent and rates.
- Preventive and reactive maintenance of plant and equipment in the IMO HQ, ensuring the smooth running of all systems to provide a safe and healthy environment.
- Ensure security for IMO HQ, including liaison with the Parliamentary and Diplomatic Protection group of the Metropolitan Police.
- Provision of office cleaning and porterage services, building and motor vehicle insurance, utilities, waste removal/recycling services.
- Manage the relationship with tenants, including calculation of rent and service charges.
- Compile reports on the Secretariat’s greenhouse gas emissions for UN Environment’s Sustainable UN programme; work towards reducing the Secretariat’s carbon footprint.

Information, Communication and Technology Services (ICTS)

- Oversee the organization’s ICTS activities, including budget planning, financial management and budgetary and expense performance, and budget transfers.
- Review and approve or clear staff related matters: recruitment; overtime; extension of appointment; performance management, including functions, roles and responsibilities, if necessary.
- Review ICT related project proposals submitted by Head, ICTS for the approval by the Director, Administrative Division.
- Provide strategic leadership and organizational oversight of IMO’s ICT function,
- Represent IMO as member of the Management Committee of the International Computing Centre.

Procurement and Asset Management Services (PAMS)

- Oversee and manage the Organization’s procurement activities.
- Plan and manage procurement of all goods and services for the Organization, including for field offices and projects implemented on behalf of World Bank, EU and other donors, ensuring good value for money.
- Negotiate and conclude contracts for goods and services procured by the Organization; contracts management including monitoring and review of performance.
- Prepare recommendations to Committee on Contracts for high-value contracts.
- Provide advice and support to senior management and requisitioning officers on procurement policies and procedures.
- Compile reports on procurement statistics for UN Procurement Network.
- Review and update the Procurement Manual.
- Asset management, including gifts to the Organization.
- Oversee and manage the registry and general service functions for the Secretariat.
- Oversee the processing of Host Government-related entitlements and privileges.
- Ensure effective operation of office services, equipment and stores.
- Ensure effective operation of mail room, registry and pouch services.

Publishing Services (PUBS)

- Oversee and manage publishing services (funded by the Trading Fund) Monitor, review and update policies and strategies related to production (including digital production) and sales.
- Provide advice and support to the Secretariat (including senior management) on publishing policies and practice. Manage the publishing element of the Trading Fund budget, including revenue forecasting and long-range expenditure planning.

Catering Services (CATS)

- Oversee and manage the Organization’s in-house catering activities (funded by a Trading Fund).
- Manage the catering element of the Trading Fund budget, including revenue forecasting and long-range expenditure planning.

Travel and Diplomatic Services (TDS)

- Oversee and manage travel and diplomatic services for the Secretariat.
- Coordinate the provision of all official travel (including mission travel, entitlement travel, recruitment and repatriation travel, consultants’ travel.
- Liaison with and performance monitoring of travel agency.
- Review and update the Travel Manual, travel policies and administrative procedures against industry standards and best practices as adopted by Other UN agencies.
- Compile statistical reports on Secretariat travel.
- Oversee the administration for the issuance of UNLPs.

**Required Competencies**

1. Ability to negotiate and influence effectively to build consensus and achieve objectives.
2. Ability to formulate and implement strategic plans and objectives, and make decisions with a focus on impact on the Organization.
3. Excellent spoken, written and presentation skills, and ability to provide guidance and explain complex issues and positions to a variety of audiences.
4. Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, at all levels including in an international, cross-cultural context.
5. Strong leadership skills and experience in managing a diverse team of staff and budgetary resources.
6. Proven analytical and organizational skills with the ability to focus on outcomes and thorough implementation of activities.

**Professional Experience**

At least 15 years of responsible experience in the management of multi-disciplinary teams, including a minimum of 5 years’ experience at a senior or international level position, with line management capacity is essential. Experience in contract and financial management is essential.

**Education**

Advanced university degree in Business/ Public Administration, Management or other relevant fields is essential.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (oral and written) is essential. Knowledge of another official language of the Organization would be an asset.

**Other Skills**

Demonstrated experience in managing several support service functions is essential. Proficiency in MS Office applications. Working knowledge in an ERP (e.g. SAP) will be an asset

6. Lead the investigation function, which examines cases of alleged fraud, misconduct, prohibited conduct, unsatisfactory conduct or other violations of the regulations, rules and policies, while ensuring that investigations and inquiries are conducted in a professional and timely manner and the due processes and procedures are followed in line with the established policies and practices.
7. Direct the preparation of high-quality reports and recommendations on audits, inspections, evaluations as well as investigations performed, monitor the actions taken on recommendations, and review and report on the adequacy and effectiveness of implementation.
8. Provide expert guidance to the Organization and its staff on ethical behaviours, code of ethics, standards of conduct, and conflicts of interest. Reinforce and promote the standards of integrity called for under the Standards of Conduct of the International Civil Service Commission.
9. Handle and address with the highest level of confidentiality all reported cases of misconduct, including initial screening and referral for early resolution, whenever feasible, and coordination of the matter with respect to Investigation. Ensure thorough and seamless end-to-end processes in accordance with staff regulations and staff rules and all relevant issuances.
10. Manage and administer the relevant sections of staff regulations and staff rules on investigation, misconduct and fraud, protection from retaliation policy and procedures, financial disclosure programme, code of ethics including conflicts of interest, outside activities, policy on gifts and all relevant policies.
11. Manage the human resources assigned to the Office in an effective and efficient manner, including fostering a positive work environment, the management and development of staff performance and ensuring completion of the work programme to highest professional standards and its timely delivery.
12. Programme and monitor financial resources, business and work plans. Report on budget/programme performance and prepare inputs for business planning and results-based budgeting in internal oversight and ethics activities.
13. Liaise and coordinate the response as the corporate focal point for the Joint Inspection Unit (JIU). Conducts analysis, prepare and provide coordinated responses to JIU, reports and comments on the status of implementation by IMO of all recommendations issued. Assess organizational risk of non-compliance with various frameworks and make recommendations on remedial actions.
14. Develop and implement standards, training and other awareness-raising initiatives for internal audit, evaluation, investigation and ethics, contributing to enhance effectiveness of oversight and ethics functions, standards and expected behaviours of staff.
15. Keep abreast of all trends, challenges and developments in the areas of internal audit, investigations, evaluations, and ethics. Collaborate and coordinate with internal Divisions and offices and other UN agencies and bodies as appropriate.
16. Prepare reports, documents and briefs to the IMO Council and Assembly.
17. Perform any other task, representation and work as required and as assigned by the Secretary-General.

**Required Competencies**

1. Strategic vision and make decisions with a focus on impact on the Organization.
2. Strong leadership skills and experience in managing a team of staff in diverse disciplines and budgetary resources.
3. Takes ownership and accountability with a focus on outcome and thorough implementation of tasks.
4. Demonstrates sound judgement and analysis of situation and a solution- oriented approach.
5. Excellent planning skills and a high level of efficiency together with the ability to work under pressure and manage conflicting priorities to deliver high-quality outputs within prescribed time and costs.
6. Aptitude to integrate a gender perspective into tasks and activities.
7. Experience in analysing and handling, with tact and due professional care, sensitive and complex issues, maintaining the highest level of confidentiality.
8. Excellent spoken, written and presentation skills, and ability to provide guidance and explain complex issues and positions clearly to a variety of audiences.
9. Excellent diplomatic skills including ability to work in a multicultural environment and to establish and maintain effective relationships, strategic networks and partnerships.

**Professional Experience**

Minimum 15 years of progressively responsible professional experience, including five years within a senior management position in an oversight or ethics function.

Experience in the development, management or implementation of oversight or ethics programmes, and management of human and financial resources is essential.

Experience at senior levels of the United Nations, government service and/or the maritime sector would be an asset.

**Education**

Advanced university degree from an accredited institution in a job related field such as business administration, public administration, social science, or law is essential.

Professional certification in audit, investigation, or ethics from an officially recognized professional body (e.g. CIA, CPA, CA, CFE, CISA or similar) is essential.

**Language Skills**

Proficiency in English (both written and oral), with excellent report writing skills is essential. Working knowledge of other official language(s) of the United Nations would be an asset.

**Other Skills**

Proven expertise in providing authoritative advice to chief executives and senior teams is essential.

In-depth knowledge and practical experience of auditing and/or evaluation standards, methodologies and practices, provision of ethics advice is essential.

Experience in fraud examinations and investigations would be an asset.

Proficiency in MS Office applications is essential and familiarity with an ERP system, ideally SAP would be an asset.

Experience with audit management tools (e.g. TeamMate) would be an asset.

jobs.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

The Europe and Asia Entity at DCAF works across Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus, Central Asia and other parts of Europe and Asia, providing policy advice, capacity-building, technical assistance and support to institutional reforms. Its work covers areas such as democratic oversight, accountability, integrity and anti-corruption, human rights, defence and security governance, and institutional resilience, working closely with governments, parliaments, security institutions, civil society and international partners.

For our country office in Kyiv, Ukraine, we are looking for a highly-motivated and dynamic individual to be our next:

**Project Officer (Europe and Asia)**

**Location: Kyiv, Ukraine**

**Starting date: As soon as possible**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: 2-year fixed-term contract \***

**The role**

The Project Officer provides essential operational and programme-delivery capacity for DCAF’s Ukraine programme, supporting the implementation of thematic activities under the substantive guidance of the respective National Advisor. The position supports the planning, organisation, implementation and follow-up of project activities and maintains regular day-to-day coordination with Ukrainian partners, experts and other stakeholders.

The Project Officer helps translate programme priorities into concrete activities and deliverables, ensuring that implementation remains timely, well organised and responsive to partner needs and changing circumstances in Ukraine. Key responsibilities include coordinating activities and meetings, preparing substantive and operational documentation, supporting expert mobilisation, monitoring activity-level results and contributing to programme reporting and development.

Within the team structure, the Project Officer provides operational support to the respective National Advisor, creating a clear division of responsibilities between substantive and implementation functions. The National Advisor provides thematic leadership, expert guidance and strategic engagement, while the Project Officer supports practical implementation, coordination, monitoring and follow-up. The position also works closely with the Head of Country Office, Resource Manager, other project colleagues and relevant Geneva-based teams to ensure coherent and efficient programme delivery. The position reports to National Advisor.

**Key areas of operation**

• Plan, organise and coordinate project activities in close consultation with the relevant National Advisor and Ukrainian partners, ensuring timely and effective delivery.
• Coordinate day-to-day engagement with beneficiary institutions, experts, civil society organisations and other stakeholders involved in project activities.
• Prepare substantive and operational documents, including meeting materials, activity plans, agendas, briefing notes and follow-up documentation.
• Monitor implementation of activities and agreed deliverables, track activity-level results and identify emerging issues requiring follow-up or corrective action.
• Support expert mobilisation, missions, workshops, consultations and other programme events, ensuring effective logistical and substantive coordination.
• Contribute to programme reporting, documentation and development, providing relevant inputs on implementation progress, results, challenges and partner feedback.

**Your experience**

• 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience in project or programme implementation, international cooperation, governance, security sector reform, human rights or a related field.
• Professional proficiency in Ukrainian and English, with the ability to communicate effectively with Ukrainian partners, experts and international colleagues.
• Demonstrated experience in project coordination and implementation, including organising activities, coordinating stakeholders, preparing documentation and following up on deliverables.
• Experience working with government institutions, international organisations, civil society and/or development partners, preferably in a complex or rapidly evolving environment.
• Strong organisational, communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities and deadlines, work independently and support effective delivery across different stakeholders.
• Ukrainian citizenship at the time of application is a prerequisite.

**We offer**

• a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience

• the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people

• the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

• the position is offered on the basis of an official employment contract, with all applicable taxes and statutory social security contributions paid by the employer in accordance with Ukrainian legislation.

• the expected net monthly salary (after applicable taxes and employee social security contributions) is EUR 1,600–1,800, depending on qualifications and relevant experience.

*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.*

**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Head of Support Services

Location : Remote

Job Type: Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Head of Support Services provides strategic leadership and oversight of INARA’s global finance and operational support systems across all country operations and legal entities. The role ensures strong financial management, compliance, internal controls, budgeting coherence, donor financial accountability, and organizational financial sustainability.

The post-holder serves as the central finance oversight function between Headquarters and Country Offices, ensuring that financial systems, reporting processes, fund management, and accounting practices operate in alignment with donor requirements, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory frameworks.

The role also supervises finance staff across country operations, supports organizational audits and compliance obligations, oversees financial systems optimization, and strengthens institutional financial management capacity across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

Key responsibilities include and may not be limited to:

1. **Financial Planning and Budget Oversight**

The Head of Support Services leads organizational budgeting processes and ensures financial planning aligns with operational realities and strategic priorities.

Tasks:

- Review and consolidate annual organizational budgets and donor project budgets from all country operations
- Ensure consistency between programmatic plans, operational priorities, and financial forecasts
- Validate budget assumptions including exchange rates, inflation projections, staffing costs, and operational estimates
- Review cost allocations across grants, shared costs, and general organizational operations
- Support Country Offices and program teams in developing realistic and compliant donor budgets
- Ensure budget structures align with donor regulations and internal financial controls
- Monitor overall organizational financial sustainability and resource allocation

Key Competencies:

- Strong financial planning and budgeting expertise
- Advanced analytical and forecasting skills
- Understanding of donor budgeting requirements
- Strategic financial oversight capacity

1. **Fund Management and Financial Oversight**

The role oversees organizational fund management processes and ensures financial liquidity and accountability across all operations.

Tasks:

- Oversee inter-office fund transfers and HQ financial allocations
- Review and approve fund requests from Country Offices
- Monitor cash flow, liquidity, and financial reserve levels
- Monitor foreign exchange exposure and associated financial risks
- Ensure donor funds are utilized in accordance with approved budgets and restrictions
- Track organizational spending thresholds and authorization compliance
- Support the CEO on high-level financial decision-making and risk management

Key Competencies:

- Strong treasury and cash-flow management skills
- Financial risk management expertise
- Understanding of multi-country fund management
- Strong attention to accountability and financial control

1. **Expenditure Management and Internal Controls**

The Head of Support Services ensures organizational expenditures comply with internal policies, donor regulations, and approval frameworks.

Tasks:

- Review expenditures above approved authorization thresholds and submit to the CEO for final approval where required
- Review complex procurement packages including competitive bidding documentation and vendor justifications
- Ensure expenditures comply with donor restrictions and organizational policies
- Monitor implementation of internal control procedures across all country operations
- Identify and address financial control weaknesses and operational risks
- Ensure procurement and expenditure documentation is audit-ready and properly archived

Key Competencies:

- Strong internal control and compliance knowledge
- Procurement and donor compliance understanding
- Risk identification and mitigation skills
- Attention to detail and accountability

1. **Accounting, Reconciliation, and Financial Systems Oversight**

The role ensures the accuracy, integrity, and efficiency of organizational accounting systems and financial records.

Tasks:

- Oversee organizational accounting and bookkeeping processes across all country operations
- Ensure financial entries, reconciliations, and classifications are accurate and completed on time
- Review month-end and year-end closing processes
- Conduct periodic spot checks of financial records and supporting documentation
- Ensure bank reconciliations and petty cash reconciliations are completed accurately and on schedule
- Supervise organizational use of QuickBooks Online (QBO)
- Coordinate with system consultants on QBO structure optimization and reporting systems
- Maintain oversight of chart of accounts, donor classes, and financial coding structures

Key Competencies:

- Advanced accounting and bookkeeping knowledge
- Strong financial systems management skills
- QBO proficiency and oversight experience
- Strong reconciliation and audit trail management skills

1. **Financial Reporting and Donor Compliance**

The role oversees organizational financial reporting processes and ensures compliance with donor and regulatory requirements.

Tasks:

- Consolidate financial data from all country operations into organizational financial reports
- Review and validate donor financial reports prior to submission to the CEO and donors
- Ensure financial reports meet donor formatting, compliance, and deadline requirements
- Review budget versus actual (BvA) reports and variance explanations
- Provide structured feedback to Country Offices on reporting quality and compliance gaps
- Ensure consistency between programmatic implementation and financial reporting
- Support donor financial reviews and due diligence processes

Key Competencies:

- Strong donor financial reporting expertise
- Financial analysis and variance interpretation skills
- Understanding of humanitarian donor compliance frameworks
- Strong organizational and coordination skills

1. **Audit, Compliance, and Organizational Risk Management**

The Head of Support Services leads financial compliance and audit coordination processes across all INARA operations.

Tasks:

- Maintain and update financial policies, SOPs, and internal control frameworks
- Coordinate external audits including donor audits, IRS filings, and independent organizational audits
- Ensure implementation and follow-up of audit recommendations
- Oversee submission of IRS Form 990 and other compliance-related financial filings
- Support compliance across INARA’s legal entities and jurisdictions
- Identify organizational financial risks and recommend mitigation measures
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, anti-fraud standards, and applicable legal requirements

Key Competencies:

- Strong audit and compliance management experience
- Knowledge of nonprofit regulatory frameworks
- Risk management and governance expertise
- Strong policy development and implementation skills

1. **Systems Strengthening and Capacity Building**

The role strengthens organizational financial systems and supports finance staff development across all operations.

Tasks:

- Supervise and support Country Finance Leads and finance staff across all country operations
- Conduct finance staff performance evaluations and capacity development planning
- Organize training workshops and refresher sessions on financial procedures and systems
- Identify inefficiencies within financial systems and recommend improvements
- Support automation and financial process optimization initiatives
- Strengthen organizational financial documentation and reporting systems
- Promote standardization of financial practices across all country operations

Key Competencies:

- Leadership and staff management skills
- Capacity building and mentoring experience
- Systems improvement and problem-solving skills
- Strong coordination and communication abilities

**Key working relationships**

- CEO: Primary line manager and final financial approval authority
- Country Directors: Coordination on budgets, expenditures, and operational finance oversight
- Country Finance Leads: Technical supervision and financial management oversight
- Partnerships & Development Department: Coordination on proposal budgets and donor financial reporting
- Program Teams: Budget planning and financial monitoring support
- Auditors and External Consultants: Compliance, audit, and systems coordination
- SMT: Strategic financial planning and organizational decision-making

**THE POST-HOLDER WILL BE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE MEASURABLE PROGRESS AGAINST THE FOLLOWING WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS:**

The post-holder will be expected to demonstrate measurable progress against the following within the first six MONTHS:

- Reporting validation process fully established and adhered to across all active country operations
- Zero reports submitted to Partnerships & Development without completed quality review
- SMT action tracker operational and actively maintained, with no overdue items going unescalated
- Entity documentation archive created and populated for all INARA legal entities
- Coordination gaps between Country Offices, Finance, and Partnerships & Development visibly reduced
- Positive feedback from Country Directors, Finance, and the CEO on coordination quality and turnaround times

**Requirements & Qualifications**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field
- Professional accounting qualification preferred

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressive finance and operational management experience
- Experience in humanitarian or nonprofit sector finance management
- Experience managing multi-country financial operations
- Strong knowledge of donor compliance and nonprofit financial systems
- Experience with QuickBooks Online and financial reporting systems

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Advisor
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we’d like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action. Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home.

The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Job Overview:**

IRC’s Global Crisis Analysis, Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security, and Preparedness teams have come together to form ‘ASAP’ (Analysis, Security, Access and Preparedness) to strengthen global and regional support to IRC teams to deliver in the most complex, volatile and high-risk operating environments to reach the worst-affected and least-served people in need. Housed within the IRC’s Emergency Unit, but supporting countries and emergencies responses across IRC’s footprint, the Advisor allies with country and emergency response leadership, ASAP colleagues, and Regional Safety and Security Directors, to provide strategic, technical and operational support to enable IRC to open, expand, and sustain programs in emergencies, major crises, and complex environments – to reach the worst-affected and least-served populations.

The Advisor will work alongside the Director, and the Emergency Response Team Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Coordinator, to split responsibilities by country portfolio and/or thematic demands and/or level of complexity based on their respective scope of work and experience. The role brings additional capacity, and challenges and supports teams to meet IRC’s mandate through effective analysis and scenario planning to inform program and operational ambitions, and support to deliver on these with enhanced humanitarian access and security management.

The International Rescue Committee’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads IRC’s global emergency preparedness and response to sudden-onset crises, complex emergencies, and high-risk contexts. EmU strengthens IRC’s ability to operate safely and effectively in volatile environments through surge capacity, systems development, and expert technical leadership.

***Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either Kenya, UK or Geneva. Candidates from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply as well and will be hosted in that country.*

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Humanitarian access management**

- Plan and deliver inclusive in-person and remote scenario development workshops as part of wider ASAP support to frontline program teams responding to major crises, linking those scenarios relevant strategies to support the IRC to serve the worst-affected and least-served populations despite conflict, volatility and risk.
- Support frontline program teams to develop and track indicators for tracking crisis developments in support countries, where requested as part of wider support, and actively contribute to information sharing with IRC colleagues about key crisis developments in support countries.
- Support country leadership to develop and implement specific access and acceptance strategies, in support of the Country Director/Emergency Team Leader, ASAP and/or RSSDs to enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access to reach target populations, in line with IRC policy and international humanitarian law – these may include a wide range of access approaches including broader risk management and remote management.
- Ensure strategies include how IRC builds relationships, engages and negotiates with authorities, key power brokers, security actors, and community stakeholders, including with state and non‑state actors, to ensure IRC’s mission and activities are understood and accepted, and that staff and programs can operate safely and without disruption.
- Build and maintain an active network of humanitarian access and security staff internally and across organisations.
- Maintain currency with methods, approaches and professional developments in relevant topics, and represent IRC in relevant global fora where needed.

**Safety and security management**

- Support country leadership and access, safety and security teams to identify, analyze and mitigate safety and security (S&S) risks across emergency responses, ensuring alignment with IRC Security Minimum Standards (SMS), Duty of Care, GEDI and PEERS principles, and integrate into access, security, preparedness strategies where relevant.
- Support the implementation of S&S standards and approaches to strengthen humanitarian access, and ensure S&S preparedness and contingency align with program ambitions.
- Support country/response teams in incident management, where relevant.

**Emergency preparedness**

- In close collaboration with ASAP and the Director, Emergency Performance and Quality, support country programs to develop and implement humanitarian access, safety and security approaches in their emergency preparedness and contingency plans, streamlining existing strategies and plans where relevant/possible, through in-country or remote mentoring, training and technical support.
- Support EmU in the development and adaptation of humanitarian access, safety and security systems, practices and resources, and centralized knowledge management.

**Learning & Development**

- Co-develop, with consortium partners, a humanitarian access framework that is accessible and used by partners to define access ambitions and strategies.
- Support the development, revision and uptake of IRC’s technical resources for analysis, security, access and preparedness, learning from operational experience, as well as global trends and good practices.
- Guide, train, coach and mentor IRC country leaders and frontline staff on humanitarian access approaches, safety and security, including Security Risk Management (SRM), and partner capacity strengthening, ensuring the inclusion of gender-sensitive approaches that address gender-specific risks.
- Design, deliver and track humanitarian access, safety and security capacity strengthening activities (including training, coaching, peer-to-peer learning) for EmU and priority country teams in access, safety and security training (including READI and humanitarian negotiation) and context analysis and scenario planning – leveraging internal and external resources.
- Ensure an ongoing exchange of learning and good practice in ASAP methods and approaches with partners; and deliver capacity sharing activities on analysis, access and security where relevant and prioritized.
