Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Sri Lanka is a key partner in driving sustainable development, tackling economic, social, and environmental challenges in Sri Lanka. Through its Country Programme (2023–2027), UNDP focuses on strategic, integrated solutions that align with national priorities and strengthen resilience in a changing socio-economic landscape. The Country Office enhances its advisory and programmatic functions by providing technical expertise, policy support, efficient delivery of results and strong implementation oversight. By promoting inclusive economic growth, climate resilience, and governance reforms, UNDP collaborates with government, civil society, and the private sector to develop scalable, localized solutions. With a focus on innovation, strategic partnerships, and efficient programme management, UNDP Sri Lanka ensures impactful, sustainable development, helping the country progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals.

The Front Offices supports the day-to-day functioning and overall coordination led by the Resident Representative and the Deputy Resident Representative and also serves as a close link with the middle management team through the Integrated Management Team (IMT) to ensure effective functioning of the Country Office. It is the front-facing office of the UNDP Country Office.

The Executive Analyst provides comprehensive support to the Resident Representative and the Front Office, undertaking responsibilities to strengthen strategic management, coordination, stakeholder engagement and organizational effectiveness. This role requires exceptional organizational skills, the ability to handle a wide range of administrative tasks, and the capacity to work independently with minimal supervision. The Executive Analyst will play a crucial role in facilitating smooth operations and ensuring efficient communication and cross-functional coordination within the Country Office.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Resident Representative and in close collaboration with the Deputy Resident Representative, the incumbent will perform the duties and responsibilities below.

1- Strategic planning, country office coordination and management follow-up.

- Support country office planning processes, including annual business planning, and management reporting, in close cooperation with Results and Resources Management Team (RRMT) and Integrated Management Team (IMT) as required.

- Coordinate all staff and Integrated Management Meetings (IMM), other meetings, leadership retreats, forums and strategic discussions, including agenda development, background documentation, minutes and follow-up actions.

- Monitor implementation of senior management and IMM decisions and country office commitments in close collaboration with the RRMT, ensuring timely escalation, follow-up and reporting.

- Coordinate cross-office initiatives and facilitate collaboration across programme, operations, communications, partnership and project teams on priority corporate and strategic matters.

2- Strategic executive coordination and Front Office support.

- Coordinate the day-to-day functioning of the Front Office, ensuring efficient information flow, prioritization of requests, timely follow-up and effective support to the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative.

- Manage schedules, correspondence, protocol arrangements, official visits, travel planning and high-level meetings, ensuring that materials and logistical arrangements for the RR and DRR are prepared in a timely manner.

- Backstop other members of the Front Office, when required in preparing materials and following up on required actions.

- Maintain organized records, files and working documents for the Front Office, ensuring confidentiality, accessibility and institutional memory.

3- Analytical, briefing and knowledge management support.

- Prepare briefing notes, talking points, speeches, presentations, meeting dossiers, background papers and strategic analyses for the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative in close coordination with programme and partnership teams.

- Review, synthesize and quality assure key documents, briefs, presentations and reports to ensure accuracy, coherence and readiness for senior management use.

- Collect, organize and analyse programme, financial, partnership, risk and operational information to support evidence-based management decisions.

- Undertake substantive ad hoc assignments, research and data analysis under the guidance of the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative.

4- Partnerships, stakeholder engagement and high-level missions.

- In close coordination with the Partnership team, coordinate and support high-level missions, including mission programmes, stakeholder mapping, logistical coordination, briefing packages, mission notes and follow-up on outcomes and action points.

- Maintain stakeholder management systems and track commitments, correspondence, mission outcomes and strategic engagements with government counterparts, development partners, UN Country Team and other stakeholders.

5- Communications, correspondence and knowledge products.

- Coordinate with the Communications Team drafting, review and coordination of sensitive correspondence, official communications, management messages and responses for internal and external audiences initiated by the Resident Representative.

- Compile and provide inputs to Country Office publications, newsletters, profiles and other knowledge products, including liaison with contributors, authors, designers and relevant teams, where relevant.

- Provide quality assurance for management responses to Regional Bureau inquiries and decisions, in close coordination with relevant units and the appropriate country office counterparts, to enable Resident Representative clearance and final sign-off.

6- Office effectiveness, information management and operational support.

- Provide information to internal and external parties as appropriate, maintaining effective communication channels and working relationships across the Country Office, UNCT and key partner networks.

- Organize documentation, printing, distribution and other operational requirements for Front Office meetings, events, publications and activities.

- Support development of templates, standard operating procedures and guidance notes for the office effectiveness and communications, in line with UNDP corporate standards and Country Office best practices.

The Executive Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Resident Representative and collaborates closely with the Deputy Resident Representative and country office teams.

The Programme Associate supports the planning, organization, and implementation of programme activities in accordance with project documents, work plans and UNDP rules and regulations. The role ensures timely and efficient administration of programme activities, coordination of projects and support to programme staff in a variety of operational and programme support tasks.

The Programme Associate works in close collaboration with other staff and personnel within the team, Operations, and projects’ staff in the Country Office, Regional Hub and UNDP HQ, and UN Agencies to exchange information and resolve complex programme support-related issues. The Programme Associate is also expected to work closely with external partners, including key government and CSO counterparts, donors, and other partners.

Support Programme Formulation, Pipeline Management and Resource Planning

- Provide inputs for the preparation and review of project documents, annual work plans, budgets, proposals, and other programme-related documentation, including information on implementation arrangements.

- Draft and provide input for the development of briefing notes, concept notes, proposals, and other documents related to pipeline development and resource mobilization.

- Ensure effective pipeline management by facilitating and maintaining up-to-date information on prospective projects, funding opportunities, resource requirements, and project development status.

- Support preparation and monitoring of DPC/DES cost recovery projections and related information for projects.

- Provide relevant programme, financial and implementation information to support decision-making, identify implementation arrangements and address potential bottlenecks during project formulation and implementation.

Provide effective support to Programme and Project Implementation, Resource Management and Oversight

- Create projects in the ERP system and support budget revisions, project status changes, determination of unutilized funds, and operational and financial closure of projects.

- Provide day-to-day guidance to implementing and responsible partners and project teams on programme implementation, financial management and applicable UNDP rules and procedures, and monitor the utilization of financial resources.

- Ensure monitoring and follow up of corporate dashboards and other programme and project performance requirements, including tracking indicators, targets, milestones and success criteria, and maintaining accurate programme data.

- Support the preparation of programme, project and donor reports and other reporting requirements, ensuring accuracy and compliance with applicable donor guidelines and UNDP rules and regulations.

Reporting, Compliance, Quality Assurance and Records Management

- Identify programme and project implementation bottlenecks, coordinate follow-up with relevant stakeholders, and propose practical solutions to facilitate timely implementation.

- Provide effective oversight of specific funding requirements, including Vertical Funds, Funding Windows, European Union, joint programmes and other third-party cost sharing donors in line with UNDP POPP and applicable donor requirements.

- Organize oversight and monitoring processes for the implementation of HACT requirements, including follow-up on HACT assessments, micro-assessments, assurance activities and related financial management actions, and provide guidance to implementing partners on compliance with HACT requirements.

- Ensure internal and external programme/project audits through preparation and review of supporting documentation, follow-up on audit queries, and monitoring of audit recommendations.

- Provide administrative and quality assurance support to the Programme Unit, including review of technical reports and payment requests, maintenance of expenditure records and coordination with relevant units to address issues and ensure timely corrective action.

- Maintain accurate programme and project records, databases and filing systems to support effective implementation, monitoring and reporting.

Support implementation of the CO partnership and resource mobilization strategies

- Contribute to the implementation of the Country Office partnership and resource mobilization strategies by providing relevant analysis and information on donors, funding opportunities and partnership prospects.

- Prepare and maintain up-to-date donor profiles and the unit’s resource mobilization pipeline, including tracking prospective and confirmed funding opportunities.

- Track and report on mobilized resources and support the review of contribution agreements and management of contributions in the ERP system.

Facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing

- Organize and deliver programme related training for relevant programme/project and operations personnel in assigned programme area.

- Compile lessons learned and best practices.

- Provide contributions to knowledge networks, communities of practice and digital knowledge platforms.

jobs.title: Policy and Economics Officer [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Organizational Context

UNDP has been working in India since 1951 in almost all areas of human development. Together with the Government of India and development partners, we have worked towards eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, strengthening local governance, enhancing community resilience, protecting the environment, supporting policy initiatives and institutional reforms, and accelerating sustainable development for all.

With projects and programmes in every state and union territory in India, UNDP works with national and subnational government, and diverse development actors to deliver people-centric results, particularly for the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. As the integrator for collective action on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the UN system, we are committed to supporting the Government of India’s national development vision and priorities and accelerating the achievement of the SDGs for the people and the planet.

UNDP India’s new Country Programme (2023-2027) builds on our prior work and aims to provide an integrated approach to development solutions in three strategic portfolios:

- Strong, accountable and evidence-led institutions for accelerated achievement of the SDGs.

- Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized.

- Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability.

South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture.

You are invited to join a team of future-smart development professionals to support India in achieving the national and globally agreed goals. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with diverse stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to sustainable development and reach those furthest behind first.

Office / Unit/ Project Description

The Policy Unit leads UNDP India’s research and advocacy on Global Goals and the national development agenda, with a special focus on environment and climate change, skill development, inclusive growth and strengthening systems for SDG localization.

Scope of Work

Main Purpose:

The position will support the Senior Economist and the Policy Unit in advancing UNDP India’s strategic priorities through the formulation and implementation of integrated policy initiatives and programmes. It will contribute to strengthening linkages between policy and programme priorities, supporting partnerships and resource mobilization, and promoting knowledge and evidence to inform UNDP’s development interventions.

Duties and Responsibilities

1- Support the formulation, development, and design of new integrated policy initiatives in UNDP priority areas through:

- Preparing substantive inputs to key strategic and policy documents, which direct and guide UNDP interventions on climate change, livelihoods, health, gender, and localization of SDGs.

- Collaborating closely with the country office programme teams and external counterparts to identify new policy ideas in line with the UNDP’s priorities, initiate project concepts; lead the consultations on project formulation;

- Coordinating closely with technical advisors at the UNDP/Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH), governmental and other institutions to ensure an effective formulation process leading to the approval of the projects;

- Ensures a strong relationship between UNDP India’s programmatic work and policy initiatives, with oversight on quality of published policy documents.

2- Provides oversight and management of initiatives in UNDP Policy Unit through:

- Effective application of Result Based Management (RBM) tools in project management; establishment of management targets and monitoring achievement of results;

- Performance of the functions of project manager in Atlas as defined and participation in recruitment processes for projects;

- Proactive financial and substantive monitoring and evaluation of the projects, identification of operational and financial problems, development of solutions; timely escalation of issues and challenges, follow-up on audit and other recommendations;

- Preparation and contribution to the regular reports on outputs and outcomes as required.

3- Engages in partnership building and resource mobilization through:

- Coordination of activities and communications with all relevant stakeholders to build new, and strengthen existing relationships with partners and relevant government counterparts;

- Identification of capacity building and institutional development needs and implementation of appropriate interventions to enhance capacity and skills at the local level for programme/project development and resources mobilization;

- Scanning of funding windows and any other potential sources, preparation of substantive briefs on possible opportunities for project finance and co-finance in particular with a focus on private sector, financial institutions and Government cost-sharing;

- Representing UNDP in relevant meetings and for a when directed by the supervisor;

- Contribution to the UN’s work in India and actively participate in the UNCT Result Groups and fora.

4- Ensures facilitation of knowledge generation and management through:

- Formulating and developing best lessons learnt products and tools;

- Leading the preparation of knowledge products with relevance for UNDP’s policy priorities;

- Identifying, synthesizing and sharing lessons learnt and good practices directly linked to programme country policy goals;

- Identifying sources of information related to policy-driven issues; and quality contribution to knowledge networks regionally and globally to support the provision of quality advisory services and facilitation of knowledge building and management.

5- Supports the Senior Economist (in his/ her capacity as the head of the Policy Unit) in people management, knowledge management, partnership building/ resource mobilization, and any other task as assigned by the supervisor.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Institutional Arrangements:

- Reporting To: Country Economist

- Reporting to this position: - N/A

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Business management

Results- based management

Ability to manage programmes and projects with a strategy aimed at improved performance and demonstrable results

Business Direction & Strategy

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management

Monitoring

Business Management

Business Management

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Partnership management

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Economics , Development Studies, Social Sciences, Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, or related field is required; or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with Master’s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in Economics, Development Studies and Social Sciences.

Required Skills:

- An understanding of India’s development challenges, the federal structure, and key development policy debates is essential

- Proven track record in providing policy advice and technical assistance on Public Policy at mid- or senior management level is required.

- Excellent writing skills/experience with the ability to condense technical reports to simple text for a general audience is required.

- Experience of designing and carrying out data-driven research, an understanding of research methods, and an awareness of the public policy research landscape and its key players is required.

- Strong and proven ability to analyze and visualize data-backed research in easy-to-grasp ways is required.

Desirabel Skills:

- Significant working experience in Government or relevant multilateral institutions is desired

- Experience of leveraging and understanding different data sources, including economic data (both secondary and primary), government reports and surveys, and understanding trends from economic indicators is desired.

- Sound knowledge of UN/UNDP rules and regulations, policies, procedures, and practices. Strong writing skills, including drafting financial policies and processes is desired.

Required Languages:

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

The Economist Network of the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) is one of the region’s most valuable initiatives to enhance policy support and capacity. The Country Economist plays an important role at the country but also regional and global levels in contributing to renewed development momentum in an era of turbulence and uncertainty.

Main Purpose:

The Country Economist works under the direct guidance of the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative in the Country Office India, in close collaboration with programme and operations teams, and has a dotted line to the RBAP Chief Economist.

The Country Economist integrates the activities UNDP delivers in the region and ensures these contribute the greatest development impact possible. S/he makes a difference by being keenly aware of the changing development landscape, embedding a sharp strategic focus on the development interventions that matter the most, and connecting diagnostics and solutions to the politics of change and the art of delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

In this respect, the Country Economist works closely with colleagues of RBAP as well as the Global Policy Network (GPN). S/he develops and maintains a professional network across development partner agencies, government institutions, the private sector, and civil society at the country level.

Summary of key functions:

- Policy support and strategic positioning at the country level particularly in preparation for the country office analysis for CPD and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

- Development of at least four thematic briefs aligned with the new strategic plan.

- Advise and provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management and programme teams to strengthen foresight analytics, systems thinking and portfolio design.

- Provide technical expertise and global best practice to national and sub-national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and (sub-) national development priorities, with regard to sustainable and inclusive economic policies.

- Advocate and engage with partners to support UNDP’s role and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative.

- Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas.

Duties and Responsibilities:

1- Advise and provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management and programme teams to strengthen foresight and portfolio design

- Provide analysis to UNDP Country Office management with the preparation and implementation of country programmes and strategies, including the development of country programme document (CPD) and related analyses.

- Advise and support UNDP Country Office teams to develop and manage relevant thematic portfolios, such as activities to support inclusive growth and progress towards the SDGs and (sub-) national development priorities.

- Lead UNDP Country Office efforts to conceptualize and implement the Development Finance Assessment (DFA) and accompanying process and use existing financial resources more effectively and efficiently to achieve the SDGs.

- Provide analysis, research and foresight in priority thematic areas at the country level, including publication of policy briefs (and state briefs) or other analytical outputs.

- Provide analysis of economic, social and political developments at national and sub-national level.

- Support the preparation of policy briefs, background notes, speeches, talking points, presentation materials, etc., on critical development issues within the SDG framework for senior management at the country and regional levels.

- Lead the development of the National Human Development Report (HDR) at national and sub-national level and ensure that it provides added value in terms of development economic analysis, updated data, and information for policy formulation; Compile data and perform statistical analysis as required to support innovative knowledge work country strategies and activities.

- Collaborate across UNDP teams, especially to ensure linkages to the work emerging from the network of acceleration labs.

- Advise on systems thinking and support the creation of large-scale development solutions to help address complex development challenges.

- Support expansion of Country Office service offers on financing for development, including innovative financing models and country specific/sector specific studies.

2- Provide policy advice and technical expertise to (sub-) national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and (sub-) national development priorities, with regard to sustainable and inclusive economic policies;

- Advise and facilitate dialogue on sustainable development issues with government officials, development partners, civil society, and the private sector, providing and sharing global experience and policy

- Provide the best global practice, policy and programming advice and support for development planning and policy formulation at the national, sub-national, and local levels, including on data for development, systems thinking and foresight exercises. Advise and support the identification and analysis of interventions that can impact multiple development goals and targets at the same time.

- Advise and support monitoring and reporting of progress related to SDGs and other national development frameworks, including to help strengthen national and local level data collection and statistical capacity.

- Guide to leverage UNDP’s regional and global programmes, to provide holistic and effective support to the country.

- Leverage support and expertise from the UNDP’s global/regional Economist networks to strengthen UNDP’s support on economic analysis and policy development for the Government and the UN Country Team.

3- Advocate and engage with partners, including to support UNDP’s role and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Contribute, in close collaboration with senior management, to the development and/or strengthening of partnerships with UN agencies, IFIs, bilateral development agencies, private sector entities, and civil society.

- When delegated, represent the UNDP Country Office in relevant forums, conferences, or workshops, including presenting research or programmatic results.

- Facilitate the Resident Representative in resource mobilization and future growth strategies and contribute to the design of large-scale programme and development solutions.

- Contribute to national, regional, and global knowledge networks and communities of practice.

4- Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas.

- Substantively contribute as possible to UNDP regional knowledge products and development of programming offers in regional priority areas (e.g., inequality, future of work, innovative financing, development strategies, economic governance, political economy).

- Participate actively in the Economist Network of RBAP by attending regional meetings (in-person and/or virtual), sharing relevant experiences, and conducting peer reviews.

- Collaborate and contribute to regional and sub-regional publications, practice notes, and Regional Human Development Reports.

- Stay informed about broader developments, contribute to cross-border and cross-GPN initiatives, and support the economist network through common analyses, frameworks, and templates.

- Enhance UNDP’s understanding and design of new approaches to sustainable development across the region by acting as a regional thematic lead where possible.

jobs.title: Asistente Local de Seguridad OCSA - NPSA5
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

El Departamento de Seguridad Integrada de las Naciones Unidas en Colombia – UNDSS ISW Colombia, se encarga de apoyar a las organizaciones enmarcadas en el Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas (UNSMS – UN Security Management System, por sus siglas en inglés), a través de los servicios brindados, la asesoría y el acompañamiento del personal de la oficina, para facilitarles el desarrollo de las actividades que les permiten cumplir con su mandato. Todo esto, dentro de las medidas de seguridad necesarias que promueven la integridad del personal, los bienes de la organización y la realización de sus programas.

Para cumplir con esta tarea UNDSS ISW Colombia ha venido consolidando una estructura que permita darle una gestión integral a la seguridad a través del fortalecimiento de diferentes áreas, entre ellas, comunicaciones, operaciones, formación, análisis de la Información, así como el relevante suporte administrativo, logístico y financiero para implementación de estas actividades.

En este contexto y buscando dar soporte a las actividades operativas de las oficinas territoriales, el/la Asistente Local de Seguridad, bajo la dirección general del Asesor Jefe de Seguridad y de acuerdo a las líneas de reporte del Concepto de Operaciones de UNDSS ISW Colombia (CONOPS), realizará el seguimiento administrativo a gestiones operacionales relacionadas con adquisiciones, reclutamiento, misiones, sistemas, archivo, servicios generales y seguridad, con el fin de apoyar el correcto funcionamiento de la administración de seguridad, prestando un servicio eficiente y oportuno tanto a las oficinas, como al personal de UNDSS en el nivel de terreno, y a la oficina nacional en Bogotá.

El/la Asistente Local de Seguridad trabaja en estrecha colaboración con personal de todas las áreas del Departamento de Seguridad Integrada de las Naciones Unidas y otras Agencias de Naciones Unidas, intercambiando información y asegurando la prestación de servicios de manera consistente, enfocada en el servicio al cliente interno y externo, y en alcanzar resultados de calidad, en aras de facilitar las labores ejecutadas en el mandato de apoyo a las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Colombia.

El/la Asistente Local de Seguridad proporcionará servicios de seguridad, elaboración de productos, asegurando alta calidad, exactitud bajo la supervisión del Asesora Jefe de Seguridad (CSA) y Asesor Jefe de Seguridad Adjunto (DCSA) y con disponibilidad para viajar, inclusive en áreas aisladas y de difícil acceso y con poco tiempo de aviso y Disponibilidad para trabajar en fines de semana y/o festivos según sea requerido.

Duties and Responsibilities

Las funciones principales que desarrollará el/la Asistente Local de Seguridad se resumen, entre otras, en las siguientes actividades:

1.Asistir al CSA/DCSA en recoger, actualizar y comunicar información pertinente a la situación de seguridad del área de responsabilidad:

- Bajo la autoridad del CSA/DCSA y siguiendo sus indicaciones coordina, con las organizaciones de seguridad y su personal del gobierno anfitrión; incluidas las autoridades militares y policiales a nivel nacional, regional o local, así como aquellas no gubernamentales en el área de responsabilidad.

- Apoyar a la valoración de la situación de seguridad en su destino, asegurando una adecuada recopilación de información de seguridad, su verificación, y el apoyo que pueda ser requerido para su adecuado análisis por el CSA/DCSA.

- Apoya las comunicaciones y valoraciones de seguridad adecuadas a los representantes de las agencias, fondos y programas del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas, de acuerdo con las instrucciones dadas por el CSA/DCSA.

- Mantiene un contacto regular con los Puntos Focales de Seguridad del Sistema de las NNUU, en el desarrollo de sus funciones.

- Proporciona apoyo y asistencia técnica a las reuniones del Equipo de Gestión de la Seguridad (SMT) según le sea requerido por el CSA/DCSA.

2. Asistir en el mantenimiento del Plan de Seguridad, incluida la actualización de las listas del personal.

- Apoya la preparación y revisión del Plan de Seguridad de las NNUU.

- Ayuda en la puesta en práctica de las acciones necesarias para garantizar la ejecución del Plan de Seguridad.

- Desempeña las funciones de Duty Officer de acuerdo con los lineamentos vigentes, verifica y aprueba misiones a Bogota y Cundinamarca, atiende los incidentes de seguridad en Bogota y Cundinamarca a los funcionarios de las Naciones Unidas.

3. Apoya al CSA/DCSA en la elaboración del sistema de Gestión del Riesgo (Security Risk Management – SRM, por su denominación en inglés), incluyendo, pero no limitado a:

- Colabora en la realización de SRMs, análisis de amenazas y evaluaciones de instalaciones

- Realiza evaluaciones de seguridad residencial (RSM) y proporciona consejo sobre las medidas de seguridad residencial de acuerdo con las Políticas de UNSMS

- Establece y mantiene un sistema de Puntos Focales de Seguridad del UNSMS, y mantiene actualizada la información de oficinas de las NNUU y residencias de su personal.

- Administra el sistema de pases y documentos de identificación del personal de las NNUU.

- Mantiene el enlace con las compañías comerciales usadas por el sistema de seguridad de las NNUU (UNSMS), asegurando un uso eficiente y efectivo de los medios y personal de seguridad.

4. Asiste en la elaboración y registro de informes de incidentes de seguridad que afecten al personal de las Naciones Unidas, sus oficinas y bienes; y asiste en la preparación de informes como el Informe de Incidentes de Seguridad, la Evaluación de Seguridad, y el Informe de Incidentes de Seguridad Trimestral.

- Apoyar la recopilación y consolidación de información relacionada con incidentes de seguridad que afecten al personal de las Naciones Unidas, sus oficinas, instalaciones y bienes.

- Mantener organizados y actualizados los archivos y soportes relacionados con los incidentes de seguridad y los informes elaborados.

- Realizar seguimiento a la información pendiente o requerida para completar los registros e informes de seguridad.

5. Proporciona apoyo en la organización y desarrollo de cursos talleres y charlas de seguridad para mantener los conocimientos y preparación de seguridad apropiados, y proporciona orientaciones de seguridad al personal nuevo o recién asignado. Realiza sesiones de información de seguridad, según se necesite.

- En apoyo, participa en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Apoyar otras actividades de desarrollo de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y promuevan la acción.

- Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro de la oficina de país y a nivel regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado.

- Realizar contribuciones significativas a las redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

6. Proporciona asistencia administrativa y logística al CSA/SCSA para la gestión la unidad y el personal de UNDSS ISW Colombia:

- Mantiene un sistema confidencial y actualizado de archivo de correspondencia y documentos de UNDSS ISW Colombia.

- Mantiene una base de datos de contacto con las relaciones del gobierno anfitrión y sus autoridades de seguridad.

- Apoya los aspectos logísticos para la realización de reuniones internas y externas de UNDSS y de aquellos eventos solicitados por la Sede.

- Organiza reuniones, llamadas telefónicas, y respuestas de manera discreta y efectiva, y toma notas y levanta acta de reuniones.

- Mantener actualizada la información sobre vacaciones, licencias y compensatorios del personal de UNDSS ISW Colombia.

- Lidera el proceso de inventarios de UNDSS ISW Colombia, y realiza los trámites pertinentes para adelantar los procesos de compras, reposiciones, cambios de planes y diferentes actividades relacionadas con la adquisición de bienes.

- Mantener actualizada la historia de los vehículos oficiales, mantenimientos, seguros, facturas y posible logística de reemplazos.

- Gestionar las actividades pertinentes a los contratos de personal de UNDSS ISW Colombia; y llevar un control de las fechas de vencimiento de los documentos expedidos por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores a los funcionarios internacionales de UNDSS y gestionar ante el PNUD el proceso de renovación de estos.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Organización Institucional

El Asistente Local de Seguridad desempeñará sus funciones bajo la guía y supervisión directa del Asesor Jefe de Seguridad, y la coordinación directa del Coordinador de Información y Operaciones de Seguridad.

Competencies

- Competencias Core/Núcleo:

Lograr Resultados: NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles y entrega trabajo de calidad dentro del plazo.

Pensar de forma innovadora: NIVEL 1: Abierto/a a ideas creativas y a riesgos conocidos; resuelve problemas de manera pragmática e impulsa mejoras.

Participar y Asociarse: NIVEL 1: Muestra compasión y comprensión hacia los demás; construye relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: NIVEL 1: Aprecia y respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los sesgos inconscientes y confronta la discriminación.

- Competencias Transversales y Técnicas

Desarrollo de Institucional

Integración dentro de la ONU: Capacidad para identificar e integrar la capacidad y los activos del sistema de las Naciones Unidas, y participar en el trabajo conjunto; conocimiento del sistema de las Naciones Unidas y capacidad para aplicar este conocimiento a la estrategia y/o situaciones prácticas.

Servicios de Seguridad

Asesoramiento, planificación y coordinación de seguridad: Capacidad para proporcionar asesoramiento autorizado y Orientación sobre gestión de seguridad, planificación y coordinación de actividades de seguridad.

Gestión de la información de seguridad: Capacidades analíticas para procesar información de seguridad diversa y desarrollar recomendaciones

Gestión de riesgos: Capacidad para evaluar amenazas y riesgos, identificar y supervisar la implementación de medidas de mitigación, incluida la capacidad de diseñar y probar planes de seguridad

Gestión y seguimiento de incidentes de seguridad: Capacidad para brindar una respuesta adecuada frente a incidentes o sucesos de seguridad

Gestión institucional

Comunicación: Comunicarse de forma clara, concisa y precisa, tanto de manera escrita como verbal; personalizar los mensajes y seleccionar los métodos de comunicación según la audiencia. Capacidad para gestionar las comunicaciones internas y externas a través de los medios de comunicación, las redes sociales y otros canales apropiados.

Datos

Análisis de datos: Capacidad para extraer, analizar y visualizar datos (incluidos los datos en tiempo real) con el fin de obtener perspectivas significativas y ayudar a tomar decisiones eficaces.

Required Skills and Experience

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos

Se requiere un mínimo de 5 años (con Educación Secundaria) o 2 años (con pregrado) de experiencia relevante en alguna de las siguientes áreas:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

II. CORPORATE BACKGROUND:

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities and build resilience to sustain development results.

UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The key 2030 Agenda principle of leaving no one behind and stamping out inequality is at the core of everything we do.

UNDP focuses on helping countries build and share solutions in three main areas:

- Sustainable development

- Democratic governance and peacebuilding

- Climate and disaster resilience

In all our activities, we encourage the protection of human rights and the empowerment of women, minorities and the poorest and most vulnerable.

III. INTERNSHIP OFFICE BACKGROUND:

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in the Programme of Assistance to the Palestinian People (PAPP) works in partnership with the Palestinian Authority, local and international partners to strengthen socio-economic resilience of the Palestinian people, including greater self-reliance, enhance ownership and leadership, and a cohesive identity. PAPP supports key sectors including democratic governance & quality services, inclusive economic opportunities, and sustainable natural resources management.

In line with its ongoing efforts, UNDP/PAPP is seeking an intern to support its Senior Management in key administrative and strategic activities aimed at improving organizational performance, strengthening partnerships, and advancing the UNDP mandate in Palestine. This position will offer valuable insight into development cooperation, project management, and the operational dynamics of UNDP in Palestine.

Duties and Responsibilities

The primary objective of this internship is to support Senior Management in the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of development programs, and to assist in the overall management of the PAPP office’s daily operations:

1) Support in Strategic Planning, Research and Analysis: 40%

- Assist with the preparation, review, and tracking of strategic plans, work plans, and program initiatives, in line with UNDP/PAPP’s objectives.

- Conduct background research, gather data, and prepare briefs and presentations for Senior Management on context and trends.

2)Project Support, Documentation and Internal Reporting: 35%

- Support in day-to-day implementation of projects, helping to monitor and reporting project progress, identifying challenges & solutions.

- Support the preparation of donor brochures and other internal reporting, etc.

3)Support in Internal Comms & Coordination & Admin: 25%

- Assist in drafting of communications materials, including internal memos, and internal newsletters to enhance internal communications and info-sharing.

- Help organize & coordinate meetings, workshops, including preparing agendas, minutes & action points.

- Support admin/other activities as seen relevant and needed

Competencies

Other competencies and attitude:

1) Interest and motivation in working in an international organization.

2) Strong interest in development work and the mandate of UNDP/PAPP.

3) Good analytical skills in gathering and consolidating data and research for practical implementation; with the ability to synthesize complex information and present it clearly.

4) Outgoing and initiative-taking person with a goal-oriented mind-set.

5) Communicate effectively when working in teams and independently.

6) Good in organizing and structuring various tasks and responsibilities; & time management skills

7) Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability.

8) Prior experience in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) or Middle East & North Africa region, is an asset but not mandatory.

9) Responds positively to feedback and differing points of view.

10) Willingness to learn, adapt and take on new challenges.

11) Consistently approaches work with energy and a positive, constructive attitude.

**High levels of professionalism and discretion.

Required Skills and Experience

Education: Field of study: International Relations, Development Studies, Political Science, Public Administration or equivalent.

Candidates must meet one of the following educational requirements:

- 1)currently in the final year of a Bachelor’s degree; or

- 2) currently enrolled in a Master’s degree; or

- 3) have graduated no longer than 1 year ago from a bachelor’s or master’s degree or equivalent studies.

Field of study: International Relations, Development Studies, Political Science, Public Administration or equivalent.

IT skills:

- 1.Knowledge and a proficient user of Microsoft Office productivity tools.

- 2.Familiarity with digital tools and communication platforms.

Languages:

- 1.Excellent written and verbal communications skills in English is required.

- 2.Knowledge of other UN languages is an advantage. (Arabic is a plus).

INTERNSHIP CONDITIONS

The intern will be supervised by the Strategic Coordination & Liaison Officer within the UNDP/PAPP office, who will provide ongoing guidance, feedback, and mentorship throughout the internship period. Regular check-ins will be scheduled to discuss progress and professional development.

- -UNDP will not pay internships but will provide a stipend in the amount of NIS 3,523 monthly in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP internship policy; all other expenses connected with it will be borne by me or my sponsoring Government or institution.

- -UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship.

- -Interns are responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed.

- -Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship.

- -Interns must provide proof of enrolment in health insurance plans.

- -Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity.

- -Interns are expected to work full-time, but flexibility is allowed for education programmes;

- -Interns need to obtain financing for subsistence and make own arrangements for internship, travel, VISA, accommodation, etc.

jobs.title: Analista de Programa - AGDI (Abierto a candidatos externos e internos)
jobs.description:
Descripción de la Oficina/Unidad/Proyecto

El PNUD, como principal organismo de desarrollo de las Naciones Unidas, ocupa una posición única para ayudar a implementar los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y articular esfuerzos para alcanzar la Agenda 2030. En Ecuador, el PNUD trabaja con un enfoque integral y multisectorial, apoyando procesos nacionales que involucran el diseño de políticas públicas, la planificación, la coordinación, el desarrollo de legislación, el monitoreo y la evaluación. Para el cumplimiento de la agenda global, el PNUD trabaja con instituciones del Estado a nivel nacional y local, así como con la sociedad civil, la academia y el sector privado.

El PNUD Ecuador cuenta con seis áreas de trabajo vinculadas a la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible:

- Erradicar la pobreza.

- Gobernabilidad democrática.

- Igualdad socioeconómica y transformación productiva sostenible.

- Prevención de crisis, seguridad humana y resiliencia.

- Gestión ambiental, acción por el clima y energía limpia y asequible.

- Igualdad de género y empoderamiento de las mujeres.

El PNUD, además de actuar como plataforma para la integración, aplicación y seguimiento de los ODS, presta servicios y apoya la ejecución de proyectos que allanan el camino hacia el logro del desarrollo sostenible en el Ecuador. Existen tres catalizadores para apoyar a los países a avanzar hacia estos objetivos: la digitalización, la innovación estratégica y la financiación para el desarrollo.

La Unidad de Programa trabaja para apoyar el logro de los objetivos estratégicos del PNUD para crear un mundo donde las personas y el planeta prosperen juntos, y para ayudar a la Oficina de País a actuar con ambición y escala para abordar los problemas urgentes que enfrenta el país, así como el deterioro de las condiciones climáticas globales. El personal de programa asiste a la Oficina de País en la formulación e implementación de estrategias de programa que van más allá de resolver los desafíos inmediatos del desarrollo para crear cambios sistémicos integrados e inteligentes a futuro en la resiliencia y el fortalecimiento de capacidades dentro del país.

La diversidad, la equidad y la inclusión son principios fundamentales en el PNUD. Valoramos la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que operamos, fomentamos la inclusión como una forma de garantizar que todo el personal esté facultado para contribuir a nuestra misión, y aseguramos la equidad y la justicia en todas nuestras acciones. Adoptar un enfoque de "no dejar a nadie atrás" en nuestros esfuerzos por la diversidad significa aumentar la representación de las poblaciones desatendidas.

El Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo de la Oficina de País del PNUD gestiona proyectos e iniciativas en múltiples temas como, por ejemplo, la protección social, contributiva y no contributiva, inclusión socioeconómica, promoción de derechos y empoderamiento de las mujeres, la integración de la población en movilidad humana, en el fomento de medios de vida, empleo y emprendimiento, el financiamiento del desarrollo, la innovación, ciencia y tecnología, la participación democrática, el acceso a la justicia, la seguridad humana y la resiliencia comunitaria, la prevención de la violencia social y criminal y la transformación pacífica de los conflictos.

El Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo de la Oficina de País del PNUD requiere contratar a un/a profesional que cumpla el rol de Analista de Programa para gestionar actuales proyectos e iniciativas de la cartera, así como para identificar y promover nuevas intervenciones, en particular (pero no exclusivamente) en los temas de reducción de la pobreza, protección y desarrollo social, inclusión socioeconómica, innovación y financiamiento del desarrollo.

Alcance del Trabajo

El PNUD adopta un enfoque de portafolio para acomodar las cambiantes necesidades de la organización y aprovechar las vinculaciones entre las distintas intervenciones para alcanzar sus objetivos estratégicos.

Para ello, se espera que el personal del PNUD esté dispuesto a colaborar a través de unidades, funciones, equipos y proyectos en equipos multidisciplinarios para potenciar y facilitar la colaboración horizontal.

De esta manera, el/la Analista de Programa contribuye no solo a la gestión eficiente de proyectos específicos, sino que también apoya la integración y sinergia dentro del portafolio más amplio, facilitando la comunicación, el intercambio de información y coordinando actividades con otros proyectos o unidades relacionadas.

Además el/la profesional trabajará en colaboración estrecha con los equipos de soporte gerencial, de gestión y desarrollo de programa y operaciones de la Oficina de País, así como otros colegas dentro del área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo del PNUD, personal de programa de otras Agencias de la ONU, personal de la Oficina Regional y la Sede del PNUD y autoridades gubernamentales, asesores técnicos y expertos, donantes multilaterales y bilaterales y la sociedad civil, asegurando una implementación exitosa de los programas del PNUD, a través de las siguientes actividades:

1.Contribuir con la planificación estratégica y a la provisión de asesoría técnica programática

- Diseñar e implementar estrategias de programa enfocadas en la reducción de la pobreza, protección social, desarrollo humano y equidad en el contexto de Ecuador.

- Brindar asesoría técnica de alta calidad a instituciones gubernamentales y contrapartes sobre políticas públicas intersectoriales y la multidimensionalidad de la pobreza.

- Asegurar el alineamiento de las intervenciones con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS), la Agenda 2030 y las prioridades nacionales.

- Analizar y sintetizar la situación política, social y económica del país para la preparación de estudios, notas técnicas e insumos sustantivos para la toma de decisiones.

2. Gestionar integralmente el ciclo de vida de los proyectos a su cargo

- Gestionar la cartera de proyectos asignada, supervisando desde el arranque (acuerdos, registro de riesgos e hitos) hasta el cierre técnico y administrativo.

- Elaborar notas conceptuales, documentos de proyecto, planes de trabajo y presupuestos, asegurando la calidad técnica y el cumplimiento de la normativa institucional.

- Monitorear y evaluar el desempeño financiero y sustantivo de los proyectos, identificando riesgos operativos y desarrollando soluciones proactivas.

- Coordinar auditorías y evaluaciones, asegurando la implementación oportuna de las recomendaciones derivadas de estos procesos.

3. Impulsar la movilización de recursos y el desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas

- Desarrollar y fortalecer alianzas estratégicas con agencias de la ONU, instituciones financieras internacionales (IFI), gobierno, sector privado y sociedad civil.

- Liderar la estrategia de movilización de recursos, identificando oportunidades de financiamiento, analizando perfiles de donantes y formulando propuestas de cooperación.

- Participar en negociaciones y redes de contacto para promover el desarrollo de programas conjuntos y la coordinación de actividades interinstitucionales.

4. Coordinar la gestión del conocimiento y la difusión de productos estratégicos

- Liderar la elaboración y difusión de productos estrella, como los Informes sobre Desarrollo Humano y otros instrumentos corporativos del PNUD.

- Sistematizar lecciones aprendidas y mejores prácticas derivadas de la ejecución de proyectos para fortalecer las redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica del PNUD.

- Identificar fuentes de información y tendencias en políticas de desarrollo para alimentar la estrategia programática del país.

5. Asegurar el reporte oportuno y el seguimiento efectivo de resultados

- Preparar informes sustantivos y financieros de alta calidad para donantes, socios y sedes corporativas.

- Mantener un flujo constante de información y coordinación con otras agencias del Sistema de Naciones Unidas y autoridades estatales.

6. Promover el desarrollo de capacidades y la mejora continua del equipo

- Organizar capacitaciones especializadas para el personal de proyectos en temas programáticos y operativos.

- Promover el aprendizaje activo y el crecimiento profesional dentro del equipo, contribuyendo a las herramientas y redes de conocimiento del PNUD.

El/La titular desempeñará otras actividades dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Área, la Oficina y de la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la titular trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del Coordinador del Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo del PNUD.

En línea con los principios del PNUD, se espera que el/la profesional seleccionado/a aplique un enfoque de igualdad de género en todas sus funciones, asegurando que las intervenciones y análisis contribuyan activamente a la reducción de las brechas de género y al empoderamiento de las mujeres y niñas.

Competencias

Adaptarse con Agilidad

Nivel 2: Adapta procesos y enfoques a nuevas situaciones, involucra a otros en el proceso de cambio

Nivel 2: Capaz de perseverar y lidiar con múltiples fuentes de presión simultáneamente

Comprometerse y Asociarse

Nivel 2: Actúa como facilitador e integrador, promueve el trabajo en equipo. Crea y mantiene asociaciones

Requisitos mínimos de educación

- Título Universitario a nivel avanzado (de Maestría o equivalente) en Economía, Ciencias Sociales, Ciencias Políticas o un campo relacionado es requerido; o

- Título Universitario de Tercer Nivel (Licenciatura/Ingeniería) en Economía, Ciencias Sociales, Ciencias Políticas en combinación con dos (2) años adicionales de experiencia relevante se dará debida consideración en lugar de la Maestría.

Los aplicantes con título de Maestría en un campo de estudio relevante no necesitan tener experiencia laboral profesional.

Los aplicantes con título de Licenciatura/Ingeniería deben tener mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional relevante en planificación, gestión, monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos de protección, desarrollo social y/o inclusión socioeconómica.

Experiencia y/o habilidades deseables (adicionales a las competencias mencionadas en la sección de competencias)

- Experiencia de al menos un (1) año en coordinación o dirección de proyectos.

- Experiencia de al menos un (1) año en instituciones públicas o en organismos internacionales.

Idioma(s) requerido(s) (Nivel):

Certificados profesionales (si aplica):

No aplica

Documentos que deben ser presentados por los postulantes:

- La Unidad de Contratación puede solicitar (“ad hoc”) cualquier información o documento relevante para evaluar la experiencia, por ejemplo: reportes, presentaciones, publicaciones u otros.

Política de Diversidad en el Trabajo

Todas las aplicaciones serán tratadas con la más estricta confidencialidad.

Información importante para las/os postulantes

Nota: El salario neto mensual de esta posición es USD 2.908,01 + 8,33% (contribución Seguridad Social)

Todos los puestos en las categorías NPSA están sujetos a contratación local.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

El PNUD, como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que opera. En este sentido, se alienta a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postularse a las vacantes de la organización. Las decisiones de empleo se basan en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación de ningún tipo.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a la misión institucional, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse plenamente y acceder a oportunidades profesionales en igualdad de condiciones.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, el acoso sexual, la explotación, la discriminación ni el abuso de autoridad. Todas las personas seleccionadas estarán sujetas a verificaciones pertinentes y deberán cumplir con las normas, políticas y principios aplicables del sistema de las Naciones Unidas.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos
