jobs.title: Blue Economy Investment Specialist, IPSA11, Fiji - Suva (UNCDF)- [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

- SME Finance

- Sub-National Finance

- Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

UNCDF is seeking a Blue Economy Investment Specialist to lead the origination, structuring, and deployment of ocean-positive and nature-based blended finance investments in the Pacific. The position will focus on mobilizing concessional and catalytic capital toward enterprises and financial intermediaries that generate sustainable livelihoods while protecting and restoring coastal and marine ecosystems, with a particular emphasis on reef-positive, fisheries, aquaculture, coastal tourism, waste management, and ocean-climate resilience solutions.

Among other tasks, the incumbent is expected to manage the blue economy portfolio in the Pacific, in particular the EU-funded Sustainable Pacific Blue Circle Fund (SPBCF) project, an impact investment vehicle that provides investment capital backed by venture-building support (technical assistance, grants, loans, guarantees) to businesses that have the potential to generate revenue and create a positive development impact ongoing till 2028. The incumbent is also expected to oversee other blue economy focused and reef-positive interventions that are implemented in the Pacific region.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Regional Investment Specialists for the Pacific and in close collaboration with other colleagues in IID and IFOD, the Blue Economy Investment Specialist will lead and support the development, structuring and execution of blue‑economy or other relevant sectoral investment initiatives. The Specialist will work closely with IID and IFOD colleagues, as well as other UNCDF counterparts, country focal points, government partners, private sector actors and development partners.

1) Project Management of Blue‑Economy Investment Initiatives

- Manage all aspects of the blue economy initiatives implemented in the Pacific.

- Lead the preparation and implementation of Annual Work Plans (AWPs), budgets and activity schedules for Pacific blue‑economy investment programmes.

- Manage day‑to‑day implementation of activities, including stakeholder engagement, technical assistance delivery, pipeline development and progress monitoring.

- Manage project documentation, track financial delivery, oversee audits when required, and support organization of steering committee meetings.

- Ensure effective coordination between countries, regional teams, and corporate oversight units to deliver a complex multi-country programme.

- Apply UNCDF Social and Environmental Standards (SES), including safeguards related to human rights, gender equality, SEA/SH prevention, and grievance mechanisms.

- Maintain and update project risk registers, escalate high-risk issues, and contribute to assurance activities, audits, and evaluations.

- Apply adaptive management approaches, identifying implementation risks and bottlenecks and proposing timely corrective actions.

- Ensure efficient use of project resources, value for money, and adherence to approved budgets.

2) Investment Pipeline Development and Blended Finance Execution

- Lead the sourcing, screening, and development of a diversified pipeline of blue and green economy MSMEs

- Oversee incubation and acceleration pathways, ensuring MSMEs receive tailored technical assistance and progress toward investment readiness.

- Guide and quality-assure financial, technical, environmental and social (ESG), and gender-lens due diligence processes for MSMEs and financial-sector partners.

- Coordinate the structuring and deployment of investment grants, concessional loans, and credit guarantees benefiting the blue economy in line with UNCDF investment policies and approval committees.

- Support engagement with local financial institutions, development banks, and impact investors to crowd in private capital in support of the blue economy.

- Ensure supported enterprises are prepared for graduation to concessional or commercial finance.

- Contribute to the design, feasibility assessment, and investor engagement for the expansion of blended finance in the blue economy, ensuring alignment with UNCDF’s catalytic mandate.

3) Partnership Development, Stakeholder Engagement, and Policy Dialogue

- Serve as UNCDF’s primary focal point for blue economy related engagement with governments, central banks, regulators, donors, financial institutions, NGOs, business development service providers, and private investors.

- Build and sustain strategic partnerships that enhance MSME incubation, financial sector capacity, and capital mobilization for blue and green economy investments.

- Support structured dialogue with policymakers and regulators to strengthen enabling environments for sustainable finance and MSME access to capital.

- Coordinate engagement with regional and international partners working in the blue economy to leverage synergies and avoid duplication.

- Represent UNCDF in national, regional, and international forums related to blended finance, blue economy, and climate finance.

- Promote South–South and Triangular Cooperation initiatives and knowledge exchange around blue economy matters.

4) Monitoring, Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Learning

- Oversee and maintain robust M&E systems capturing both programme and investment‑level results, including blue‑economy‑specific indicators (e.g., sustainable fisheries outcomes, marine ecosystem co‑benefits, climate resilience).

- Ensure high-quality data collection, analysis, and reporting, including disaggregation by sex, youth, sector, and country.

- Contribute to timely and accurate donor reports, annual progress reviews, and mid-term and final evaluations.

- Lead knowledge capture and dissemination, including case studies, lessons learned, and good practices for blue and green economy finance.

- Support learning and replication by sharing evidence and insights within UNCDF and with regional and global partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies - UNDP Core Competencies can be found here.

- Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively - LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously - LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination - LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner - LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Business Direction & Strategy

Strategic Thinking

Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNCDF’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business

Development

Knowledge Generation

Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business

Management

Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business

Management

Working with

Evidence and Data

Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

Finance

Development finance expertise

Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.

Business Direction & Strategy

Systems Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Partnerships management

Private Sector engagement

Ability to identify, conduct outreach and manage relationships with the private sector.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An Advanced (Master’s level) university degree in business administration, finance, marketing, economics, accounting or related fields is required.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with a Masters’ Degree) or 9 years (with Bachelor’s Degree) of relevant work experience in either the financial sector or the private sector or a mix, preferably with investment and/or business management expertise.

- A minimum of 5 years investment experience in the blue economy and financial instruments is required.

- Experience working in venture capital and/or banking within an international financial environment, preferably in development finance institution, impact investor or similar is required;

- Experience in private credit and/or equity for investments with a social mission in emerging/frontier markets, is required.

- Experience in project preparation and/or in development of investment opportunities, especially for investment projects focusing on blue economy in developing countries is required.

- Competency with financial modeling and analysis in Microsoft excel is required.

- Computer literacy, including proficient use of research applications is required.

Desired Experience:

- Experience in nature-related or climate-aligned investments

- Experience in evaluating environmental impacts alongside commercial viability.

- Understanding of the investment needs of enterprises and the mix of debt/equity required at different growth stages—from incubation to scaling up to commercial viability.

- Strong knowledge of financial markets and financing for sustainable development, with the ability to apply it to strategic and/or practical situations.

- Strong analytical writing skills; experienced in producing concise, executive level reports (PowerPoint) and presentations, training modules and materials.

- A minimum of 2 years of experience in working for/in the UN System or similar international development finance institution;

Language:

- Written and spoken fluency in English is required;

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Senior Country Economist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Asia-Pacific region is not on track to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). On current trends, 88% of SDG targets are unlikely to be met by 2030. Meanwhile, human insecurity is at all-time highs, with more than half of people in most countries worried about their jobs. Looking ahead, the development landscape is likely to become more turbulent as existential threats from climate change combine with fresh headwinds to growth and job creation amidst rising governance risks.

It is against this backdrop—a large unfinished agenda, elevated levels of insecurity, and a more turbulent development landscape—that UNDP supports countries to accelerate progress towards the 2030 Agenda and beyond. As the UN’s global development network, UNDP advocates for change, and connects countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP is on the ground in over 170 countries and territories. Combining local presence with global expertise, it aspires to eradicate poverty, accelerate structural transformation, build resilience, and contribute to lasting sustainable development.

The Country Economist Network of the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) is one of the region’s most valuable initiatives to enhance policy support and capacity. The Network has gained additional relevance in light of the significantly more challenging context described above. In this respect, the Country Economist plays an important role at the country but also regional and global levels in contributing to renewed development momentum in an era of turbulence and uncertainty.

In the programme countries, UNDP supports stabilization, state-building, governance and development priorities in in partnership with the host governments, the United Nations system, the development partners and other partners to help the country to achieve sustainable development by eradicating poverty in all its forms and dimensions, accelerating structural transformations for sustainable development and building resilience to crises and shock.

UNDP has the mandate to support SDG Integration to ensure faster progress on sustainable development and offers support in four areas, (1) integrated policy and programming solutions, (2) SDG metrics, data and analysis using state-of-the-art tools for modelling and forecasting, (3) knowledge and innovation and (4) SDG Financing options to help countries identify innovative ways to expand public and private contributions to reach the 2030 agenda.

In addition, UNDP works closely with the Government of Malaysia in providing thought leadership through support in formulation of policy options. This includes receiving high level policy requests on support for the 13th Malaysia Plan and undertaking structural economic policy analyses to achieve Malaysia’s aim of being a high income and sustainable nation by 2030.

The Country Economist works under the direct guidance of the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative in the Country Office, in close collaboration with programme and operations teams, and has a dotted line to the RBAP Chief Economist. S/he is an ambassador of the Economist Network and is expected to contribute about 20% of her/his time to activities across the Network (in other countries, the subregion or the region). S/he will also serve as principal adviser to senior management on economic and development policy matters.

The Country Economist integrates the activities UNDP delivers in the region and ensures these contribute the greatest development impact possible. S/he makes a difference by being keenly aware of the changing development landscape, embedding a sharp strategic focus on the development interventions that matter the most, and connecting diagnostics and solutions to the politics of change and the art of delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

In this respect, the Country Economist works closely with colleagues of RBAP as well as the Global Policy Network (GPN), based in Bangkok, New York, and other locations. S/he develops and maintains a professional network across development partner agencies, government institutions, the private sector, and civil society at the country level.

Duties and Responsibilities

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: This role will be responsible for supervising personnel including the consultants; and therefore, requires demonstration of UNDP People Management competencies. Provides leadership, strategic direction and quality assurance for the economics and policy function.

Advise UNDP Country Office management and programme teams on ways to strengthen evidence-based and future-oriented programme development and implementation;

- Advise UNDP Country Office management in the preparation and implementation of country programmes and strategies, including the development of country programme document (CPD), and related analyses;

- Advise and support UNDP Country Office teams to develop and manage relevant thematic portfolios, such as activities to support inclusive growth and progress towards the SDGs;

- Lead UNDP Country Office efforts to conceptualize and implement the Development Finance Assessment (DFA) and accompanying process and use existing financial resources more effectively and efficiently to achieve the SDGs;

- Lead macroeconomic, sectoral and political-economy analysis and provide strategic economic policy advice to Country Office management, programme teams and government counterparts;

- Produce periodic economic, development and policy outlooks identifying trends, emerging risks, opportunities and implications for UNDP's country programme and strategic positioning;

- Lead the development of the National Human Development Report (HDR) and ensure that it provides added value in terms of development economic analysis, updated data, and information for policy formulation;

- Compile data and perform statistical analysis as required to support innovative knowledge of work country strategies and activities;

- Advise and support the creation of large-scale development solutions to help address complex development challenges;

- Lead the expansion of Country Office service offers on financing for development, including innovative financing models and country specific/sector specific studies;

- Lead the Country Office's economic and policy knowledge agenda, including flagship reports, policy notes, strategic foresight papers, executive briefs and thought-leadership publications;

- Translate economic analysis into actionable programme concepts, policy advisory services, partnership opportunities and resource mobilization pipelines.

Lead policy advice to national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and the introduction of sustainable and inclusive economic policies;

- Advise and facilitate dialogue on sustainable development issues with government officials, development partners, civil society, and private sector;

- Provide policy and programming advice and support for development planning and policy formulation at the national, sub-national, and local levels;

- Advise and support the identification and analysis of interventions that can impact multiple development goals and targets at the same time;

- Advise and support monitoring and reporting of progress related to SDGs and other national development frameworks, including strengthening national and local level data collection and statistical capacity;

- Leverage UNDP’s regional and global programmes, to provide holistic and effective support to the country;

- Leverage support and expertise from the UNDP’s global/regional Economist networks to strengthen UNDP’s support on economic analysis and policy development for the Government and the UN Country Team.

- Convene and shape policy dialogues, strategic roundtables and knowledge exchanges that advance UNDP's policy influence and thought leadership.

Advocate and engage with partners to support UNDP’s institutional positioning and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative;

- Contribute, in close collaboration with senior management, to the development and/or strengthening of partnerships with UN agencies, IFIs, bilateral development agencies, private sector entities, and civil society.

- Represent UNDP as a recognized thought leader and technical spokesperson in national and regional economic-policy forums;

- Support the Resident Representative in resource mobilization and future growth strategies;

- Contribute to national, regional, and global knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with government, academia, think tanks, the private sector and development partners to strengthen policy influence and programme development.

Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas and facilitating knowledge sharing:

- Contribute to UNDP regional knowledge products and development of programming offers in regional priority areas (e.g., inequality, future of work, innovative financing, development strategies, economic governance, political economy);

- Participate actively in the Economist Network of RBAP by attending regional meetings (in-person and/or virtual), sharing relevant experiences, and contributing to peer reviews;

- Collaborate and contribute to regional and sub-regional publications, practice notes, and Regional Human Development Reports;

- Stay informed about broader developments, contribute to cross-border and cross-GPN initiatives, and support the economist network through common analyses, frameworks, and templates;

- Enhance UNDP’s understanding and design of new approaches to sustainable development across the region by acting as a regional thematic lead where possible.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need; Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches; Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience; Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment; Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Digital

- Data literacy: Understand the potential as well as the limitations of using data driven innovation; Ability to use a mix of data sources (quantitative, qualitative or real-time techniques) to develop understanding, identify patterns to inform decision making or identify opportunities for further exploration

- Co-creation: Ability to design and facilitate a process that enables a diverse group of stakeholders to solve a common problem, develop a practice, or create knowledge together; Ability to embrace diversity, work with a diverse group of stakeholders, understand their interests, perspectives and views and tap into them as a source for creativity; Ability to facilitate processes and create conditions that are open for diverse inputs, stimulate collaboration and sharing.

Programme and policy

- SDG Integration: Microeconomic Models/ Analysis; Macroeconomic Models/ Analysis; Economic Forecasting; Integrated Policy

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics or related field is required; Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Economics or related field in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- A Ph.D. in Economics will be an advantage.

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level that includes extensive experience in research and policy-level analysis, and some experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development projects is required;

- Extensive experience in research and policy-level analysis, covering (for example) labour markets, public finance, development finance, structural transformation, economic modelling, and AI-related policy issues is required;

- Proven policy, advisory, and advocacy experience is required;

- Experience in preparing high-quality policy briefs and guidance notes for use by senior policymakers is required;

- Experience in strategic visioning with strong technical and highly developed analytical capabilities is desired;

- Experience leading or managing an economics, research or policy advisory function is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of the SDGs and their application at the national level, politically astute with demonstrated experience in stakeholder analysis and engagement is an asset;

- Experience in handling data and software programmes for statistical analysis is desired;

- Previous work experience in Asia and the Pacific region and cross-country experience would be an asset.

Languuage Requirement:

- Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station (Bahasa Melayu) is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language is an asset.

Equal opportunity

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development. We support countries and communities as they work to eradicate poverty, implement the Paris Agreement on climate change and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. We advocate for transformative change, and we connect countries to the resources they need to help people build a better life. Additionally, UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

The UNDP Rome Centre for Climate and Energy (the “UNDP Rome Centre”) is the key platform for the strategic engagement between UNDP and the Italian Government. It focuses on the critical policy areas of climate finance, youth engagement in climate action, and energy for development. These objectives are pursued through the effective implementation of its four main programmes:

• PISTA (Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance)

• Youth4Climate

• Energy For Growth

• Digital Flagship

PISTA, the Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance, aims to mobilise finance for climate, energy and the environment. Specifically, PISTA aims to support projects that contribute to the decarbonization efforts of developing economies and to their transition to climate-resilient economies, and it aims to catalyse international financial resources toward these initiatives. Matching impactful projects with investors and capital providers goes hand in hand with the engagement with financial institutions - both institutional and private - at Italian and global level. In its current portfolio, PISTA is supporting 24 projects across Africa, to which it is providing technical assistance with the goal of strengthening their bankability - from developing financial models, to enhancing environmental and social impact management, to more ad hoc project supportYouth4Climate promotes youth engagement in climate action, contributing to SDG13. Youth4Climate supports the implementation of youth-led and youth-inclusive solutions to environmental and climate challenges, both financially and through capacity development. It also gives young people around the world who are committed to fighting climate change a platform to engage with policymakers and global leaders.

Energy For Growth (“E4G”) aims to promote access to sustainable energy in developing countries, contributing to SDG7. The goal of the initiative is to assist partner countries in unlocking finance to scale up the diffusion of clean energy solutions, increase access to energy and boost the energy transition. E4G aims to foster the mobilization of public and private capital toward projects aligned with the international policy agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. It does so by connecting UNDP's capacity and connections in emerging economies and developing countries with the public-private ecosystem of Italy and other G7 countries, in the crucial sector of energy.

The Italy–Africa Digital Flagship is a key initiative under the Italian Mattei Plan, implemented by the UNDP Rome Centre under its Strategic Initiatives portfolio, it is delivered in close partnership with national governments, the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Italian public and private sector partners. It focuses on advancing digital public infrastructure, digital identity systems, agritech solutions, and data-driven governance, contributing to sustainable development and inclusive economic growth.

Duties and Responsibilities

UNDP Rome Centre requires an additional team member to work as a Digital and Public Investment Specialist to contribute to its growing pipeline of large, impactful, and bankable projects. The UNDP Rome Centre, through PISTA and other programmes, provides support to projects across sectors in the climate and energy space, helping them on project development (e.g., technical feasibility studies, financial viability assessments, environmental and social impact assessments, impact framework development, advanced stakeholder engagement etc.) and connecting such projects with financiers.

Among such projects, UNDP is providing preparatory phase technical support to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire under the Italy-Africa Digital Flagship Programme to translate strategic investment concepts in the thematic areas of climate-resilient agriculture, smart irrigation, AI and data innovation into structured, bankable and implementation-ready public sector projects.

Given the nature of the assignment, UNDP seeks to hire a specialist with experience in structuring public sector and public-private investment projects for multilateral development banks (MDBs), development finance institutions (DFIs), and sovereign or blended finance platforms.

The successful candidate will make a crucial contribution to the Digital Flagship and PISTA team as a technical expert. The Specialist will play a pivotal role in overseeing and managing the post-origination phase of projects, that is ensuring interventions are designed to fit Italian and international DFIs/MDBs criteria to unlock climate finance and lead the investment structuring in collaboration with relevant DFIs/MDBs.

The Public and Digital Investment Specialist will report to the Digital Flagship team lead, and will have a secondary reporting to the PISTA team lead; she/he will engage with other UNDP Rome Centre colleagues as needed.

The scope of work over the course of the period may vary depending on the specific assignment and development of the programme.

A. Investment Structuring and Bankability Advisory

• Contribute to quality-assure the structuring of the two investment packages so that they are suitable for appraisal, financing and implementation, in line with the project's objective of producing executive feasibility studies and investment-ready project documents.

• Support the definition of a clear and financeable investment perimeter for: (i) the integrated climate-resilient agriculture and smart irrigation package; and (ii) the AI and Data Innovation Hub.

• Ensure that technical proposals are translated into coherent investment packages with clear CAPEX/OPEX assumptions, implementation sequencing, institutional responsibilities, and financing pathways.

• Assess the bankability of proposed investments, identify critical gaps, and recommend measures to strengthen technical credibility, revenue logic where applicable, affordability, public value, sustainability, and implementation feasibility.

• Support development of trancheable and modular investment options to preserve financing optionality and enable phased financing and implementation, as envisaged in the project strategy.

• Ensure alignment of the financial structuring with likely appraisal requirements of CDP and other prospective financiers engaged in climate, digital infrastructure, agriculture, and public sector modernization.

• Based on the project’s needs, support the identification of suitable co-financing partners and windows, including MDBs, bilateral development partners, climate funds, impact investors, and other DFIs to move to financial close.

B. Appraisal Readiness and Transaction Support

• Review feasibility outputs to ensure they meet the level of definition needed for financing review, procurement preparation and smooth implementation without further design work, consistent with the project document.

• Contribute and support on due diligence expectations commonly applied by MDBs/DFIs, including requirements related to technical feasibility, economic justification, safeguards, climate rationale, governance, procurement, operations and maintenance, and institutional readiness.

• Support the development of investment memoranda, decision notes, financing briefs, and presentations tailored to prospective financiers and government decision-makers.

• Contribute to the packaging of documentation required for downstream engagement with financing institutions, including review of procurement strategy, implementation roadmap, governance arrangements, and risk mitigation measures.

• Identify issues that may affect appraisal timelines or financing decisions and propose mitigation measures early in the preparation process.

C. Coordination with Feasibility Study Teams and Stakeholders

• Work closely with the multidisciplinary consulting teams engaged for the agriculture-irrigation and AI Hub feasibility studies, whose scopes include engineering, hydrology, climate analysis, digital systems architecture, cybersecurity, institutional modelling, financial structuring, and safeguards.

• Participate in technical working groups, validation workshops, and review sessions convened under the project governance arrangements.

• Advise UNDP and government counterparts on strategic engagement with key sectoral ministries and technical agencies to ensure investment structuring is grounded in national systems, implementation realities, and institutional mandates.

• Support structured engagement with Italian partners and other strategic stakeholders to ensure alignment with financing priorities, appraisal standards and market expectations.

• Provide targeted advisory inputs for discussions with engineering firms, technology providers, agritech companies, cloud and data infrastructure providers, and other relevant market actors, in compliance with transparency and procurement rules.

D. Quality Assurance and Knowledge Contribution

• Provide expert review and written comments on inception, interim and final feasibility outputs, with particular focus on investment logic, financing strategy, implementation readiness and institutional sustainability.

• Contribute to the quality assurance of project outputs against international infrastructure and development finance appraisal standards, as well as UNDP's investment preparation standards reflected in the sample ToR.

• Capture lessons learned and good practices on structuring integrated public sector investments that combine physical infrastructure, digital systems, climate resilience and institutional reform.

• Contribute to internal knowledge products or strategic notes that may support replication of the model in other countries under the Italy-Africa Digital Flagship Programme.

E. Knowledge Sharing, Monitoring and Evaluation

• Monitor activities to track progress, results, and identify areas for improvement for assigned investment projects

• Report on project effectiveness and impact, contribute to the development of the PISTA's annual report by providing data and insights on performance of projects under the Specialist’s responsibility

• Assist with donor engagement and relationship management activities as required, including for the timely publication and dissemination of reports against the Digital Flagship and PISTA milestones and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

• Contribute to knowledge sharing initiatives within the Digital Flagship and PISTA team and with UNDP Country Offices.

The incumbent may also be requested to perform other related tasks necessary for the successful delivery of the assignment.

4. Institutional Arrangement

• The incumbent will be office-based;

• The incumbent will report to the Digital Flagship team lead and will have a secondary reporting to the PISTA team lead, and will work in close coordination with UNDP Country Office, relevant UNDP technical teams, the Project Board, and the Technical Working Groups established for the two feasibility studies.

• The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment.

• International mission travel may be required.

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction and Strategy-System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management-Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment

Business Management & Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Finance & Development Finance Expertise: Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.

Digital & Alternative Finance: Ability to identify potential alternative forms of finance and mobilise them for the purpose of addressing development challenges. Ability to review the skills, capacities, procedures and protocols that are needed to enable new financial mechanisms, and to assess the risks, limitations and implications of using them. Ability to set up the processes and structures to design, test and implement new financial mechanisms, including managing outreach and stakeholder engagement.

Digital & Digital Transformation Design: Practical and strategic skills in digital transformation design for governments and organisations.

Business Management & Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. .Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Finance, Economics, Public Policy, Infrastructure Finance, Engineering, Business Administration, International Development, or a related field is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor´s degree) in the above fields in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of an advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in project development, investment structuring, transaction advisory, infrastructure finance, development finance, or related fields is required.

- Proven track record of experience in preparing, structuring, appraising or financing complex public sector or sovereign-backed investment projects, an emerging market or developing country is required.

- Demonstrated experience working on projects involving one or more of the following: irrigation or water infrastructure, climate-resilient agriculture, digital public infrastructure, data centers/cloud systems, innovation ecosystems, or public sector digital transformation is required.

- Strong experience reviewing or developing feasibility studies, business cases, investment cases, financial models, implementation roadmaps and procurement strategies for major projects in emerging economies and developing countries is required.

- Prior professional experience with, or directly advising on projects financed by, institutions such as the World Bank Group, African Development Bank, Islamic Development Bank, European Investment Bank, or other multilateral development banks and development finance institutions is desired.

- Experience with sovereign lending, blended finance, climate finance, or large public investment programmes supported by MDBs/DFIs is desired.

- Experience in structuring projects to meet lender appraisal requirements and investment committee standards is desired.

- Experience with entire investment management cycle including demonstrated ability to structure blended finance support and/or advisory services to enhance project bankability is desired.

- Demonstrated experience with safeguards, climate finance rationale, institutional assessments, and implementation arrangements required for investment approval is desired.

- Experience engaging public authorities, technical ministries, implementing agencies, and private sector actors to develop implementable, financeable investment projects is desired.

- Experience in Africa, including Francophone Africa is desired.

Languages:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in French is highly desirable.

Descripción de la oficina/unidad/proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Desde hace 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

El proyecto 1005035 “Instituto de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el desarrollo Humano INADEH 4.0: Formación para la Competitividad y el desarrollo”, busca contribuir al posicionamiento del INADEH como rector de la formación profesional, al fortalecimiento institucional, a la mejora de la calidad de la oferta educativa de hoy y del futuro, y a la mejora de la gestión operativa.

De esta manera, la acción del PNUD se centra en apoyar en la generación de una visión del sistema de formación técnica profesional con alternativas diferenciadas que sirvan a las personas, a la economía y a la sociedad. Organizar la gobernanza de la formación técnica y profesional, la vinculación educación – empleo, superar la sexta frontera, y poner el talento y capacidad de las y los panameños en reactivar nuestra economía y desarrollar la estrategia del cambio del proyecto definida como “Formación profesional como instrumento para fortalecer competencias, asegurar medios de vida y hacer una economía competitiva”.

La Oficina de Proyectos del INADEH es la instancia principal de comunicación y gestión de proyectos que ejecuta el INADEH con diversos organismos e instituciones, por lo que su rol principal es brindar estrecho seguimiento a la ejecución de los proyectos que se ejecutan como aquellos que se proyectan ejecutar en la institución, tanto en el corto como en el mediano plazo.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática fortalecerá la gestión de la Oficina de Informática del INADEH, brindando apoyo técnico en el análisis, diseño, desarrollo, validación, documentación y mantenimiento de programas y soluciones informáticas, de acuerdo con las necesidades institucionales y los requerimientos establecidos.

Las actividades específicas incluyen el apoyo en:

- Análisis, diseño y desarrollo de programas y soluciones informáticas Apoyar en el levantamiento, análisis y documentación de las necesidades de los usuarios y de los datos requeridos para el desarrollo o mejora de programas y soluciones informáticas. Desarrollar y actualizar programas, aplicaciones o componentes informáticos, utilizando los lenguajes de programación y las herramientas tecnológicas definidas para cada solución. Diseñar los pasos lógicos requeridos para el desarrollo de programas individuales o que formen parte de sistemas informáticos, incluyendo la preparación de flujogramas y la codificación correspondiente. Interpretar y procesar información relacionada con las actividades de su área de trabajo, utilizando los medios y herramientas tecnológicas requeridas, de acuerdo con los procedimientos técnicos aplicables.

- Validación, mantenimiento y documentación de programas Ejecutar pruebas funcionales de los programas, aplicaciones o componentes desarrollados, identificar posibles errores y realizar los ajustes requeridos dentro de su ámbito de competencia. Revisar y comprobar las listas de validación de los programas elaborados. Documentar los programas desarrollados y preparar las instrucciones necesarias para su operación y utilización. Mantener organizada y actualizada la documentación y los archivos relacionados con los programas y soluciones informáticas bajo su responsabilidad. Proponer mejoras a los métodos y procesos de trabajo relacionados con las funciones del puesto, cuando corresponda.

- Asistencia técnica, seguimiento e informes Atender consultas y brindar asistencia técnica, dentro de su ámbito de competencia, al personal de la institución y a terceros, cuando corresponda, de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos. Apoyar en la preparación de informes periódicos sobre las actividades desarrolladas, avances y resultados de los trabajos asignados.

- Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el fortalecimiento de capacidades en el marco del proyecto. Participar en actividades de capacitación y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras iniciativas de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la elaboración de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción. Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes —a nivel nacional, regional e internacional— relacionadas con la labor del proyecto. Realizar aportes valiosos a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización de los conocimientos, productos y herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia difusión entre los socios.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Proyecto, la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

- Supervisión: El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática trabajará bajo la supervisión general del/de la Coordinador/a del Proyecto y del/de la Director/a del Proyecto. Sus servicios tendrán alcance nacional y se prestarán en el marco del Proyecto 01005035, “Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH) 4.0: Formación profesional para la competitividad y el desarrollo humano”. La relación contractual se establecerá directamente con la Oficina de País del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), en coordinación con el equipo del Proyecto, el Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental y el Instituto Nacional de Formación Profesional y Capacitación para el Desarrollo Humano (INADEH).

- Lugar de trabajo: El/la Asistente en Programación de Informática estará asignado/a a la Oficina de Proyectos de Transformación y Mejora Integral del INADEH, sin perjuicio de los desplazamientos a otros centros o sedes institucionales que sean requeridos para el cumplimiento de las funciones establecidas en estos Términos de Referencia.

- Horario: El/la profesional deberá laborar en horario regular de lunes a viernes. Cuando las necesidades del Proyecto lo requieran, deberá tener disponibilidad para laborar en horario extendido.

- Movilización: Los gastos de movilización, alojamiento y alimentación derivados de misiones oficiales o actividades previamente autorizadas, conforme a los requerimientos del Proyecto, serán cubiertos por este, de acuerdo con las normas y procedimientos aplicables.

Habilidades deseadas

- Experiencia o conocimientos en análisis y visualización de datos, utilizando herramientas como Python, Power BI, Tableau u otras.

jobs.title: Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026.

Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards.

As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing.

The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management.

UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups.

The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level.

The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience.

Duties and Responsibilities

She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities:

1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning:

- Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates.

- Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data.

- Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making.

- Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements.

- Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations.

- Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue.

- Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making.

- Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems:

- Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs.

- Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information.

- Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops.

- Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms.

- Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information

3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning:

- Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement.

- Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes.

- Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up.

- Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs.

- Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations.

- Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning.

- Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up.

4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms and Technology-Enabled Learning:

- Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge.

- Administer the WordPress-based content management system, including user and publishing workflows, system performance, backups, security and other functions necessary for reliable operation of the platform.

- Coordinate with government counterparts, technical experts and project teams to publish and disseminate policy documents, research, dashboards, knowledge products and other programme evidence through relevant digital platforms.

- Develop and integrate website functionalities and linkages with project dashboards, monitoring systems, mobile applications and other digital knowledge and evidence platforms to improve accessibility and use of programme evidence.

- Monitor platform usage and analytics and use findings to strengthen access to and dissemination of monitoring evidence, research and programme learning.

- Support technology-enabled programme learning, knowledge-sharing and evidence-dissemination events through appropriate digital tools, including digital registration, QR-based attendance, electronic feedback, digital materials, presentation and information-sharing systems, ensuring that relevant participation and feedback data contribute to programme learning and knowledge management.

5- Coordinate MEL, Evidence Use and Reporting with Government and Partners:

- Coordinate with the Cabinet Division, General Economics Division, BBS, relevant ministries/divisions, implementing partners, UN agencies, development partners, academia, civil society and other stakeholders on monitoring, reporting, evidence generation and use of programme data.

- Facilitate institutional coordination, data-sharing and validation processes required for national and sub-national monitoring systems and evidence-based social protection decision-making.

- Provide technical guidance to government counterparts and partners on RBM, MEL approaches, data quality, evidence use, digital monitoring systems and reporting requirements.

- Support Project Board, Project Steering Committee, Technical Committee, donor and other strategic meetings through preparation and presentation of monitoring reports, dashboards, analytical findings, evidence products and briefing materials.

6- Strengthen Institutional Capacity, Quality Assurance and Cross-Cutting Integration:

- Plan and support capacity-building initiatives for government counterparts and project personnel on MEL, RBM, evidence use, data management, digital MEL systems, dashboards, GRS and related knowledge and learning functions.

- Strengthen institutional capacity to generate, manage, interpret and use monitoring, administrative, survey and programme evidence for policy and programme decision-making.

- Ensure that gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights and Leave No One Behind principles are appropriately integrated into monitoring frameworks, data analysis, digital systems, evaluations and learning products.

- Monitor programme risks, assumptions and mitigation measures relevant to the Analyst’s functional areas and contribute to periodic updating of the Project Risk Log.

- Support quality assurance and compliance with UNDP Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), Central M&E requirements, corporate reporting standards, information-security requirements, audit recommendations and other applicable standards.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) will work under the direct supervision of the National Project Manager of the SSPS Program II and will also report to and receive technical guidance from the Project Adviser (Technical) on substantive matters related to MEL, evidence generation, data analytics, and related technical areas. The Project Analyst will supervise the work of Project Associate (Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning) and Project Associate (MIS).
