Aproximación por Niveles (Tiered Approach)

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organización, la mayoría de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicación por niveles (tiers) en donde:

- Nivel 0: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos sáran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

- Nivel 1: otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

- Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas

- Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor tenga en cuenta del nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si lo hay, y asegúrese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

Descripción del proyecto

El PNUD trabaja en unos 170 países y territorios, ayudando a erradicar la pobreza, reducir las desigualdades y la exclusión, y fomentar la resiliencia para que los países puedan mantener el progreso. Como organismo de desarrollo de las Naciones Unidas, el PNUD desempeña un papel fundamental para ayudar a los países a alcanzar los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible. El personal del PNUD está unido por un propósito común: ayudar a los países y comunidades de todo el mundo; y perseguir vidas pacíficas y prósperas, vividas en armonía con el planeta.

PNUD Guatemala, de acuerdo con las prioridades estratégicas acordadas en el Documento de Programa de País (DPC) para el período 2022-2025 es la organización de las Naciones Unidas que contribuye a los esfuerzos nacionales hacia un desarrollo sostenible, resiliente, equitativo e inclusivo, utilizando un enfoque participativo e innovador. Esto ha implicado un aumento de las alianzas con socios de cooperación, dentro del Sistema de Naciones Unidas y con instituciones nacionales y locales, y con redes de la sociedad civil y comunidades.

Las prioridades estratégicas del PNUD son:

- Instituciones fuertes : El PNUD brinda apoyo técnico a mecanismos de coordinación interinstitucional liderados por instituciones nacionales en gabinetes sociales y económicos, desarrollo rural integrado y alianzas de ciencia y tecnología. Trabaja en la promoción de la innovación en el uso de la tecnología, la generación de datos, el desarrollo de sistemas de información y el análisis de género para fortalecer la toma de decisiones basada en evidencias a nivel nacional y local.

- Paz, seguridad y justicia : El PNUD apoya el fortalecimiento de las instituciones estatales que trabajan para aumentar la seguridad ciudadana, el acceso a la justicia y la transformación de los conflictos.

- Fomento de la resiliencia para la adaptación al cambio climático : El PNUD trabaja para fortalecer las plataformas de coordinación interinstitucional e intersectorial para la planificación del desarrollo, la adaptación al cambio climático y su mitigación, la gestión de la biodiversidad y las áreas protegidas, la seguridad alimentaria y la gestión de la reducción del riesgo de desastres.

- Desarrollo socioeconómico sostenible e inclusivo . El PNUD está trabajando para fortalecer el sistema nacional de protección social, utilizando una perspectiva de género y priorizando las vulnerabilidades a las que se enfrentan las personas en situaciones de crisis y choques. Se promueven la coordinación, la colaboración y las alianzas con otras instituciones públicas, el sector privado y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil para una coordinación territorial eficaz y el intercambio regional de mejores prácticas.

El proyecto “Mejoramiento Instalaciones Deportivas y Recreativas en 10 Avenida 23-91 Zona 5 Estadio Nacional Doroteo Guamuch Flores Guatemala, Guatemala”, implementado por el PNUD en alianza con la Confederación Deportiva Autónoma de Guatemala (CDAG), tiene como objetivo contribuir al fortalecimiento institucional y al desarrollo sostenible mediante la modernización de infraestructura deportiva estratégica, particularmente el Estadio Nacional Doroteo Guamuch Flores.

La intervención contempla la rehabilitación de la pista de atletismo conforme a estándares internacionales (World Athletics), mejoras en el campo de juego, sistemas de iluminación tipo FIFA A, accesibilidad universal, así como la incorporación de criterios de sostenibilidad ambiental y eficiencia en el uso de recursos.

El proyecto se enmarca en la Política General de Gobierno 2024–2028 y en el Programa de País de PNUD, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de instituciones públicas eficaces, inclusivas y transparentes, así como a la promoción del deporte como motor de desarrollo social, cohesión comunitaria y reducción de desigualdades.

Asimismo, la intervención busca fortalecer las capacidades institucionales de la CDAG para la planificación, ejecución, supervisión y mantenimiento de infraestructura deportiva bajo estándares de calidad, transparencia y sostenibilidad.

Para la implementación de los componentes de infraestructura, el proyecto se articula con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, que ejerce autoridad metodológica y técnica transversal en infraestructura, incluyendo estándares, metodologías, QA/QC (Quality Assurance / Quality Control), control de proyectos, revisiones técnicas y aseguramiento, conforme a la matriz institucional de roles y responsabilidades.

El/la Analista Técnico/a en Adquisiciones de Infraestructura será responsable de apoyar la planificación, estructuración y gestión de la estrategia de adquisiciones del proyecto, asegurando que los procesos de contratación reflejen adecuadamente los requerimientos técnicos, minimicen riesgos y permitan una ejecución eficiente y conforme a estándares internacionales, en coordinación con la Unidad de Adquisiciones y con base en los insumos técnicos validados por el equipo del proyecto y la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, según corresponda.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Analista Técnico/a en Adquisiciones de Infraestructura será responsable de coordinar la planificación, estructuración y gestión de los procesos de adquisiciones del proyecto, asegurando la calidad técnica, el cumplimiento de las políticas de PNUD y la adecuada gestión de riesgos a lo largo del ciclo de contratación.

El/la titular trabajará en estrecha coordinación con la Unidad de Adquisiciones del PNUD, la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, especialistas técnicos y el equipo del proyecto, sin sustituir las responsabilidades de elaboración, validación o aprobación técnica ni las atribuciones de los comités y autoridades competentes.

Funciones específicas:

1) Estrategia y Planificación de Adquisiciones

- Garantizar el desarrollo e implementación de la estrategia de adquisiciones a nivel del proyecto, en coordinación con la Unidad de Adquisiciones, incluyendo paquetes contractuales y modalidades de contratación adecuadas (RFI, RFP, ITB, IC u otros) y aplicando los estándares y lineamientos técnicos definidos por la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Alinear la estrategia con el cronograma y los hitos técnicos validados por el equipo del proyecto, articulando con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo cuando corresponda.

- Incorporar análisis de riesgos de adquisiciones, operativos y de mercado, e integrar los riesgos técnicos identificados y validados por los especialistas y la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, según corresponda. Promover enfoques que optimicen competencia, calidad y eficiencia.

2) Investigación y Análisis de Mercado

- Diseñar y conducir estudios de mercado (RFI u otros mecanismos) en coordinación con la Unidad de Adquisiciones y con participación técnica de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo cuando corresponda.

- Analizar proveedores, capacidad del mercado y niveles de competencia.

- Identificar riesgos de mercado y proponer mitigaciones.

- Facilitar la validación técnica de las soluciones por los especialistas responsables y la revisión técnica o aseguramiento de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, cuando corresponda.

- Documentar resultados para la toma de decisiones.

3) Estructuración Técnica de Procesos de Adquisición

- Preparar e integrar TDR, especificaciones técnicas y criterios de evaluación con base en insumos técnicos debidamente validados, sin sustituir la responsabilidad de los especialistas que los elaboran, revisan o aprueban.

- Verificar la calidad, claridad, consistencia y licitabilidad de los documentos desde la perspectiva de adquisiciones, y gestionar las revisiones técnicas y de aseguramiento que correspondan.

- Integrar aportes técnicos multidisciplinarios del equipo del proyecto y canalizar a la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo los documentos sujetos a revisión técnica o aseguramiento.

- Traducir requerimientos en documentos licitatorios alineados a buenas prácticas.

- Contribuir a que los criterios de evaluación sean objetivos, transparentes, verificables y consistentes con las políticas de PNUD y los requerimientos técnicos validados.

4) Coordinación con la Unidad de Adquisiciones del PNUD y Gestión de Procesos

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de las políticas y procedimientos de PNUD, bajo la autoridad procedimental de la Unidad de Adquisiciones.

- Gestionar revisiones internas y aseguramiento de calidad articulando la revisión procedimental de la Unidad de Adquisiciones y la revisión técnica o aseguramiento de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Coordinar los insumos del proyecto para la publicación de procesos, respuestas a consultas y enmiendas, cuya tramitación corresponderá a la Unidad de Adquisiciones conforme a sus atribuciones.

- Actuar como enlace técnico del proyecto, la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo y la Unidad de Adquisiciones.

- Dar seguimiento a los procesos desde la publicación hasta la adjudicación.

- Monitorear avances, riesgos y cumplimiento de plazos.

- Asegurar trazabilidad documental.

5) Evaluación de ofertas y apoyo a la adjudicación

- Participar y fortalecer la coordinación en los procesos de evaluación técnica de ofertas cuando sea formalmente designado/a, observando la segregación de funciones y las atribuciones del comité de evaluación.

- Verificar, dentro del ámbito de su competencia, la conformidad de las ofertas con los requisitos establecidos y documentar las aclaraciones o desviaciones identificadas.

- Participar en la preparación de informes y recomendaciones de adjudicación sin sustituir la deliberación, decisión ni aprobación de las instancias competentes.

- Identificar riesgos técnicos en las propuestas con el apoyo de los especialistas responsables y, cuando corresponda, de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Asegurar transparencia, objetividad y rigor técnico.

6) Estructuración contractual y gestión de cambios

- Colaborar con la definición de condiciones contractuales y asignación de riesgos en coordinación con Gestión Contractual, la Unidad de Adquisiciones y la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo en los aspectos técnicos aplicables.

- Verificar la coherencia entre documentos de licitación y contrato final, bajo la revisión y aprobación de las instancias competentes.

- Analizar las implicaciones procedimentales y contractuales de las solicitudes de cambio utilizando el sustento técnico validado por los responsables correspondientes, y determinar la ruta de tramitación aplicable.

- Integrar el expediente de sustento para modificaciones contractuales, incorporando la justificación técnica validada, el análisis de costo, plazo y riesgos, y las aprobaciones requeridas.

- Dar seguimiento a la formalización de enmiendas una vez obtenidas las revisiones y aprobaciones técnicas, programáticas, contractuales y de adquisiciones aplicables.

- Coordinar con Gestión Contractual, la Unidad de Adquisiciones, el equipo del proyecto y la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, según el ámbito de la modificación.

7) Gestión de riesgos en adquisiciones

- Identificar y analizar riesgos de adquisiciones de mercado, contractuales y operativos, e integrar los riesgos técnicos identificados por los especialistas y la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Incorporar medidas de mitigación en la planificación y ejecución.

- Dar seguimiento a riesgos durante el ciclo de contratación.

- Coordinar acciones correctivas con el equipo del proyecto y escalar a la Unidad de Adquisiciones, la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo o la gobernanza del proyecto, según la naturaleza y criticidad del riesgo.

8) Facilita la creación y el intercambio de conocimientos sobre adquisiciones en el proyecto.

- Organizar capacitaciones sobre adquisiciones para el personal del proyecto.

- Organizar capacitaciones sobre adquisiciones para proveedores en módulos de adquisiciones electrónicas.

- Sintetizar las lecciones aprendidas y las mejores prácticas en materia de adquisiciones.

- Realizar contribuciones valiosas a las redes de conocimiento y las comunidades de práctica.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

La posición reportará al/la Gerente del Proyecto y a el/la Oficial de Programa de Gobernabilidad Democrática. En materia de adquisiciones, actuará bajo la autoridad procedimental de la Unidad de Adquisiciones. En materia técnica de infraestructura, mantendrá una relación funcional de coordinación con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo y aplicará sus estándares, metodologías y lineamientos institucionales, sin modificar la línea de reporte ni la autoridad programática de la Cartera de Gobernabilidad.

Competencias

Competencias esenciales

- LOGRO DE RESULTADOS - NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

- PENSAMIENTO INNOVADOR - NIVEL 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

- APRENDIZAJE CONTINUO - NIVEL 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

- ADAPTARSE CON AGILIDAD - NIVEL 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

- ACTUAR CON DETERMINACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

- COMPROMISO Y ASOCIACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

- FAVORECE LA DIVERSIDAD Y LA INCLUSIÓN - NIVEL 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias transversales

- DIRECCIÓN Y ESTRATEGIA INSTITUCIONAL PENSAMIENTO SISTÉMICO : Capacidad para recurrir al juicio y a un análisis objetivo de problemas para comprender cómo los elementos interrelacionados coexisten dentro de un proceso o sistema general, así como para analizar cómo la alteración de un elemento puede repercutir en otras partes del sistema.

- GESTIÓN INSTITUCIONAL GESTIÓN DE RIESGOS : Identificar y organizar acciones destinadas a reducir, mitigar y gestionar riesgos de forma proactiva.

Competencias técnicas

- ADQUISICIONES GESTIÓN DE ADQUISICIONES : Capacidad de adquirir bienes, servicios y obras de una fuente externa. GESTIÓN DE CONTRATOS : Conocimiento de los conceptos, principios y métodos de la gestión de contratos, así como la capacidad de aplicarlos en situaciones estratégicas o prácticas. PROVISIÓN ESTRATÉGICA : Conocimientos de los conceptos, principios y métodos de provisión estratégica, así como capacidad para aplicarlos a situaciones estratégicas y prácticas.

Habilidades y experiencia requeridas

Educación

- Estudios universitarios avanzados (nivel de maestría o equivalente) en Gestión de Proyectos, Contratación Pública o áreas relacionadas es requerido, o

- Título universitario (nivel licenciatura) en Arquitectura, Ingeniería Civil o disciplinas afines, en combinación con dos (2) años adicionales de experiencia relevante, será considerado favorablemente en lugar de Maestría.

- El nivel 3 de CIPS es muy deseable para este puesto y los candidatos que posean este nivel en el momento de la solicitud tendrán una clara ventaja. Si la certificación deseada no está disponible en el momento de la contratación, deberá obtenerse en el plazo de un año a partir de la contratación. Los candidatos que posean una certificación CIPS de cualquier nivel inferior en el momento de la solicitud tendrán una ventaja proporcional.

Años de experiencia laboral relevante

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia (con Maestría) o 4 años de experiencia profesional relevante (con licenciatura) en: Estructuración y gestión de procesos de adquisiciones en proyectos de infraestructura, preferiblemente en organismos internacionales, banca multilateral o sistemas de cooperación internacional. Elaboración de TDR, especificaciones técnicas y documentos de licitación para proyectos de infraestructura. Evaluación técnica de ofertas y participación en procesos de adjudicación. El sector de infraestructura (desde el enfoque técnico), incluyendo diseño, ejecución o supervisión de obras.

Requisitos adicionales

- Experiencia traduciendo requerimientos técnicos de infraestructura en procesos de contratación estructurados y licitables.

- Experiencia en redacción técnica avanzada (TDR, especificaciones, criterios de evaluación).

- Experiencia en análisis crítico de propuestas técnicas y comerciales.

- Experiencia en la articulación entre equipos técnicos y áreas de adquisiciones.

Habilidades y competencias deseables

- Experiencia en infraestructura deportiva de alto rendimiento.

- Experiencia con estándares internacionales (FIFA, World Athletics u otros).

- Experiencia en proyectos con múltiples contratos ejecutándose en paralelo.

- Experiencia en coordinación con entidades regulatorias (ambientales, municipales, etc.).

Idiomas

- Fluidez en el idioma español.

Información importante para las/os postulantes

Todos los puestos en las categorías NPSA están sujetos a contratación local.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

El PNUD, como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que opera. En este sentido, se alienta a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postularse a las vacantes de la organización. Las decisiones de empleo se basan en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación de ningún tipo.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a la misión institucional, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse plenamente y acceder a oportunidades profesionales en igualdad de condiciones.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, el acoso sexual, la explotación, la discriminación ni el abuso de autoridad. Todas las personas seleccionadas estarán sujetas a verificaciones pertinentes y deberán cumplir con las normas, políticas y principios aplicables del sistema de las Naciones Unidas.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos

Se exhorta a las personas postulantes a consultar la guía del PNUD sobre el uso responsable de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos de selección y contratación.

Alerta de estafa

El PNUD no cobra ninguna tarifa en ninguna etapa de sus procesos de reclutamiento. Para mayor información, visite www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Public Outreach and Communication Analyst [Open to internal and external candidates]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Climate Change Programme of the UNDP Armenia’s Climate, Environment and Resilience Portfolio supports the Government of Armenia in implementing national climate priorities and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement. The Programme promotes climate resilience, enhanced transparency, improved air quality, and accelerated climate action through policy support, institutional capacity development, technical assistance, public awareness, and stakeholder engagement.

The Programme currently comprises the following UNDP-implemented projects:

- Multi-donor funded Armenia's component of the UNDP global initiative "Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact";

- EU-funded Joint Programme "Clean Air for Health and Green Growth in Armenia (EU4CleanAir in Armenia)";

- GEF-funded project "Development of the First Biennial Transparency Report and the combined Fifth National Communication and Second Biennial Transparency Report of Armenia to the UNFCCC";

- GEF-funded project "Strengthening the National Framework for Climate Transparency in Armenia – CBIT 2";

The Programme works closely with the Ministry of Environment of Armenia and other national stakeholders to strengthen climate governance, enhance public participation, and raise awareness of climate change and air quality issues, as well as improve environmental information systems.

Duties and Responsibilities

Communication, Visibility and Public Outreach

- Develop, implement and periodically update the projects’ communication and outreach plans whenever required, ensuring coherent communication and branding across all projects and compliance with UNDP and donor visibility requirements.

- Develop and disseminate high-quality communication products, including news stories, press releases, newsletters, success stories, fact sheets, presentations, social media content, photo and video stories, and other visibility materials.

- Maintain and regularly update Climate Change Programme website and digital communication platforms, monitor media and social media coverage, and prepare communication analytics and visibility reports.

- Contribute to knowledge management by documenting projects' achievements, lessons learned and good practices, and supporting the preparation of communication inputs for donor reports, publications and international knowledge-sharing platforms.

Media Relations, Events and Stakeholder Engagement

- Promote and disseminate advocacy materials, newsletters, publications to support projects’ activities within the assigned area of responsibility

- Ensures organization of planning, and communication of the projects’ events, including workshops, conferences, training sessions, launches, campaigns, field visits and other public outreach activities.

- Prepare event communication materials, coordinate media participation, photography and videography, and ensure effective dissemination of event outcomes through appropriate communication channels.

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with government counterparts, development partners, media representatives, civil society, academia and other stakeholders to promote projects’ objectives and achievements.

- Support awareness-raising and advocacy initiatives aimed at increasing public understanding of climate change, air quality, transparency and related environmental issues.

- Produce communication and advocacy materials for awareness-raising campaigns, including social media materials in coordination with the direct supervisor.

- Ensure all communication products comply with UNDP corporate guidelines.

Programme Support

- Provide communication support in the implementation of annual work plans and communication activities across all Climate Change Programme projects.

- Prepare Terms of Reference, technical specifications, and substantive inputs for the procurement of communication-related services and products.

- Coordinate and monitor external communication service providers, review their deliverables, provide technical feedback, and ensure quality, timely completion, and compliance with UNDP and donor communication and visibility requirements.

- Monitor the implementation of communication activities and visibility indicators, maintain communication records and visibility evidence, and contribute communication inputs to project and donor reports.

Assist country office’s knowledge management and dissemination

- Provide support to Identify and synthesize best practices and lessons learned directly linked to programme goals and activities.

- Contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice including corporate communications repositories.

- Assist in keeping the project’s Intranet up-to-date and free from unnecessary data.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Public Outreach and Communication Analyst will support the implementation of communication, visibility and public outreach activities across the Programme’s projects, ensuring coherent messaging, effective dissemination of project results, and compliance with UNDP and donor communication and visibility requirements.

Under the overall guidance of the CER Programme Analyst and direct supervision of the UNDP Climate Change Programme Manager, in close collaboration with UNDP CO Communications Analyst and Project Coordinators, the Public Outreach and Communication Analyst will support the implementation of communication, visibility and public outreach activities across the Climate Change Programme and its projects.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and onitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional and Technical Competencies:

Business Management

- Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Partnerships management Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Communications

- Social Media Management Ability to represent and promote the UNDP brand in virtual communities and networks.

General (across the functions)

- Events planning and execution Ability to plan, manage and execute of public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNDP's overall brand and mandate.

Digital

- Social media Knowledge of social media and ability to advise the use of social media for development outcomes.

- Story telling Ability to empathize with people's perceptions, motivations, feelings and mental models and craft narratives to build an emotive argument for change accordingly. Ability to present data, insights or information in compelling ways to mobilize resources, talent or action. Ability to choose media and channels that is fit for purpose to reach specific target audiences.

Business Development

- Knowledge generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Journalism, Social Media Communication, Social Media Marketing, Social Sciences or another relevant field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS’s staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP’s Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP’s development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven, including in its programme support efforts.

The Quality and Impact Hub aims to expand UNDP’s value position as an accountable, transparent and therefore trusted and neutral development partner. The Impact Hub serves as the corporate custodian and strategist driving continual improvement of UNDP’s institutional architecture that guides UNDP programming. The Impact Hub leads changes in UNDP policy instruments and quality assurance approaches to enable UNDP programming - spanning all funding sources, including core, non-core, and Vertical Funds (VFs) - that is risk-informed, agile, results-focused, and integrates social and environmental risks and opportunities. The Impact Hub brings together two existing units in BPPS: the Vertical Fund Hub (VF Hub), and the Quality Programming Team (QPT - including the Social and Environmental Team (SES) Team) to be the central pillar of trust and transparency in UNDP.

By consolidating policy custodianship, quality assurance, risk management, and results oversight, the Impact Hub will be better able to support UNDP in achieving higher accountability, fostering greater trust with partners, reducing fiduciary risks, being more adaptable, and achieving greater developmental quality and impact. A renewed focus on fit-for-purpose and relevant policies will enable and steer UNDP into new partnerships with the private sector, with IFIs, and with the VFs. The Impact Hub will also institutionalize quality assurance and oversight into UNDP, where risk management, results assurance, and policy coherence operate seamlessly through digital systems, enabling evidence-based decision-making and learning across all UNDP programming. The Impact Hub will drive continuous improvement internally while learning from external engagements with the UNDP Executive Board and Boards of the Vertical Funds amongst others to ensure UNDP remains fit-for-purpose, dynamic, agile and relevant in an ever-changing international development landscape. The Quality and Impact Hub will continue to lead UNDP’s accountability and engagement with the VFs and ensure UNDP VF programming complies with VF policies and requirements, as well as continue to provide financial oversight of VF programming to ensure VF funds are used for their intended purpose as required by the VFs and VF fiduciary management, reporting and auditing as mandated by the VFs.

Position Purpose:

The Programme Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Director, Quality and Impact Hub to provide data-driven analyses, including on VF performance and resource mobilization, operational support and coordinate integrated programme support across the three sub-teams of the Quality and Impact Hub. The Programme Analyst will work in close collaboration with BPPS HQ colleagues, Regional Bureaus, VF Secretariats and other teams/bureaus and external partners, where required, to address programme-related and operations-related issues and to ensure consistent and high-quality service delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1-Programme Support and Knowledge Management

- Provide support to the various initiatives overseen by the Quality and Impact Hub, including relationship management with the Vertical Funds.

- Coordinate Hub contributions to UNDP internal work planning, annual performance reports, and other internal communication.

- Support coordination of the Quality and Impact Hub with the Planet Hub and Regional Bureaus;

- Support risk reporting to the VF Secretariats;

- Organize meetings, including planning and logistics as needed;

- Prepare correspondence, directives, and comments on behalf of the Director for signature and follow-up when required;

- Prepare and/or compile relevant background materials, briefing notes, presentations, reports, and/or talking points as needed

- Substantively review and critically analyze key documents to ensure all briefs and presentations are complete and accurate;

2-VF Hub data management, use and quality control

- Support all aspects of the vertical fund portfolio risk management globally through anticipatory action, proactive monitoring, data mining and producing analyses of VF business intelligence and business processes, pipeline management and overall workflow;

- Assist with the management of the VF portfolio and pipeline, including tracking and monitoring of key deadlines

- Undertake analyses of data and information from PIMS+, compiling syntheses, reports, charts, tables, graphs, presentations, etc. as required

- Undertake analyses of data and information in Quantum to ensure alignment with PIMS+ as needed

- Support the management of the VF intranet space, and PIMS+ as needed.

- Maintain informal communication channels and networks with BPPS (Planet Hub) colleagues and region-based technical teams to facilitate high-quality data entry and use of PIMS

- Manage standard information flows and protocols between UNDP and the VF Secretariats

- Manage UNDP access and user rights to the VF information portals, follow VF portal updates, and ensure UNDP colleagues are fully informed/trained as appropriate

- Manage quality assurance of UNDP data entered in the VF information portals

- Support with the timely preparation and signature of VF Delegations of Authority, financial authorizations, legal agreements and other relevant documentation for approved Vertical Fund Projects.

3-Administrative Support and Operations

- Coordinate and plan all aspects of the missions for Quality & Impact Hub as requested by the supervisor. This includes: formulating mission travel plans, obtaining management approval, verifying travel budget, obtaining travel authorization, submitting completed travel settlement forms and maintaining files;

- Liaise with the official UNDP travel agency on travel authorizations and issuance of tickets;

- Process travel transactions, handle claims, refunds, reconciliations, and settlements in UNall and Quantum;

- Provide administrative support to conferences, workshops, and retreats upon assignment;

- Oversee logistics, documentation, preparation/review of budget and authorization of expenses;

- Provide budget planning, monitoring, and financial oversight support, including budget revisions in Quantum, budget tracking, and management of budget and contract monitoring tools;

- Coordinate closely with centralized Business Solutions Hub;

- Identify and execute opportunities to improve operational efficiency for the Hub

4-Facilitate knowledge building and management.

- Identify policy-driven issues; and identify and compile best practices and lessons learned directly linked to the operations of the Hub.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks, communities of practice, and digital knowledge platforms.

Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Background

Tanzania has maintained relative peace and stability for decades, positioning itself as a beacon of harmony in the region. However, emerging socio-economic and environmental challenges such as youth unemployment, climate-induced stresses, and localized tensions pose risks to this stability. With over 60% of the population under 25, young people represent both a demographic dividend and a potential source of vulnerability. Their meaningful engagement in peacebuilding is critical to sustaining peace and achieving inclusive development. The Tanzania Development Vision 2050 identifies Governance, Peace, Security, and Stability as its foundational pillar, emphasizing good governance, justice, and strong local governance. In 2025, UNDP, in collaboration with the Government of Tanzania, supported by the UN Peace and Development Trust Fund—the Secretary General’s Peace and Security Sub-Fund, has officially launched the second phase of the Dumisha Amani project. This new phase aims to deepen peace building, strengthen community resilience, and unlock inclusive development across Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar. The project is implemented with in collaboration with key partners, including the President’s Office – Youth Development (PO-YD) in Tanzania Mainland, the Second Vice President’s Office (SVPO) in Zanzibar, civil society and youth-led and community-based organizations.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Work closely with UNDP technical teams to ensure effective coordination, quality assurance, and timely delivery of Dumisha Amani II activities.

Multi-Stakeholder Coordination & Partnership Management

- Facilitate coordination between UNDP, government institutions, CSOs, community structures, and development partners.

- Provide technical inputs to strengthen multi-stakeholder collaboration across Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar.

- Lead stakeholder consultations, interviews, meetings, and organize validation workshops for priorities and proposed interventions.

Peace for Infrastructure Strengthening

- Support capacity-building activities for community policing structures and other local peace mechanisms to enhance their effectiveness in addressing community security and peacebuilding challenges.

- Support the establishment, strengthening, and operationalization of community policing initiatives as platforms for enhancing community safety, social cohesion, and trust between communities and law enforcement agencies.

Peacebuilding Action Plans Support

- Provide technical leadership and coordination support for the implementation and monitoring of the National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security (NAP-YPS).

- Facilitate and provide technical guidance to government and community stakeholders in the development, review, and implementation of Community Peacebuilding Action Plans.

- Support consultations, stakeholder engagement, and capacity-building initiatives to ensure inclusive and evidence-based peacebuilding planning processes.

5.Peace and development Nexus Improving

- Support the establishment, operationalization, and sustainability of youth centres as platforms for youth engagement, social cohesion, peacebuilding, skills development, and community resilience.

- Provide technical assistance to government counterparts, local authorities, and community stakeholders in integrating peacebuilding approaches into development planning and implementation processes.

- Contribute to capacity-building, knowledge-sharing, and evidence generation on effective approaches for linking peacebuilding and development interventions.

6.Gender Equality Integration

- Ensure all Dumisha Amani II interventions fully integrate gender equality principles.

- Promote meaningful engagement of young women and girls through gender-responsive tools, training modules, and monitoring approaches.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP supports countries in achieving sustainable and inclusive human development by helping them eradicate poverty in all its forms, accelerate structural transformations for sustainable development, and build resilience to crises and shocks. UNDP partners with people at all levels of society to help build nations that can withstand crisis, and that drive and sustain the kind of growth that improves the quality of life for everyone.

The Kingdom of Morocco has embarked on an ambitious development trajectory anchored in the New Development Model (NMD), and key reform agendas such as on social protection and advanced regionalization, well aligned with implementation of the 2030 Agenda. The country has positioned itself as a regional leader in climate ambition, digital transformation, financing for development (FfD), including through its active engagement in the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4) and the Compromiso de Sevilla, and South-South and triangular cooperation.

Within this context, UNDP Morocco's Programme is structured around three integrated pillars (Governance, Planet, Prosperity). The Prosperity Pillar focuses on inclusive economic transformation, decent work and employment, social protection, financing for sustainable development, human capital, and the territorialization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with a strong emphasis on leaving no one behind and reaching the most vulnerable populations and territories.

To scale up delivery of its inclusive growth portfolio in line with national priorities, UNDP Morocco is recruiting an Inclusive Growth Coordinator at the NPSA-9 level. Under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, and under the direct supervision of the Programme Analyst of the Prosperity Pillar, the Coordinator will provide substantive coordination, programmatic and policy advisory support across a portfolio covering inclusive growth, poverty reduction and employment, social protection, health and development, and financing for development, with a particular emphasis on the local and territorial level.

Scope of Work

The Inclusive Growth Coordinator will lead the coordination, technical backstopping and policy positioning of UNDP Morocco's inclusive growth portfolio, ensuring substantive coherence, quality assurance, and integrated programming across thematic areas. The Inclusive Growth Coordinator will work closely with the Programme Analyst of the Prosperity Pillar, Project Managers, Programme Analysts, the and counterparts in Government, the UN Country Team, Development Partners, the private sector, academia and civil society.

Under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, and direct supervision of the Programme Analyst of the Prosperity pillar, the Inclusive Growth Coordinator will drive the following key functions:

A. Ensure portfolio coordination, quality assurance and strategic positioning

- Coordinate the implementation, monitoring and reporting of the inclusive growth portfolio, ensuring alignment with the Country Programme Document (CPD), the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), Agenda 2030 and the Sustainable Development Goals and other internationally agreed development goals, the “Nouveau Modèle de Développement” (NMD) and Morocco's national priorities.

- Provide substantive backstopping and quality assurance to project managers and analysts working on poverty, employment, private sector development, social protection, health and Financing for Development (FfD), including review of workplans, narrative and financial reports, results frameworks and donor deliverables.

- Lead integrated programming across the portfolio, identifying synergies between projects and with the Planet and Governance pillars, and cross-cutting accelerators (digital, innovation, gender, youth).

- Contribute to the design of new initiatives and concept notes, including project documents, theories of change, results and resources frameworks, and risk and stakeholder analyses, in line with UNDP's programme and operations policies and procedures (POPP) and Social and Environmental Standards (SES).

- Support the Programme Analyst and senior management in positioning UNDP as a strategic partner of choice on inclusive growth, including by drafting strategic notes, briefings, talking points, op-eds and policy papers for the Resident Representative, the Deputy Resident Representative and the Team Leader.

B. Ensure substantive coordination and programming across thematic areas

- Provide substantive coordination, programmatic and policy advisory support across the thematic scope of the inclusive growth portfolio, ensuring evidence-based, integrated and territorially-grounded programming. The portfolio covers (and are not limited to) the following key thematic areas, with a particular focus on the local and territorial level:

- Inclusive growth, poverty reduction and inequalities, including multidimensional poverty (MPI), the leaving-no-one-behind (LNOB) agenda, territorial disparities, and the operationalization of the New Development Model.

- Decent work and productive employment, including youth employment, women's economic empowerment, the social and solidarity economy (SSE), MSMEs and entrepreneurship ecosystems, skills development, and integrated local economic development (LED).

- Social protection, including the generalization of universal health coverage (AMO), family allowances, pensions and unemployment insurance; adaptive, climate- and shock-responsive social protection; and the financing, governance and equity of social protection systems.

- Health and development, including health systems strengthening and health financing, the social determinants of health, climate and health, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and non-communicable diseases, and inclusive and rights-based approaches to health.

- Financing for sustainable development with a strong territorial focus, including the Integrated National Financing Framework (INFF, and ILFF), domestic resource mobilization and Tax for SDGs, sub-national and municipal finance, SDG-aligned budgeting, blended and innovative finance, insurance and risk finance, public-private partnerships, diaspora financing and SDG Investor Maps, in line with the Compromiso de Sevilla.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

In Ghana, UNCDF is managing a portfolio of projects focused on youth empowerment, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) finance and climate finance for a total portfolio of 10M USD. Under this framework UNCDF team is supporting a wide range of service providers from public and private sector to design and pilot new business models to increase access and usage of digital services for the most vulnerable segments (youth, women, MSMEs in particular).

UNCDF will be specifically in charge of supporting the ecosystem and Small and Growing Companies (SGCs) and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) in accessing finance through different interventions, such as (but not limited to):

- Support service providers that can better equip these Small and Growing Companies (SGCs) and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) in using digital solutions to better access financial services

- Support key policy makers to provide enabling environment for the financial services and investments that target the Small and Growing Companies (SGCs) and Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)

By helping companies grow their businesses, achieve commercial sustainability, strengthen their balance sheets, and build credit history, UNCDF aims to unlock further private capital to companies that serve last mile communities, to scale up what works and to foster local economic development.

UNCDF is seeking a candidate to lead the technical implementation of investment readiness and pipeline development activities, supporting micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), financial institutions, and ecosystem partners to become investment-ready and access appropriate financing solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Investment Specialist will work under the direct supervision of UNCDF Programme Management Specialist in Ghana and guided by the UNCDF Regional Investment Specialist.Under the supervision of the UNCDF Programme Management Specialist based in Accra and in close collaboration with other colleagues in-country as well as the Regional Office (Dakar, Senegal), the Investment Specialist will contribute to capital deployment and delivery of investment transactions, with particular focus on Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) finance.

The Investment Specialist will be responsible for leading and executing the following tasks and deliverables:

1. Pipeline Development & Partner Identification

- Develop and adapt pipeline-sourcing approaches for the Ghanaian market and maintain a documented pipeline of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), financial institutions and ecosystem partners, with updates provided at least monthly against agreed work-plan targets.

- Identify and build a pipeline of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), financial institutions, and ecosystem partners with potential for financing.

- Conduct initial screening and segmentation of partners based on investment readiness levels and financing needs.

- Support the design and implementation of calls for applications (RFAs) and pipeline sourcing strategies.

- Conduct detailed due diligence on the identified investees, covering financial, operational, legal, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) dimensions.

2. Investment Readiness & Technical Assistance

- Assess gaps in financial management, governance, business models, and digital capabilities affecting investment readiness.

- Design and coordinate tailored technical assistance (TA) interventions to improve bankability of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs)and partner institutions.

- Provide hands-on advisory support on financial structuring, record-keeping, business planning, and creditworthiness.

- Work with service providers (e.g. incubators, digital solution providers) to deliver targeted capacity building.

- Contribute to the preparation of investment cases and basic financial models to facilitate financing decisions.

- Liaise with UNCDF investment team and external financiers to align pipeline with available instruments.

3. Ensure Stakeholder Engagement

- Engage financial institutions, fintechs, crowdfunding platforms, and DFIs to connect investment-ready entities with financing opportunities.

- Support collaboration with regulators and government stakeholders to address systemic barriers affecting access to finance.

4. Ecosystem Coordination

- Facilitate partnerships between micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), financial service providers, and ecosystem actors.

- Design and support the organization of investment-focused events, such as investor roundtables, pitch sessions, and matchmaking forums, to connect MSMEs and financial institutions. Add value to investment-related events by facilitating discussions, showcasing pipeline opportunities, and strengthening linkages between investees and financiers.

5. Monitoring, Learning & Reporting

- Track progress of supported partners along the investment readiness pathway.

- Document lessons learned and contributed to knowledge products on SME financing and investment readiness.

- Work with the monitoring and evaluation personnels to track the progress of partners against the KPIs and corporate indicators

6. Facilitate knowledge sharing

- Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application.

Background

The ongoing crisis in Myanmar is a complex mix of political and economic crises that is exacerbating, and escalating humanitarian and human development needs and has already placed basic needs of the people at risk. After a decade of strong economic growth, the recent political setbacks coupled with the impact of the global COVID-19 pandemic, threaten Myanmar’s chances of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). A recent UNDP report (April 2021) warns that up to 25 million people (48.2% of the population) may end up below the poverty line by early 2022. These estimates were further confirmed in UNDP’s latest survey that shows that urban poverty will triple, and rural poverty increase by a third. Furthermore, after a period of relative peace, contested ethnic areas— in particular Chin, Kayah, Kachin and Shan states and Sagaing region—have witnessed a resumption in armed conflict. The formal peace process is considered stalled, and 295,000 people have been displaced by insecurity since February 2021, adding to the 370,000 people already displaced by conflict before 2021 (UNOCHA Myanmar Humanitarian Snapshot, December 2021). The consequences of these trends are catastrophic. Major gains over the past 10 years on good governance and economic inclusion are at risk. This context, and the uncertain political situation in Myanmar is driving a simultaneous humanitarian and development crisis that threatens hard-won socio-economic gains.

While meeting critical and immediate humanitarian needs where they appear is vital, these actions must be underpinned by simultaneous efforts to address rapidly growing multi-dimensional vulnerabilities, enhance resilience to shocks, protect development gains and invest in local capacities of civil society as an important agent of change in sustainable development. Furthermore, urgent efforts are needed to protect basic human rights like education, health, work, housing and food, to address exclusion, intergenerational poverty that will further exacerbate the crises. In response to the current context and challenges UNDP has launched a number of initiatives under the “Community First Programme” that aims to enhance resilience of vulnerable communities by working directly at the community level.
