Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

This vacancy is open to nationals or holders of residence permits for the respective country.

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

The Regional Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean (RBLAC) covers 26 Country Offices and one Regional Service Centre. In total RBLAC covers over 40 country programmes. Across Latin America and the Caribbean, UNDP helps countries build and share their own solutions to urgent development challenges, supporting coalitions for change and connecting individuals and institutions so they can share knowledge, experience and resources. As countries develop local capacity, they draw on the people of UNDP and our wide range of regional and global partners. The regional priorities include democratic governance, sustainable development, reducing inequalities, disaster and conflict risk reduction and the advancement of women, among others.

As part of UNDP’s organizational optimization exercise and broader efforts to strengthen regional delivery and country support functions, the position of Deputy Assistant Administrator and Deputy Regional Director for the Regional Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean (RBLAC) has been relocated from New York to Panama.

This strategic repositioning reflects UNDP’s corporate commitment to bringing senior leadership closer to country operations, regional implementation mechanisms, and country-support platforms. Based in Panama, the Deputy Regional Director will oversee the operation and functioning of the Regional Hub and provide closer leadership, coordination, and oversight of regional support services to Country Offices across Latin America and the Caribbean. It is intended to strengthen alignment between corporate decision-making and operational realities on the ground; enhance responsiveness to Country Office needs; improve integration between policy, programme, and operations support functions; and facilitate more effective engagement with regional stakeholders and partners. The Panama-based leadership structure will also reinforce coordination with the Bureau’s Country Support Unit and Regional Hub teams to ensure timely, integrated, and high-quality support to Country Offices in delivering UNDP’s Strategic Plan and regional priorities.

Duties and Responsibilities

The overall purpose of this post is to ensure that the Deputy Regional Director receive the immediate administrative and operational support they need to concentrate on their managerial, representational and oversight functions. The position provides high-level executive, administrative and operational support to the Deputy Regional Director and, as required, coordinated support to the RBLAC Directorate in its day-to-day management of the Bureau, applying administrative rules and regulations and establishing internal operational procedures to enable the smooth functioning of the Deputy Director’s office. The incumbent works in close collaboration with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Regional Director, the Executive Associate to the Regional Director in NY, the Executive Associate(s) in Panama, and relevant Bureau and Regional Hub teams to contribute to coherent and well-coordinated support across the Directorate.

The incumbent coordinates closely with the Executive Associate to the Regional Director in New York and provides reciprocal backstopping (virtually), as required, to ensure business continuity and the smooth functioning of the Directorate.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1. Ensures effective and efficient functioning of the office of the RBLAC Deputy Director, focusing on achievement of the following results:

• In coordination with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director, management of the schedule/calendar for the RBLAC Director with external and internal parties;

• Coordinates and processes official travel arrangements for the Deputy Regional Director and, if required, for other RBLAC Directorate or Bureau’s staff, ensuring compliance with UNDP travel policies and coordination with other travel partners from the internal or external environment;

• Coordination with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director and with other Regional Hub and Bureau staff for the timely preparation of high-quality briefing materials for appointments, meetings, missions;

• In coordination with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director, management of the RBLAC Deputy Director´s extensive mission and representation schedule. Understanding of all protocol procedures and ensuring that procedures are fully implemented with respect to all visitors and guests of the Bureau;

• Use of office management systems for effective functioning of the RBLAC Deputy Director’s office, including maintenance of rosters of high-level partners, telephone and contact lists, maintenance and use of automated filing systems and ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials.

2. Ensures effective communications support to the RBLAC Deputy Director, focusing on achievement of the following results:

• Coordinates the flow of information from the RBLAC Deputy Director’s office to other RBLAC units at the Regional Hub, Headquarters and in the field, other UNDP and UN units; identification of opportunities to improve or streamline information flow and communications channels in the office including through innovative IT solutions;

• Liaises in a timely manner with all RBLAC units to ensure that the RBLAC Deputy Director’s decisions, instructions and requests for action and information are communicated to the correct people for follow-up actions;

• Self-directed and timely follow-up with all units on actions expected by the RBLAC Deputy Director;

• Reviews of incoming correspondence for the RBLAC Deputy Director´s attention and prioritizing of documents according to action required;

• Reviews, proofreads and edits of all correspondence for proper clearance prior to the RBLAC Deputy Director’s signature, ensuring quality control, substance, sensitivity of issues, and compliance with UNDP standards;

• Directs queries to appropriate party or substantive focal points within RBLAC for responses;

• Presents proposals to eliminate communication bottlenecks in the office and streamline communication procedures between the Directorate and other internal and external units;

• Drafts and prepares correspondence, directives, comments on behalf of the RBLAC Deputy Director for his/her signature and ensuring follow-up as needed;

• Assists in the organization of Directorate’s meetings and tracking follow-up actions.

3. Provides administrative support to effective advocacy of UNDP and RBLAC activities under the guidance of the Deputy Regional Director and in close coordination with the RBLAC Directorate, focusing on achievement of the following results:

• Supports the Directorate in facilitating the Bureau’s interaction (in sensitive, political, diplomatic, others) with various external partners of RBLAC, such as ambassadors, donor country delegations, parliamentarians and high-level senior officials, as well as the Administrator and the Executive Office.

• Assists in the maintenance of information on the Directorate staff activities;

• Assists the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director in the research, obtaining and analysis of background materials for the preparation of the briefings, meetings, official missions and appointments.

• Assists in the preparation of public information materials and folders, as requested.

• Assists in the organization of official hospitality events on behalf of RBLAC.

4. Provides administrative support to the Deputy Regional Director and Regional Hub senior management staff, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Applies ‘best practices’ with respect to administrative, procedures, rules, regulations and systems, and introduction of relevant proposals for their eventual application in the functioning of the RBLAC Deputy Regional Director’s office;

- Organizes and schedules meetings originated by RBLAC, including reservation of room, notification to attendees, logistics; preparation of agenda; organization and distribution of key documentation.

- Drafts/revises meeting minutes.

- Processes travel requests in line with UNDP Travel Policy.

- Calculates DSA entitlements and processes claims, ensuring the timely settlement of claims;

- Provides administrative support to conferences, workshops, retreats organized by RBLAC.

5. Ensures facilitation of knowledge building and management, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Conducts research on various work-related subjects at the request of the RBLAC Deputy Director, in collaboration with the Special Assistant;

- Contributes to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Ensures availability of coverage and reciprocal backstopping for the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director and Executive Associate to the Director (virtually) during peak times.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

- Business Management & Strategy - Customer Satisfaction/Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Business Development - Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- General (across the functions) - Event planning and execution: Ability to plan, manage and execute of public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNDP's overall brand and mandate.

- Business Management - Results-based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- Administration & Operations - Travel policy and procedures: Knowledge of travel policy and procedures; ability to interpret travel policy, the Staff Rules, administrative circulars and financial regulations and rules on travel related matters.

- Business Management - Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

• Secondary Education is required with specialized secretarial training, OR

• University Degree in Social Sciences, Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance or equivalent will be given due consideration, but is not a requirement.

• Minimum 7 years (with secondary education) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible administrative, executive support or programme experience at the national or international level is required.

• Experience using computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and in handling web-based management systems is required.

• Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized.

• Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability.

South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture.

You are invited to join a team of future-smart development professionals to support India in achieving the national and globally agreed goals. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with diverse stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to sustainable development and reach those furthest behind first.

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The Action for Climate and Environment (ACE) Unit at UNDP is organized around the thematic areas of climate change adaptation and mitigation, natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem & land restoration, disaster management and resilience, and access to clean and efficient energy.

The Natural Resource Management and Biodiversity pillar of ACE is supporting the Government of India in meeting national development objectives along with commitments under important multilateral environment agreements especially the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). The programme/projects under the pillar have been supporting the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEFCC), National and State level planning for land restoration and biodiversity conservation, habitat restoration, carbon sequestration through enhanced restoration, promotion of nature-based livelihoods and One Health approach.

UNDP is supporting the Ministry in the implementation of a GEF -7 project “Sustainable management and restoration of degraded landscapes for achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) in India”. The project aims to achieve land degradation neutrality by creating additional carbon sinks through an ecosystem-based approach for restoring degraded agricultural, forest, pastoral lands, and surface water bodies. It involves enabling institutional frameworks and policies for integrated sustainable land management practices and up-scaling landscape-wide practices in 3 states Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh contributing to the national target of restoring 26 Mha of degraded lands by 2030.

The project being implemented over a period of five years will lead to the following outcomes: (1) Enhanced national, state and district-level enabling frameworks incentivizing SLM practices and supporting participatory multi-sector platforms to avoid, reduce and reverse land degradation, biodiversity loss and climate mitigation; (2) Integrated participatory landscape design and financing models established in support of avoidance, reduction and reversal of land degradation, desertification, biodiversity loss and negative impacts of climate change to generates multiple sustained environmental and economic benefits; (3) Improved capacity for LDN monitoring, assessment and reporting to UNCCD in support of LDN target setting and evaluation of capacities of partners; allowing government institutions and other agencies to better document, analyse and disseminate effective intervention strategies for restoring productive landscapes and replication of best practices at national and state level, and at international level through improved South-South cooperation, knowledge and adaptive management.

UNDP seeks to engage a State Project Coordinator who will support the National Project Manager (NPM) in the implementation of the GEF-GoI-UNDP LDN project. S/he will also work closely with the NPMU, SPMU, LPMU and UNDP in the implementation of the project in the state. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic, motivated, and committed to making a positive contribution to development in India.

3. Job Purpose and Scope of Work

Main Purpose:

The State Project Coordinator will work under the supervision and guidance of the National Project Manager (NPM), NPMU and State Project Management Unit (SPMU). S/he will work closely with National Project Management Unit (NPMU) and Landscape Project Management Unite (LPMU) in the implementation of the project in the project state. S/he will have the following responsibilities:

Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Project Planning, Management and Implementation including support on Monitoring and Evaluation

• Support / Assist in planning, coordination, implementation and monitoring of the project to ensure that its results are in accordance with the project document and project results framework in the state.

• Assume full responsibility of project management on a daily basis in the state – budgeting, ensure adequate information flow, discussion and feedback among relevant stakeholders of the project.

• Develop state specific annual work plans and ensure accurate and timely reporting to MoEFCC and UNDP for activities of the project in the state.

• Guide the team at the landscape level and monitor the work undertaken by consultants employed under the project.

• Assist the NPMU/SPMU/UNDP in independent Mid-term and Terminal Evaluation of the project.

2. Stakeholder Coordination, Partnerships and Convergence and Resource Movilization

• Ensure regular communication and coordination with the National Project Management Unit, State Project Steering Committee, Landscape Level Committee and Management Unit, UNDP and MoEFCC with respect to project activities in the state.

• Foster partnerships with relevant line departments and technical institutions working on land and forest management and sustainable livelihood to bring convergence in the project.

• Organize, facilitate and participate in the periodic review meetings including State Project Steering Committee and State Technical Committee meetings at least once or twice, per year, subject to availability of members and follow up on decisions taken at such meetings.

• Coordinate with other state departments to ensure convergence and sharing knowledge and best practices learnt in the project landscapes for scale up and replication.

• Coordinate with NPMU and LPMU under the project to share lessons and experiences.

• Develop proposals for resource mobilization to augment support to the programme/project.

3. Procurement, Contract and Operational Management

• Develop Terms of Reference for hiring / engagements of consultants/ institutions/consultancy firms to be hired to undertake project activities and help the state government/UNDP in contracting processes.

• Commission activities including research studies, state level assessments, conduct and impart training / workshops etc. and manage the operational aspects of procurement, event management, logistics etc. in coordination with the state nodal officer and UNDP.

• Manage and track contracts with project partners and flag any potential risks and suggest its mitigation measures. Ensure timely contract management and payments.

• Review quality and consistency of reports and deliverables by partner institutions/ responsible parties including financial reports from all project partners.

4. Financial Management and Reporting

• Track and manage project expenditure in the state in accordance with the budget, financial rules and procedures of the State, MoEFCC and UNDP to ensure transparency, responsibility and timely achievement of project targets.

• Develop and ensure timely submission of Quarterly Progress Reports, Annual Progress Reports, Project Implementation Report and mid-term progress reports to NPMU and UNDP, based on inputs from the landscape and state.

5. Knowledge Management, Learning and Documentation

• Help in identification and documentation of best practices across thematic areas relevant to the project.

• Coordinate with NPMU and LPMU under the project to share lessons and experiences.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

Reporting To: National Project Manager (NPM), NPSA 10

Repotees to this position (if applicable): Landscape Project Officer (3 positions)- UNV, Community Mobilizer- UNV.

5. Competencies:

Core:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplify processes, balance speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/ is open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others, and support their learning

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/ partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management Competencies:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site. (PeopleManagementCompetencies.pdf)

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Thematic Area: Business Direction and Strategy

Name: Strategic Thinking

Definition: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Thematic Area: Business Management

Name: Project Management

Definition: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Thematic Area: Business Management

Name: Risk Management

Definition: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks.

Thematic Area: 2030 Agenda: Planet

Name: Nature

Definition: Ecosystems and Biodiversity: Natural Resource Management

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements:

• Secondary education is required.

• A university degree (bachelor´s degree) in Environmental Science/Forestry/ Agriculture/ Sustainable Development/ Social Sciences/ Public Policy/ Management or equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

7. Min. years of relevant work experience:

• Minimum of 7 years (with secondary education) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, social development, or any other related fields.

8. Required skills:

• Demonstrated technical experience in sustainable land management and socio-economic development, with experience coordinating with government agencies, stakeholders, and Project Management Units (PMUs).

• Experience in preparing technical reports, strategic plans, and progress updates for government and other key stakeholders.

9. Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

• Demonstrated experience in leading technical teams and facilitating consultations with government stakeholders to support project implementation, monitoring and evaluation, coordination, and achievement of project objectives and targets.

• Hands-on technical experience in the implementation and monitoring of development, environmental, or natural resource management projects.

• Experience working with Central and/or State Government departments, UN agencies, international organizations, or similar institutions, including coordination with government,

10. Required Language(s):

• Fluency in English and Hindi or Marathi is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

jobs.title: Security Operations Centre Assistant
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

The Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) is responsible for providing leadership, operational support, and oversight of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) globally. As a global leader in security risk management principles, UNDSS enables the safe and effective delivery of United Nations programmes and activities in the most complex and challenging environments, while maximizing precious resources, To this end, the work of the Department is aligned under a clear mission, to enable United Nations system programme activities through trusted security leadership and solutions. This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic, and exciting organization gaining unique and valuable experience where security provides great value. Besides the opportunity to gain new skills and further advance security expertise, this position offers a fulfilling environment that gives you satisfaction by contributing directly or indirectly to peace and security, human rights, and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. For more information on the Department, and how we make an impact on the world in enabling the achievement of SDGs, visit https://www.un.org/undss.

UNDSS Sudan is supporting the UN entities and International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) and International Organizations (IOS) so as to enable the conduct of humanitarian relief programmes. UNDSS seeks to fill a number of posts across Sudan. Successful candidates must be able to work within one of these locations. Additionally, successful candidates must be prepared to relocate to other parts of the country and travel on official business, based on evolving humanitarian planning in Sudan.

Scope of Work

The Security Operations Centre Assistant (SOC Assistant) works in close collaboration with the UNDSS Field Security Coordination Officers/ Field Security Associates and other UN personnel (especially Security Wardens) in providing support on telecommunications-related issues.

Duties and Responsibilities

The key functions will include:

- Support daily operations:

- Professionally operate and communicate using UN standard telecommunications facilities, including VHF and HF radio networks, to receive dispatch and relay messages as required.

- Answer all calls, whether on radio or telephone, promptly and efficiently.

- Maintain radio contact with all radio users, stations, and vehicles operating on the United Nations inter-agency radio network(s) under their responsibility.

- Maintain regular communications with staff in the field and HQ, utilizing HF / VHF / Sat phone or any other forms of telecommunication’s equipment and methods at your disposal.

- Track all missions and advise on all security-related issues.

- Provide initial response to all emergency communications to the radio room as appropriate.

- Monitor the news 24/7 and report security incidents and any accident involving UN staff.

2. Ensure information-sharing:

- Advise all concerned staff members of important incoming radio messages.

- Type, distribute, and respond by a variety of means - email, phone, messenger - and log accurately all incoming/outgoing radio/phone messages to concerned personnel to keep a detailed record of all radio traffic, telephone, and messenger messages that pass through the radio room.

- Disseminate security information and advisories to all agency security officers and security focal points.

- Ensure efficient communications and information flow for all units and agencies.

3. Monitor compliance with security communications system protocols:

- Ensure all network users are complying with standard radio procedures, and call signs and radio discipline are strictly maintained.

- Implement standard UN Call sign systems, vehicle tracking procedures, and Standard Operating Procedures at all radio rooms.

4. Support information management:

- Have access to Electronic Daily Staff List at all times. In case of an emergency immediately inform the Field Security Coordination Officers and the radio room supervisor and act accordingly.

- Ensure the radio room has updated staff lists with contact details, and vehicle lists.

- Establish daily contact with UNAFP security to confirm any changes in UN staff movements within their area of responsibility before staff starts the mission.

- Maintain strict confidentiality of all relevant messages sent and received through the radio room communications systems.

5. Ensure functional operability of the SOC:

- Ensure radio rooms are adequately equipped and have up-to-date documentation.

- Maintain properly all radio networks and communications equipment at the user level, reporting problems promptly to relevant staff.

- Analyse the communications requirements, recommend new systems and/or enhancements in the functionality of the existing systems.

- Immediately advise the radio room supervisor or Field Security Coordination Officers on faults in the telecommunications networks and undertake all necessary action to provide a prompt re-establishment of service.

- Assist the ICT officer in the installation and arrangement of equipment and fixtures where needed.

- Provide basic technical support for communications equipment in the field.

6. Perform other functions as may be required:

- Train UN’s implementing partners on a per-need basis and as time permits.

- Work closely with other agencies telecoms services.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL l: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL l: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL l: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity and uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL l: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL l: Appreciates/respects differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination.

Cross-functional & Technical competencies

Business Management:

Digital Awareness and Literacy.

Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skilfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Business Management:

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management.

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Security Services:

Security Incident Management & Monitoring:

Ability to provide adequate response to security incidents/events.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Completed secondary education. Certificate in radio telecommunications is an added value.

Experience:

- A minimum of 4 years (with secondary education) and 1 year (with a Bachelor’s degree) of experience in radio communications. Good knowledge of computer applications (MS Office, Internet).

- Knowledge of hardware installation and maintenance is desirable.

- Experience as radio operator, call agent or related is desirable.

- Excellent knowledge of Codan VHF and Motorola VHF systems, knowledge of Selective calling and SELV- and programming of the same is required.

Required skills:

Strong computer skills, including proficiency in MS Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Previous UN experience.

- Proficiency in operating HF and VHF radios.

- Familiarity with the host country's safety regulations.

- Valid driver's licence.

- Willingness to travel.

- Physical fitness.

Required language(s):

Fluency in English and Arabic is required.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

jobs.title: Chief Technical Specialist - Baghdad (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Iraq is recognized as one of the most affected countries by the harmful effects of climate change. Iraq ratified the Paris Agreement on January 14, 2021. In October 2021, the Government of Iraq (GoI) signed their first National Determined Contribution (NDC), which has been presented at the COP26. The Government of Iraq has requested UNDP support in implementation of the NDC, including through capacity development, advisory for sectoral planning and formulation of related strategies, frameworks, and instruments.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels offers a spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in UNDP's Strategic Plan.

UNDP is an accredited Implementing Agency for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Trust Fund and the family of funds such as the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Special Climate Change Fund (SCCF), and the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBBF). As an Implementing Agency, UNDP offers countries highly specialized services for eligibility assessment, project formulation and due diligence, co-financing mobilization, implementation oversight, results management and evaluation, and knowledge management.

Iraq faces significant environmental and public health risks associated with persistent organic pollutants (POPs), hazardous chemicals, obsolete pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), unintentional POPs (UPOPs), industrial POPs (IPOPs), and chemically contaminated sites. Previous assessments identified substantial quantities of obsolete pesticides and potentially PCB-contaminated electrical equipment and highlighted significant technical and institutional capacity gaps in chemicals and contaminated-sites management.

The Government of Iraq is a Party to major international chemicals and waste conventions, including the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and Minamata Conventions. Iraq has previously developed a National Implementation Plan (NIP) under the Stockholm Convention; however, the existing NIP requires updating to reflect newly listed POPs, improved inventories, updated risk information, institutional developments and current national priorities.

The Integrated Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and Chemical Hotspots Management Project, therefore adopts an integrated approach combining:

- strengthening the national framework for POPs and hazardous chemicals management;

- updating the national POPs inventories and National Implementation Plan;

- strengthening laboratory, inspection, monitoring and institutional capacities;

- environmentally sound management and disposal of obsolete pesticides;

- management and disposal/phase-out of PCB-contaminated equipment, oils and waste; and

- assessment and remediation planning for priority chemical pollution hotspots

The project comprises three components. Component 1 focuses on improved management of POPs and hazardous chemicals; Component 2 focuses on high-risk POPs in the agriculture and power sectors; and Component 3 addresses chemical pollution hotspots and contaminated sites.

Implementation will require extensive technical assistance, consultancy services, procurement of laboratory and field equipment, hazardous waste management services, capacity building, site assessments, remediation planning and policy/regulatory development.

Scope of Work

LEAD ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SAFEGUARDS COMPLIANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT

- Lead and coordinate implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), applicable Environmental and Social Standards, UNDP Social and Environmental Standards, and relevant national environmental, occupational health and safety, labour and stakeholder-engagement requirements.

- Establish and maintain a project-level environmental and social safeguards compliance and assurance system covering technical studies, field investigations, sampling, laboratory activities, procurement, transport, temporary storage, treatment, disposal, contaminated-site work and contractor operations.

- Review project activities and procurement packages for environmental and social risks and advise the Project Manager and UNDP on the safeguards instruments, mitigation measures, monitoring requirements and contractual provisions required before implementation.

- Review and provide technical clearance/advice on Environmental and Social Management Plans, site-specific management plans, occupational health and safety plans, waste-management plans, emergency preparedness and response arrangements, stakeholder-engagement measures, labour-management measures and other safeguards instruments required under the ESCP/ESF.

- Ensure that safeguards requirements are adequately incorporated into Terms of Reference, technical specifications, bidding documents, contracts, contractor method statements and implementation plans.

- Undertake or coordinate safeguards monitoring of consultants, contractors, laboratories, hazardous-waste operators and field activities; identify non-compliance and recommend corrective and preventive actions, including escalation of material risks to UNDP management.

- Provide safeguards oversight for handling, packaging, temporary storage, transport, treatment and disposal of obsolete pesticides, PCB-contaminated equipment/oils and other hazardous wastes, including worker and community health and safety and emergency-response considerations.

- Ensure appropriate environmental and social due diligence for chemical hotspot investigations and remediation planning, including community exposure pathways, vulnerable groups, land/access implications, occupational risks and stakeholder consultation.

- Support incident and accident reporting, root-cause review, corrective-action tracking and safeguards reporting to UNDP, the Ministry of Environment and the World Bank, as applicable.

- Maintain safeguards records and prepare periodic safeguards compliance notes/reports, including status of ESCP commitments, material risks, corrective actions and outstanding issues.

- Provide technical guidance and capacity development to the PMU, government counterparts, consultants and contractors on ESF/ESCP, UNDP safeguards, hazardous-chemicals risk management and good international industry practice.

ESTABLISH AND LEAD THE PROJECT TECHNICAL QUALITY ASSURANCE SYSTEM.

- Establish and maintain a systematic, risk-based technical quality assurance framework covering all project components, with defined review gates, technical acceptance criteria, peer-review requirements, corrective-action tracking and documentation of technical clearances.

- Review and advise on the technical adequacy of major Terms of Reference, scopes of work, technical specifications, sampling and analytical protocols, technical designs, bidding documents and evaluation criteria before procurement or implementation.

- Review consultants’ and contractors’ inception reports, methodologies, work plans, sampling plans, QA/QC plans, draft and final technical reports, feasibility studies, remediation designs, disposal/treatment proposals, laboratory methodologies, monitoring plans and technical training materials.

- Validate the scientific and technical soundness, internal consistency, traceability and fitness-for-purpose of technical data, assumptions, findings, conclusions and recommendations against project requirements, international standards and relevant convention guidance.

- Verify achievement of key technical milestones and advise the Project Manager on acceptance, conditional acceptance, revision or rejection of technical deliverables, without replacing the formal procurement/contract approval authorities.

- Provide written technical review notes and recommendations for corrective action where technical gaps, methodological weaknesses, data-quality concerns, safeguards risks or implementation deficiencies are identified.

- Support technical evaluation of specialized environmental procurement when requested, including assessment of technical methodologies, equipment specifications, laboratory capability, contractor qualifications and proposed treatment/disposal technologies.

- Promote harmonized methodologies, sampling protocols, laboratory procedures, QA/QC systems and environmental assessment approaches so that Component 3 technical systems can support subsequent implementation of Components 1 and 2.

TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT AND QUALITY ASSURANCE OF POPS, HAZARDOUS CHEMICALS, PCBs AND OBSOLETE PESTICIDES

- Provide senior technical review of national inventories and assessments of industrial POPs (iPOPs), unintentionally produced POPs (uPOPs), POPs pesticides, obsolete pesticides, newly listed POPs and other priority hazardous chemicals.

- Assess whether inventory methodologies, data sources, sampling strategies, analytical methods, laboratory QA/QC and data-management systems are consistent with Stockholm Convention guidance and internationally accepted practice.

- Review characterization, classification and prioritization of POPs stocks, waste streams, contaminated materials and exposure pathways, and ensure that inventory findings are appropriately reflected in risk-reduction measures, management plans and the updated National Implementation Plan (NIP).

- Provide technical quality assurance for the updated NIP, including validation of inventory findings, prioritization, action plans, resource requirements, risk-reduction measures and consistency with Iraq’s obligations under the Stockholm Convention.

- Review uPOPs assessments and application of the UNEP Toolkit, including source identification, emission estimation, prioritization and proposed Best Available Techniques/Best Environmental Practices (BAT/BEP).

- Provide technical oversight and independent review of the PCB inventory, including sampling and testing strategies for transformers, capacitors, oils and associated contaminated materials; classification and risk categorization; and prioritization for phase-out, treatment and disposal.

- Review and validate PCB management and phase-out plans and provide technical advice on decontamination, treatment, destruction and disposal options, including proposed mobile or fixed treatment technologies where applicable.

- Review technical arrangements for PCB collection, draining, packaging, labelling, temporary storage, transport, treatment and final disposal, ensuring cradle-to-grave tracking and adequate documentation.

- Provide technical review of obsolete pesticide stockpile assessments, site characterization, sampling and analytical results, risk assessments and proposed management/disposal strategies.

- Assess the technical and environmental suitability of packaging, containment, temporary storage, transportation, treatment and disposal options, including in-country and transboundary disposal arrangements.

- Review qualifications, methodologies and performance of specialized hazardous-waste contractors from a technical and safeguards perspective and verify disposal/destruction documentation and certificates.

- Ensure technical consistency with Stockholm Convention and Basel Convention requirements, applicable national requirements, the World Bank ESF and recognized international hazardous-waste management practices.

TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT AND QUALITY ASSURANCE OF CHEMICAL HOTSPOTS AND CONTAMINATED SITES

- Provide senior technical oversight and independent review of national hotspot identification and prioritization and detailed assessment of priority chemical contamination sites.

- Review conceptual site models, investigation designs, sampling plans, laboratory analytical programmes, data-quality objectives, hydrogeological assessments and contaminant fate-and-transport analyses.

- Review human health and ecological risk assessments, including exposure pathways, receptors, uncertainty analysis and risk-based prioritization.

- Assess remediation feasibility studies and site-specific remediation plans for technical feasibility, environmental and social soundness, proportionality to risk, implementability and long-term monitoring requirements.

- Advise on remediation objectives, cleanup criteria/standards, verification requirements, institutional controls and post-remediation monitoring.

- Provide technical guidance for the National Programme on Contaminated Sites Management, including site screening, risk classification, investigation, remediation decision-making, technical standards, GIS/database requirements and long-term monitoring.

- Ensure that contaminated-site assessments and remediation plans adequately address POPs and other hazardous chemical contamination and are consistent with the national information-management system being developed under Component 3.

LABORATORY, SAMPLING AND DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE

- Review laboratory modernization plans, analytical equipment specifications, installation/commissioning arrangements, calibration requirements, certified reference materials, QA/QC procedures and operation and maintenance provisions.

- Review and promote fit-for-purpose sampling, chain-of-custody, sample preservation, laboratory analytical and data-validation procedures for POPs, PCBs and chemical hotspot investigations.

- Assess laboratory and field-monitoring performance, including detection limits, calibration, proficiency, blanks/duplicates, data validation and documentation, and recommend corrective measures where data quality is insufficient.

- Ensure traceability of technical evidence from field sampling and laboratory analysis through risk assessment, inventory development, remediation/disposal decisions and reporting.

TECHNICAL MONITORING, VERIFICATION AND ADAPTIVE MANAGEMENT AND CAPACITY DEVELOPMENT, KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER AND STRATEGIC TECHNICAL ADVICE

- Conduct periodic technical and safeguards implementation reviews across the project portfolio and provide concise assurance reports to UNDP management and the Project Manager on technical quality, compliance, emerging risks and required corrective actions.

- Support verification of contractor and consultant performance against approved methodologies, technical specifications, safeguards obligations, deliverables and key milestones.

- Contribute to technical review of project progress reports, Steering Committee documentation, World Bank missions and implementation-support reviews, focusing on technical quality and environmental/social compliance.

- Maintain technical issues and corrective-actions register and follow up on closure of significant findings.

- Apply adaptive management by identifying emerging technical, safeguards and implementation risks and recommending proportionate adjustments that preserve the approved project scope and contractual requirements.

- Provide targeted technical mentoring and on-the-job support to the PMU, Ministry of Environment and relevant national institutions on safeguards, POPs/PCB management, contaminated-site assessment, remediation planning, hazardous-waste management, laboratory QA/QC and technical review.

- Review technical manuals, standard operating procedures, guidance notes and training materials to ensure scientific accuracy, safeguards integration and consistency across project components.

- Support technical consultations, validation workshops and coordination with the Ministry of Environment, relevant ministries, laboratories, academia, technical institutions, the World Bank, GEF and specialized service providers.

- Document lessons learned and technical recommendations that strengthen sustainable national systems for POPs, hazardous chemicals and contaminated-site management beyond the project period.

- Provide substantive advice and technical support to the development and implementation of a capacity development/ learning plan on thematic area of the project for Country Office and participate in global/regional learning initiatives.

- Keep abreast of the developments in the thematic area of the project and provide guidance on how to incorporate them into UNDP’s current and future programming in the relevant sector. Provide technical guidance and quality assurance to content development for knowledge products.

BUILD STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND SUPPORT RESOURCE MOBILIZATION AND ACHIEVEMENT OF STRATEGIC RESULTS.

- Maintain strategic relationships with UNDP partners, Government institutions, donors, development partners, civil society, academia, private-sector stakeholders and specialized technical organizations.

- Build and maintain partnerships with donor agencies and development partners working on climate change, environment, chemicals and waste management.

- Identify and follow up on strategic opportunities for resource mobilization from traditional and non-traditional donors.

- Support the conceptualization of technically robust interventions that respond to national priorities and emerging environmental challenges.

- Work closely with the Partnerships and Planning Unit and relevant UNDP teams on resource mobilization, donor engagement, reporting and corporate compliance.

- Engage with GEF and other relevant funding mechanisms and technical networks.

- Strengthen collaboration with relevant UN agencies contributing to UNSDCF priority working groups to promote complementarity and avoid duplication.

- Maintain effective relationships with the GEF Secretariat and relevant technical networks.

- Strengthen cooperation with the mechanisms and technical networks associated with the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and other relevant environmental conventions.

- Promote engagement with laboratories, universities, research institutions, private-sector stakeholders, waste management companies and specialized disposal contractors.

- Identify opportunities for technical cooperation, knowledge exchange and joint programming.

- Identify emerging national priorities and technical gaps that could provide opportunities for new programming and resource mobilization.

- Lead or contribute to the technical conceptualization of new project ideas, programmes and funding proposals.

- Provide substantive technical inputs to concept notes, project documents, funding proposals and donor submissions.

- Identify opportunities for scaling up successful approaches and replicating technical solutions.

- Engage with traditional and non-traditional donors and development partners to communicate the strategic relevance and technical value of proposed interventions.

- Ensure that proposed interventions are evidence-based, technically feasible and aligned with national priorities and UNDP strategic frameworks.

- Contribute to monitoring and reporting on relevant CPD and portfolio results.

- Monitor implementation of targets and indicators linked to the portfolio and identify corrective actions where required.

- Support preparation and review of annual reports, donor reports and other substantive reporting requirements.

- Provide technical inputs for donor briefings, missions, steering committee meetings and strategic portfolio reviews.

- Maintain a pipeline of technically sound opportunities for future resource mobilization.

- Strengthen the positioning of UNDP as a strategic technical partner in climate change, environment, chemicals and waste management.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall and direct supervision of the DRR, and with matrix reporting to the EECC Programme Specialist, the Chief Technical Specialist (CTS) will serve as the Project’s senior technical assurance function. The position will have two principal areas of responsibility: (i) Environmental and Social Safeguards; and (ii) Technical Quality Assurance and independent technical assessment of POPs, PCBs, obsolete pesticides, hazardous chemicals and chemical pollution hotspots. The CTS will provide technical advice and assurance across Components 1, 2 and 3, while the Project Manager retains responsibility for day-to-day project management, delivery, coordination, budget, procurement administration and reporting.

The Chief Technical Specialist (CTS) will work closely with the national head of Environment, Energy and Climate Change (EECC), pillar UNDP Iraq. The CTS will work closely with Government counterparts, national authorities, project experts, donors, development partners, UNDP programmes and projects, and other relevant national and international stakeholders.

The CTS will be part of a multidisciplinary team of national and international experts supporting policy advocacy, technical oversight, capacity building, innovation and knowledge sharing in the areas of climate change, environmental management, POPs, hazardous chemicals and chemical pollution hotspots management.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Technical and Cross-functional Competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Effective Decision Making Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.

- Negotiation and influence Reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise, and create win-win situations.

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Nature Environmental Governance: Global Environmental Governance

Business Management

- Project management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Risk management Identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks

Partnership Management

- Strategic Engagement Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

Required Skills and Experience

Minimum Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Climate Change, Toxicology, Hazardous Waste Management, Environmental Management, or a closely related discipline is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Minimum years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible relevant experience at the national or international level in providing technical advice, conducting research, formulating policies, and/or developing and managing complex projects in sectors applicable to thematic area(s).

Required skills

- Experience definyning priorities, designing projects, managing budgets, preparing plans and monitoring to achieve quality results.

- Demonstrated experience with one or more of; POPs inventories, Stockholm Convention NIPs, PCB management and phase-out, obsolete pesticide management, UPOPs/BAT/BEP, hazardous waste treatment/disposal, contaminated-site assessment and remediation, environmental risk assessment, chemicals policy and regulatory development.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience with project planning and consulting, including the effective provision of substantive leadership and guidance, oversight, monitoring, and reporting for projects/programmes with similar scale, scope, and complexity.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

- Demonstrated experience in advocating for development or climate agenda in international, multi-cultural settings with problem solving capacities;

- Experience with UN operational and management common tools such as Results Based Management;

- Demonstrated experience in coordinating with multidisciplinary stakeholders; i.e. governments, academia, civil society, media and donors

- Prior experiences of working in Iraq or the Arab region, with in depth knowledge of Iraq’s social/cultural and political context;

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in English is required.

- Knowledge of Arabic is an asset.

Professional Certificates

jobs.title: Project Manager [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life, as envisaged by 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. We are on the ground in more than 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges. As they develop local capacity, they draw on the people of UNDP and our wide range of partners that can bring about results.

UNDP Turkmenistan has Health programme that includes projects funded by the Global Fund and by the Government of Turkmenistan (GoT). The Government of Turkmenistan is the principal donor to UNDP in Turkmenistan. During the previous programme cycle (2021–2025), the total volume of UNDP cooperation in the health sector amounted to approximately USD 207 million, of which USD 196 million was provided by the Government of Turkmenistan. For the new programme cycle (2026–2030), health projects totalling more than USD 56 million have already been signed, including USD 54 million in Government funding. Through these joint projects, UNDP supports a range of infectious diseases (TB, HIV, viral hepatitis, blood safety, and reproductive health), non-communicable diseases, maternal and neonatal care, rare diseases, and laboratory services.

In 2023-2025 UNDP implemented a project "Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan" (Lab-1), and upgraded 121 clinical laboratories across Turkmenistan. Those laboratories have been equipped with modern diagnostic equipment and can perform 9 categories of diagnostic testing covering more than 85 clinical laboratory parameters. This ensured that people throughout the country, regardless of their location or remoteness, now have access to timely and reliable diagnostic services. Based on successful implementation of Lab-1 project the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan and UNDP signed a new project "Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan in 2026-2027" (Lab-2). The goal of the Lab-2 project is to strengthen the potential of national healthcare system in clinical laboratory diagnostics of diseases. The project will support healthcare services to ensure the availability, accessibility, reliability and modern laboratory analyses for accurate and timely diagnosis of the most common illnesses, including infectious and noncommunicable diseases, surgery, emergency, maternal and child healthcare and others. The project will focus on laboratory capacity in primary healthcare facilities, but will also support secondary and tertiary care facilities.

UNDP Turkmenistan is seeking the Project Manager (PM) to coordinate the implementation of the project, provide strategic direction for the programme, ensure institutional capacity development and health system strengthening for wider health system issues.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager will be in charge of the following:

Ensure overall project management

- Management of the project a daily basis to achieve the performance indicators agreed with the donor and in line with the approved Budgets and Work Plans; Management and supervision of project implementation and evaluation across all components.

- Assess the programmatic impact and oversee the appropriateness and the accuracy of methods used to verify progress and the results.

- Analyse programmatic impact and takes decisions to correct possible deviations from targets.

- Assurance of successful completion of the project in accordance with the stated outcomes and performance indicators summarized in the Project Appraisal Document.

- Regular communication and coordination with the National Partner, members of the Project Board, and all other partners and interested stakeholders, with regard to all project activities. Organization of Project Board meetings at least twice a year.

- Regular communication with senior UNDP management with regard to all project activities. Assurance of coordination with other UNDP projects and broad strategic initiatives.

- Preparation of Annual Work Plans (AWP), including monthly targets and deliverables as well as annual spending targets in accordance with the Project Document. Tracking of work outputs throughout the year in light of these Annual Work Plans.

- Tracking and managing of project spending in accordance with the project budget, as well as UNDP rules and procedures, to ensure transparency, responsibility, and timely fulfilment of both program targets and budget targets.

- Preparation of regular progress reports (programmatic and financial) as per the requirements of UNDP and National Partner.

- Preparation and submission of annual Project Implementation Reviews and other required progress reports to the Project Board and UNDP in accordance with applicable requirements, in all required languages (English, Russian, and/or Turkmen, using outside translation as needed).

- Coordination of the work of international and national consultants engaged in the project.

- Supervision of regular data collection and analysis, as well as reporting and public outreach via the mass media, events, and other means, to disseminate the results of the project.

- Oversight of the overall administration of the project office.

- Travel to the project sites within Turkmenistan if required; possible travel outside the country for participation in directly relevant international meetings.

- Support during the project evaluations, if any.

- Plan the detailed actions according to annual work plans of the project approved by the Project Board and monitor progress against the initial quality criteria.

- Mobilize goods and services to initiate activities, including drafting Terms of References (ToR) and work specifications.

- Performs functions of Project Manager in Quantum (UNDP online system) for approval of requisitions. Manage requests for the provision of financial resources by UNDP, using advance of funds, direct payments, or reimbursement. Monitors financial resources and accounting to ensure accuracy and reliability of financial reports.

- Ensure the project activities are covered by the UNDP communication means regarding the project events, deliverables and key achievements.

- Prepare Final Project Review Reports to be submitted and presented to the Project Board.

- Identify follow-on actions and submit them for consideration to the Project Board.

- Manage the transfer of project deliverables, documents, files, equipment and materials to national beneficiaries.

- Prepare final CDR (Combined Delivery Reports) for signature by UNDP and the National Partner.

- In cooperation with the Head of Portfolio/ Programme Specialist, lead the process of developing and mobilizing resources for new projects in the areas of Project Manager’s expertise.

Ensure project financial resources management

- Act as financial manager and retain the ultimate responsibility for financial resources for accountability purposes.

- Ensure total accuracy and the highest level of transparency in the management of the Project financial resources in accordance with UNDP and national regulations and procedures.

- Ensure timely preparation of all necessary financial reports, including the Annual and Final Donor Reports, Quarterly Combined Delivery Reports, etc.

Project outreach

- Serve as the Project’s ambassador and advocate within the broader stakeholder’s community and beneficiaries.

- Create and foster a good working relationship with the media (print, radio and television).

- participate at national and international meetings.

- Contribute to the production and publication of public information material.

- Establish and maintain good working relationships and cooperation with peer project managers from other related projects within Turkmenistan and the Central Asia region.

Ensure Project planning and implementation

- Lead the process of quarterly and annual planning of project activities, with the participation of all Project personnel; retain the ultimate responsibility for the finished plans and submit them to the UNDP for their concurrence.

- Build effective working relationships with the main national partner and the project’s key stakeholders and UNDP’s other teams.

Monitoring and adaptive management

- Lead the implementation of the Project M&E (Monitoring and Evaluation) Plan.

- Carry out monitoring visits to Project sites on a regular basis.

- Collate the results of monitoring, analyze them, and formulate proposals for adaptive management measures for consideration by the Project Board.

- Implement the decisions and advice of the Project Board.

Reporting and accountability and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Provide a report to each Project Board meeting noting progress and achievements, acknowledging difficulties and proposing possible solutions for consideration and guidance by the Project Board.

- Assume the lead responsibility for the preparation and content of the annual Project Progress Report.

- Prepare quarterly and annual project plans and reports and present them to the Project Board, donor, etc.

- Respond to request for reports on Project management and performance from any key stakeholders.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Lab project is integrated into the health programme of UNDP country office. UNDP Health Programme Specialist is assigned with the responsibility for the overall supervision of the health programme. The day-to-day administration of the Lab project is to be carried out by a Project Manager (PM), assisted by the team of Procurement Specialist, Lab Specialist, Admin & Logistics Assistant, Driver & Customs Clerk. The project is supported by UNDP’s Global Fund Partnership and Health Systems Team based in Copenhagen and this team performs procurement of health products in accordance with the UNDP Quality Assurance Policy.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

People Management competencies:

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Finance

- Financial Planning and budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP’s long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Monitoring & Evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.discrepancy between planned and actual activities and programme performance and results.

Partnership Management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/ or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

2030 Agenda: People

- Health Health Resilience and Sustainable Systems for Health. Procurement services of health products.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Medicine, Public Health, Biology, Chemistry, Laboratory systems, or another related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in providing management advisory services, and/or hands-on experience in design or implementation of development projects.

Required Skills:

- Experience in partnership building and management with multi-stakeholders, including government agencies, health donors and civil society organizations.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Skills:

- Demonstrated ability to set forecasts and refine/review them in the light of experience and further analysis.

- Experience in management of a medical or public health project.

- Experience working with clinical or public health laboratories, including familiarity with laboratory operations and quality management systems,

- Experience in procurement, supply, or maintenance of lab equipment and supplies.

Languages:

- Fluency in English, Russian and Turkmen is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.
